## A first step that changes nothing

Size it, read-only: count rows per (`user_id`, `source_id`) where `source_type = 'MILESTONE'` and the count is above 1, on whichever database holds the table. What to do with any duplicates found is for Kam to decide; it is not proposed here.

## Related

KS 1956 (the re-award bug and its repair, pull request 1979), KS 1957 (the owner and role check on the award routes, pull request 1980).

title: originate document signing: a sign, sign-cert or sign-wallet request can answer 500 after the signature or signed document is saved, and a retry duplicates it
description:
**BLUF:** In originate, `POST /api/documents/:id/sign`, `/:id/sign-cert` and `/:id/sign-wallet` can answer 500 after the signature, or the signed derived document, is already saved. A retry then saves a second one. This is pre-existing: it happens the same way for an ordinary Error at base, and pull request 1964 does not cause it. Found by QA gate 149 on PR 1964 (findings G149-F1 and G149-F2).

**What happens** (measured by gate 149: the six real document routes in their own Node process, with an in-memory documents model that rejects AFTER it has applied the write; the identical request is then retried with no fault):

* `POST /:id/sign` (`updateDocument` is the write): the signature is persisted and the status is `signed`, the caller gets 500, and the signing nonce is NOT consumed. A retry with the same body inside the 5-minute nonce window answers 200 and appends a SECOND signature entry (1 signature, then 2).
* `POST /:id/sign-cert` and `POST /:id/sign-wallet` (`saveDocument` is the write): a derived document with status `signed` is persisted, carrying the sigJson or sigWallet envelope. The caller gets 500 and no `document.versioned` event is published. A retry mints a second derived signed document (derived 1, then 2, one event). For sign-cert the orphaned envelope can be fetched from the public `GET /:id/sig-json` route.
* `POST /:id/sign/request`: not affected. Its only write is synchronous and nothing is awaited after it; an orphan nonce expires after 5 minutes.

**Same at base:** with an ordinary `Error('Connection terminated unexpectedly')` at base, and with each of six unreadable thrown values at the head of PR 1964, the persisted state and the retry result were identical in all 288 compared cells. At base an unreadable value was worse: the caller got no answer, and so was just as likely to retry.

**Suggested shapes (from the gate, not chosen here):**

* sign: consume the nonce before the write (delete it, write, restore it on a definite pre-commit failure), or make the append idempotent on (signerId, nonce).
* sign-cert and sign-wallet: an idempotency key, or a deterministic derived id with `conflictMode: 'skip'` keyed on (parent, signature).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL or Prisma client (the documents and lifecycle tables were an in-memory model); a real ambiguous commit (modelled as "write applied, then reject"); the real `authenticate()` and the gateway hop; a real Redis event bus; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

Related: `KS-1831` (the sign route: authorization, revoked status and no signature verified), `KS-1693` (the same sign-cert and sign-wallet routes: no provenance recorded for the derived document).

title: GDPR erasure: a failed kyc or wallet-connector user.erased step leaves the subject's data in place and nothing reports it (dead-letter unread; request already marked completed)
description:
**BLUF:** When the kyc or wallet-connector `user.erased` handler fails, the erasure is left silently incomplete and nobody is told. The shared event bus tries the handler 3 times back to back, then writes one dead-letter entry with the constant text `Failed after 3 attempts` and acknowledges the message. Nothing reads the dead-letter stream and no retry job exists. The data-subject request was already marked completed: originate's erasure marks it completed at step 12, before it publishes `user.erased` at step 13. What stays behind is the subject's data in that service, as measured below.

**What survives, measured by QA gate 147** (the real kyc `index.ts` and wallet-connector `server.ts` handlers through the real shared `EventBus` subscribe loop, with only the database and the bus's Redis client replaced; the subject has one verification, three document images, one consent with IP address and user agent; a second user's rows are never touched). kyc's four deletes run in this order with no transaction: select verifications, delete images by id, delete images by user id, delete consents, delete verifications, then evict the subject key. Each attempt re-runs the whole sequence.

| failure point (fails on every attempt) | attempts | dead-letter entries | left after the dead-letter (images / consents / verifications) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| kyc: delete images by id | 3 | 1 | 3 / 1 / 1 (everything) |
| kyc: delete consents | 3 | 1 | 0 / 1 / 1 |
| kyc: delete verifications | 3 | 1 | 0 / 0 / 1 |
| wallet-connector: delete sessions | 3 | 1 | every session row for the address |

A failure on the first attempt only (consents once, or the wallet delete once) completes on the second attempt and leaves nothing. By schema (`migrations/002_*.sql` lines 474 to 533 and 813 to 820): the surviving kyc verification holds `provider_application_id`, `provider_check_id`, `liveness_score`, `overall_score`, `risk_level`, `status`, `review_notes` and `documents`; the consent holds the IP address, user agent and timestamps; wallet-connector rows hold the address, wallet type and connected time, all plaintext. Columns written under the subject key (`d1:` envelopes such as `documents` and `review_notes`) are crypto-shredded by originate's step 11. Legacy `v<N>:` kyc rows are under the platform keyring and stay decryptable; that is the same class as `KS-1953`, a different erasure gap (originate lifecycle rows).

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY Error at develop's base already leaves exactly this state. PR 1963 (the thrown-value guard on both handlers) does not cause it; it only makes the unreadable-value case behave like the ordinary one (same attempts, same rows erased and left, same dead-letter entry).

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* a dead-letter consumer or alarm that reopens or flags the data-subject request per service;
* a backoff between attempts, or a re-delivery schedule, instead of three immediate tries;
* wrap kyc's deletes in `transaction()` (the service's `db.ts` already has one) so a failure leaves all or nothing;
* record per-service cascade completion against the request.

**Related (pre-existing, read from source, not run):**

* kyc `dbDeleteUserData` returns 0 when `isDbAvailable()` is false (`index.ts` line 373). The handler then logs `handled` and the bus acknowledges: an erasure silently skipped with no dead-letter. wallet-connector's handler never clears `memConnectedWallets`, so in-memory sessions for the address persist until a restart (gate finding G147-F3).
* The `user.erased` stream entry (user id, request id, `performedBy`, wallet address) is acknowledged but never deleted: `publish` has no XDEL or MAXLEN. A dead-letter copies the raw event into `secuura:events:dead-letter`. So the subject's wallet address stays in Redis after an erasure, whether it succeeded or not (gate finding G147-F4).

**Not tested:** a real Redis (the stream, consumer group, pending list, redelivery after a crash between attempts and the acknowledgement, recovery from a missing group); a real Postgres (the real SQL semantics and the foreign-key cascade are modelled; the timing of the three attempts); a booted service, and the admin HTTP delete path at kyc `index.ts` line 1224, which calls `dbDeleteUserData` directly; originate's publish side end to end; the auth, m365 and other `user.erased` subscribers; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 147 on PR 1963, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G147-F1: HIGH, pre-existing, measured; not caused by `KS-1868`'s PR 1963, not a merge block).

title: transfer approval sweep: when the workflow reads fail, every overdue step is marked timed_out (terminal), including steps set to escalate, so escalations are silently lost
description:
**BLUF:** In the transfer service's escalation sweep (`processEscalations` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/transfer/src/services/approvalWorkflowService.ts`), when the reads that look up a step's workflow fail, every overdue pending step is marked `timed_out`, including steps configured to auto-escalate. `timed_out` is terminal: a later sweep does not select it again and `processApproval` refuses a step that is not pending, so the escalation is silently lost and running the sweep again cannot repair it.

**Cause:** `findWorkflowByStepId` (line 670) reads the workflows through `dbGetActiveWorkflows` (line 238, with a bare `catch { return []; }` at line 243) and then a second `SELECT * FROM svc_approval_workflows` whose failure is swallowed by a bare `catch { /* fall back to active-only */ }`. If both reads fail the workflow is `undefined`, so `stepDef` is `undefined`, the test `stepDef?.autoEscalate && stepDef.escalateTo && !instance.escalatedAt` (line 611) is false, and the `else` branch (lines 622 to 625) sets `status = 'timed_out'`. (The gate cites lines 235 to 243 and 695 to 698 at the PR head; the lines above are at develop `4d1ab2cb6574`, so cite by function name.)

**Measured by QA gate 146** (the REAL transfer service booted as its own Node process for every cell, the real routes and authentication; only the `pg` module replaced, by an in-memory model of the two workflow tables with a unique-id upsert). Setup: 4 overdue pending steps; I1 and I3 on a custom step with `autoEscalate`, `escalateTo: boss-user` and `timeoutHours: 1`; I2 and I4 on the default `step-1`, which times out; `POST /api/workflows/escalate` as a platform administrator. Cell `sweep_wfread`, with the workflow reads failing: the answer is 200 with `{ escalatedCount: 0, timedOutCount: 4 }`. I1 and I3, which should escalate to boss-user, are marked `timed_out`, and a second POST cannot repair them. The result is the same at develop's base and at PR 1962's head, for every kind of failure value including an ordinary Error.

**Effect on approval:** the state refuses rather than grants. The transfer's own execute path gates on the transfer record, not on step instances (`index.ts` lines 802 to 814, read, not run), so nothing this sweep writes can let a transfer proceed. What is lost is the escalation to the named escalation user.

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** when the step's workflow cannot be found, skip the row and leave it `pending` instead of marking it `timed_out`.

**Related:** a sweep that fails part-way answers `200 success: true` with partial counts and no error indicator (gate finding G146-F4; pre-existing, true at base for an ordinary Error and now for an unreadable value too). The admin caller cannot tell the sweep was incomplete; only a log line says so. Also KS-1881 (the route's platform-admin check, Done) and KS-1868 (PR 1962, unrelated cause).

**Not tested:** a real PostgreSQL (the store is a model; the real WHERE and ON CONFLICT semantics are emulated, not executed); pgbouncer or a mid-statement connection loss; the api-gateway hop to the escalate route (whether and how it is proxied is not traced); a production-mode boot; multi-tenancy pools; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Found by:** QA gate 146 on PR 1962, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G146-F3: recommended follow-up, pre-existing, measured, base = head for every value including an ordinary Error). PR 1962 does not cause it.

title: originate GDPR erasure: a lifecycle event row skipped by the erasure sweep stays decryptable under the platform keyring after the erasure reports completed
description:
**BLUF:** In originate's GDPR erasure, a lifecycle event row that the sweep skips keeps the subject's email recoverable by anyone holding the platform keyring, in live data and in backups, after an erasure that reports `success: true` with the data-subject request marked completed. Step 11 destroys only the subject's own data key (the DEK); lifecycle payloads are encrypted under the platform-wide `v<N>:` keyring (`encodeLifecyclePayload` calls `encryptField`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/utils/lifecyclePayloadCodec.ts` lines 34 to 38), not under it. Step 5d skips a row when `decodeLifecyclePayload` reports `payloadUnavailable` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/services/gdprService.ts` lines 688 to 690). The deletion log and the DSR record say nothing about the skipped row; the only trace is one error line carrying the event id.

**Not new (measured):** an ORDINARY decrypt error at develop's base already leaves the same row in the same state (a key version that is not loaded). PR 1961 (the thrown-value guard) does not cause this. It routes the unreadable-value case into that same ordinary state; before it, a hostile throw aborted the whole erasure loudly (`success: false`, DSR left open), and that abort was not atomic: the earlier steps and rows had already been written. The old state was also not a real remedy, because a retry hits the same row and aborts again (read, not run).

**Measured by QA gate 145** (the real `executeErasure`, the real lifecycle codec, the real `SubjectDekProvider`, real AES-GCM `encryptField` / `decryptField` / `encryptFieldWithDek` with keys generated in-process, the real winston logger; only the database replaced by an in-memory SQL stand-in). E2 is a lifecycle row holding the subject's email whose decrypt fails; after the erasure the whole platform keyring (v1 + v2) is loaded and E2 is tried.

| version | failure on row E2 | erasure result | DSR completed | subject DEK destroyed | row E2 rewritten | E2 decrypts with the platform keyring | E2 still holds the subject email |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| base | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| base | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| base | unreadable thrown value | `success: false` ("Erasure failed") | no | no (DEK still live) | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | none (control) | success | yes | yes | yes | yes | no |
| head (PR 1961) | ordinary decrypt error | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |
| head (PR 1961) | unreadable thrown value | success | yes | yes | no | yes | YES |

Head with an unreadable value equals base with an ordinary error in every column. In the success rows the log says `Erasure completed`; the deletion log does not mention E2.

**Why step 11 cannot shred it:** `executeErasureImpl` step 11 (`gdprService.ts` lines 893 to 894) calls `subjectDeks.destroyDek(userId)`, which sets the wrapped DEK to NULL in `pii_subject_keys` (`Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/subjectDek.ts`). No lifecycle payload depends on that key. The shared module's own comment in `Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/src/crypto/encryptedField.ts` says the `v<N>:` format "makes single-subject erasure impossible to guarantee in backups (there is no per-subject key to destroy)". After a completed erasure the skipped row can still be decrypted by `listLifecycleEvents` (`lifecycleEventRepo.ts` line 138, tenant-scoped document listing), which would show the email to whoever can list that document's events (read, not run).

**Retry does not reach it (read, not run):** `payloadUnavailable` is read only at line 690. A second erasure looks up the subject email at step 5c from a users row that step 10 already set to a placeholder of the form `deleted_<id>` at the `anonymized.local` domain, so it cannot match the address inside E2, and nothing else revisits the row.

**Suggested fix shapes (the gate's, not a decision):**

* (a) count skipped rows, and do not mark the DSR plainly `completed` while any remain; record them in the deletion log as `skipped` with the event ids; and/or
* (b) move lifecycle payloads to the subject-DEK (`d1:`) envelope so that step 11 shreds them, as the KS-291 design does for users, consents and DSRs.

**Not tested:** the live PR body; a real Postgres or Prisma client (the SQL stand-in answers by statement prefix, so the real SQL semantics of the other steps are not exercised); a real Key Vault or production keyring (keys were generated in-process); whether a real decrypt ever throws an unreadable value (none is known; Node crypto throws Errors); the HTTP routes (`POST /api/gdpr/erasure/:userId`, `executeErasureByExternalRef`) and a booted service; a second erasure run against the same subject; `listLifecycleEvents`; backups; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Related:** KS-537 (lifecycle payload encryption and erasure), KS-291 (the subject-DEK design for users, consents and DSRs), KS-1868 (PR 1961, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 145 on PR 1961, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G145-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH priority for data protection, pre-existing, measured).

title: api-gateway: with Redis unavailable, enforceDocumentTypeRules passes every document (catalogue reads empty), so MFA-required types are allowed
description:
**BLUF:** When `isRedisAvailable()` is false (every Redis outage: an ordinary error on the client, a socket `close`, or the 4th retry), `enforceDocumentTypeRules` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/services/enforcement.ts`, called at `routes/verification.ts` line 856) reads an EMPTY document-type catalogue on every replica (`documentTypesStore` is only written while the flag is false), `resolveDocumentType` returns null, and the "catalogue empty" branch returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }`. A document type registered with `requireMFA: true` is then allowed.

**Measured by QA gate 144** (real `redis.ts`, `enforcement.ts` and winston; only `ioredis` replaced; two replicas sharing one store): a type registered with `requireMFA: true` is REFUSED with 403 `MFA_REQUIRED` while the flag is true, and ALLOWED on both replicas while the flag is false, with Redis up or down, at develop's base AND at PR 1960's head after an ordinary Error. Evidence: `logs/probe_site3_table.log`, enforce block, rows `base trigger=ordinary` and `head trigger=ordinary`: `ALLOWED ok:true docType={}` on replica A and B, with `down=0` and `down=1`.

**By reading, not run:** the same pass-through skips the `isActive` check, the verification-level check (`creatorVerificationLevel`), the auth-provider check (`allowedAuthProviders`), the metadata-schema check (`metadataSchema`) and the approval-workflow gate (`createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` sees no `requiresApproval`).

**Where it sits at develop** `4d1ab2cb6574`**, read by the filer:** `resolveDocumentType` calls `redisService.getAllDocumentTypes()` at `enforcement.ts` line 72; `enforceDocumentTypeRules` reads the catalogue again at line 126 and returns `{ ok: true, docType: {} }` at lines 117 and 137, where the code comment says an empty catalogue means "never seeded, or Redis TTL expiry". The gate cites `enforcement.ts` lines 78 and 128; the statements I read are at lines 72 and 126, so cite them by function name.

**Reach:** every Redis blip in production puts the gateway in this state (an ordinary error, `close`, or retry 4). PR 1960 (the `redis.ts` error listener and `initRedis` catch) does not cause it and does not change it; it makes the unreadable-value path land in the same state an ordinary Error already reaches.

**Not tested:** a real Redis or `ioredis` client (a stand-in was used; the `ioredis` emit, close and retry path was read in `node_modules` 5.11.1, not run); a booted gateway over HTTP (the middleware and `enforceDocumentTypeRules` were called directly); `createWorkflowInstanceIfRequired` and the `isActive`, verification-level, provider and schema skips under fallback (read, only the MFA rule was run); admin routes in fallback; Node 24 (host Node v26.8.1).

**Suggested fix shape (the gate's, not a decision):** in fallback mode `enforceDocumentTypeRules` should refuse with 503 instead of treating an unreadable catalogue as an empty one, as the connector-create and connector-info readers already do (`routes/verification.ts` line 795 and `services/health.ts` line 54, which gate 144 read as answering 503 when the flag is false).

**Related:** KS-1256, KS-1540, KS-1532, KS-1627 (readers of the same flag); KS-1466 (untyped creates never meet the catalogue's document rules: a different defect); KS-1868 (PR 1960, unrelated cause).

**Found by:** QA gate 144 on PR 1960, 2026-11-03 (verdict finding G144-F1: recommended follow-up, HIGH, pre-existing, measured).

title: staking: POST /api/stake takes address and amount from the caller, so any signed-in user can create or grow a stake position for any address
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/stake` (`services/staking/src/routes/stake.ts:189-245`) takes `address` and `amount` from the request body and saves a stake position for that address with no ownership or chain check. By the same shape, the unstake routes (`POST /api/stake/unstake` `:263`, `POST /api/stake/complete-unstake` `:317`) also take the address from the body; they were not read line by line. So any signed-in caller can create or grow a stake position for any address. `txHash` is optional and is logged but never verified. KS 1942's design treats `svc_stake_positions` as NOT a trusted stake source for this reason.

## Where (develop `0e3a9b65cdd6`; read from source, NOT run)

* Mount: `services/staking/src/index.ts:80` applies `jwtAuthenticate()` to `/api`, and `:82` mounts the stake routes at `/api/stake`. Any signed-in caller reaches them.
* `routes/stake.ts:189-245`: the handler parses `StakeSchema` from `req.body` (`:191`), takes `{ address, amount, txHash }` (`:196`), loads the position for that address (`:199`), adds `amount` to it or creates it (`:213-228`), and saves it (`:230`). It also adds to the in-process pool stats (`:233-236`).
* `req.user` is not read anywhere in `routes/stake.ts`. `txHash` is optional in the schema (`:33`), and its only other use is the log line (`:243`).

## Why it matters

KS 1942 (the governance register route takes stake from the caller) is being fixed by making stake and roles admin-set only. Its design rejected `svc_stake_positions` as a stake source because this route lets any caller assert any position.

## Not checked

The unstake and complete-unstake handlers line by line. Whether the gateway restricts `/api/stake` to a role. Whether any client other than the tests calls these routes. Whether the Aiken staking validator is meant to be the source of truth (no service reads it).

## Related

KS 1942 (governance register route, same class). KS 1845 (covers only the admin listing `GET /api/stake/all`, not these routes).

## Searched first

Board search over issue content and comment bodies:

* "svc_stake_positions" and "routes/stake.ts" find KS 1845 (an issue covering only `GET /api/stake/all`) and a KS 1544 comment.
* "POST /api/stake" finds comments on KS 188, KS 256 and KS 492, about business-rule refusals and OpenAPI examples on `/unstake` and `/complete-unstake`, not ownership.
* "StakeSchema" and "staking service" find 0.
* Control: "minProposalStake" finds KS 1940.

## Found by

Seat F 23rd while designing KS 1942; filed on the coordinator's ruling (D4). Not measured against a running service.

title: api-gateway: ORG_ADMIN and ISSUER_ADMIN can set any user's verification level (tenant bound unmeasured)
description:
**BLUF:** In the api-gateway, `PATCH /api/admin/identity/users/:id/level` sits behind `requireAdmin`, and `requireAdmin` admits `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN` (and the lower-case `issuer_admin`). A probe with a stub database showed both roles reach the handler and issue `UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1 ... WHERE id = $2::uuid` for ANY user id. The SQL has no tenant or organisation predicate. **Whether row-level security (or anything else) stops those two roles from changing a user in another tenant was NOT run**, so this is an open question, not a confirmed cross-tenant write. A real-PostgreSQL probe with a cross-tenant id settles it.

## What is read in the code (develop `d9acf71a3fcc`, `Blockchain/Dev/services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts`)

* `:600` `const ADMIN_ROLES = ['SYSTEM_ADMIN', 'system_admin', 'super_admin', 'SUPER_ADMIN', 'platform_admin', 'ORG_ADMIN', 'ISSUER_ADMIN', 'issuer_admin'];`
* `:602-:605` a comment (KS 458) says platform-level admins read across tenants and that "ORG_ADMIN / ISSUER_ADMIN keep the tenant-scoped view the policy now enforces (their request ALS context applies)". `PLATFORM_SCOPE_ROLES` (`:606`) lists only the five platform roles, and `adminScope` (`:607-:610`) runs a query under the platform scope for those five only.
* `:612-:651` `requireAdmin` checks the token and then only `ADMIN_ROLES.includes(role)`; a role outside the list gets 403. It does not look at the target user, the caller's organisation or the caller's tenant.
* `:1313` `router.patch('/api/admin/identity/users/:id/level', requireAdmin, mockBodyParser, ...)`. The body's `verificationLevel` must be one of NONE, BASIC, SOCIAL, STANDARD, ENHANCED, HIGH, GOVERNMENT (anything else answers 400 with no query).
* `:1322-:1325` `adminScope(req, () => query('UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1, updated_at = NOW() WHERE id = $2::uuid RETURNING id, verification_level', [verificationLevel, id]))`. The only predicate is the user id. `rowCount === 0` answers 404.

## Source and its limit

Found by gate 98 (the QA gate on pull request 1916, the KS 1868 `admin.ts` catch-read change), finding G98-F4, 2026-11-02. It ran the real admin router (real `createAdminRoutes`, real `requireAdmin`, real `ADMIN_ROLES`) on a loopback listener with only the token verifier, the database, the logger and redis replaced. Its auth matrix: no token 401, a plain USER 403, and ORG_ADMIN, ISSUER_ADMIN and SYSTEM_ADMIN each 200 with exactly one query, `UPDATE users SET verification_level = $1`, parameters the level and the id. **The database was a stub, so row-level security was not run.** The behaviour is pre-existing and unchanged by pull request 1916 (that change only guards how a thrown value is read for a log line). Filed on Wednesday's commission from that note; I read the code lines above at `d9acf71a3fcc`, and I did not run anything against a database.

## What is not known, and what would settle it

1. **Cross-tenant.** Does the tenant row-level security on `users` reject the UPDATE when an `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` of tenant A names a user of tenant B? Settle with a real PostgreSQL carrying the project's RLS policies and migrations: two tenants, a user in B, a token for an `ORG_ADMIN` of A, `PATCH` the level for B's user. 404 (zero rows) means RLS bounds the call; 200 and a changed row means it does not.
2. **Same tenant, other organisation.** Tenant row-level security does not know organisations, so an `ORG_ADMIN` or `ISSUER_ADMIN` may be able to change the level of a user in a different organisation of the SAME tenant. Not measured either way. The policy question of which roles may cross an organisation boundary is KS 1535 and the role-list drift is KS 1536; neither covers this route.
3. **What a changed level buys.** The board's KS 1176 and KS 1190 describe the gateway's `meetsVerificationLevel` checks on this value. Which routes read the stored level for an access decision was not traced here.

## Board search (so nobody files this twice)

Run 2026-11-02 over this team's issues and comment bodies for `admin/identity`, `identity/users`, `/level`, `verification_level`, `requireAdmin`, `ADMIN_ROLES`, `ORG_ADMIN` and `ISSUER_ADMIN`; positive control KS 1865 found. The route terms hit only the KS 1868 umbrella's own comments; the symbol terms hit tickets about other routes. Closest, and not covering this route: KS 1536 (role vocabularies), KS 1584 (an organisation-bound escape through a provisioning key), KS 1855 (gateway admin stand-ins).

## Not in scope

No change to `admin.ts` is proposed or made here. Severity is not asserted: priority High is the commissioning call, pending the probe above.

title: Billing: addCertificationCredits' optimistic lock is not a compare-and-set, so one call can credit twice under a concurrent write
description:
**BLUF:** `StripeService.addCertificationCredits` keeps the credit balance in Stripe customer metadata and calls its read-update-verify loop "optimistic locking", but Stripe's customer update is unconditional, so the loop is not a compare-and-set. When a concurrent writer changes the balance between this call's update and its verify read, the loop re-reads and adds the credits AGAIN, so one call can credit twice; a write can also be lost. Read in code, not run. It is the same money class as KS-1933 (one purchase credited more than once), through a different door.

**Where** (`services/billing/src/services/stripeService.ts` at PR 1913's head `5d6bd74daa3e`)

* `addCertificationCredits` (:226-247): up to 3 attempts of retrieve (:229), compute `currentBalance + credits` (:231-232), `customers.update` with the new `certificationCredits` (:234-236), retrieve again (:239); if the read-back is not the value it wrote, it logs a conflict (:244) and goes round again from a fresh read.
* `useCertificationCredits` (:252-278) has the same loop for debits.

**A sequence that credits twice (worked from the code):** the balance is 10. Call A (+5) and call B (+3) both read 10. A writes 15, B writes 13 (A's write is lost). A's verify reads 13, not 15: A retries, reads 13, writes 18, verify passes. B's verify reads 18, not 13: B retries, reads 18, writes 21, verify passes. The final 21 is 10 + 5 + 3 + 3: B's credit landed twice.

**Not in scope here:** no fix is designed or built in KS-1933's pull request (KS-1933 adds a per-payment ledger in PostgreSQL that stops a second CALL for the same purchase; it does not change what one call does). Found by Seat F 22nd while tracing KS-1933 (Wednesday's ANSWER of 2026-11-02 commissioned this filing).

**Related:** KS-1933.

title: kyc: dbGetVerificationsByUser returns [] on any read error, so the GDPR erasure cascade (dbDeleteUserData) continues with an incomplete list, against its own comment
description:
**BLUF:** `dbGetVerificationsByUser` in `Blockchain/Dev/services/kyc/src/index.ts` (`:207-221`) catches every ordinary database or decrypt error, logs it and returns `[]`. `dbDeleteUserData` (`:332`), the GDPR erasure cascade, calls it at `:350` to collect legacy image ids and then deletes by `user_id` regardless, so on a read failure the cascade continues with an incomplete list. The comment at `:340-345` says the opposite: failures THROW so the event bus retries and dead-letters. After pull request 1900 an unreadable thrown value takes the same path. **Read, not run.**

## What I read (develop `8126b22bd5aa`, line numbers at that sha)

* `dbGetVerificationsByUser` (`index.ts:207-221`): `try { query(...); return await Promise.all(rows.map(rowToVerification)) } catch (err) { logger.error(...); return []; }`.
* `dbDeleteUserData` (`:332-368`): `:350` `const verifications = await dbGetVerificationsByUser(userId)`; `:351-357` collects `frontImageId` / `backImageId` from the decrypted documents; `:359-361` deletes those images by id; `:362-364` then deletes images, consents and verifications by `user_id`; `:367` evicts the cached DEK. The comment at `:340-345` says failures THROW "so the event bus retries and dead-letters instead of reporting a successful cascade that deleted nothing".
* Entry points: `DELETE /api/kyc/user/:userId/data` (`:1176-1186`, no `try`, answers 200 `All KYC data for user has been deleted.`) and the `user.erased` subscriber (`userErasedSubscriber.ts`, started at `:1274`, which logs and rethrows a rejection so the bus retries).

## Effect, by reading

When the read in `dbGetVerificationsByUser` fails for an ordinary reason (a database error, or a row that cannot be decrypted and throws), the helper returns `[]`. The cascade then skips the legacy image ids found through the verification documents and deletes the verification rows by `user_id`. Legacy images that carry no `user_id` can be found only through those documents, so they are not deleted, and the rows that pointed to them are. The route still answers that all data was deleted, and the subscriber logs `user.erased handled`.

## Not measured

No database failure was injected and the cascade was not run. I did not look for legacy `svc_kyc_images` rows without a `user_id` in any environment, so how many images this could leave behind is unknown. I did not read the migration that stamped `user_id` (035) for what it leaves out.

## Context

Found while raising the KS 1868 kyc passes (pull request 1900), which make an unreadable thrown value in this helper log a constant reason and return `[]`, so the cascade now continues for that value too instead of aborting. The change is deliberate and described in that pull request; this ticket is about the existing behaviour for ordinary errors. Filed on the coordinator's word after a board search by symbol and path (`dbGetVerificationsByUser`, `dbDeleteUserData`, "erasure cascade", "failures THROW": no hits).

title: tenant-provisioning checks no role on its own routes: any signed-in caller who reaches the service can suspend, archive, edit or delete any tenant
description:
## BLUF

`services/tenant-provisioning` **verifies the bearer token on every** `/api/*` **route (**`index.ts:182`**) but checks no role on any of them.** Any caller with a valid JWT who reaches the service directly, rather than through the gateway, can list, read, create, suspend, archive, edit or delete any tenant. The only role gate is the gateway's `requireSuperAdmin` on its proxy routes. **Read from code, not exercised.** Exposure on the deployed boxes is UNMEASURED. This is the same class as KS 1881 and KS 1845: an admin route in a service with no role check of its own.

## Detail (develop `cb2320368ae4`)

* `index.ts:182` is `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`. The token is verified, and no role is read afterwards: a search of `services/tenant-provisioning/src` (tests excluded) for `.role`, `isPlatformRole`, `SUPER_ADMIN`, `SYSTEM_ADMIN` and `requireRole` finds only a comment at `index.ts:141`.
* **The routes it leaves open:**
  * `POST /api/tenants` (`index.ts:219`)
  * `GET /api/tenants` (`index.ts:369`)
  * `GET /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:398`)
  * `PATCH /api/tenants/:id/status` (`index.ts:432`)
  * `PATCH /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:471`)
  * `DELETE /api/tenants/:id` (`index.ts:523`)
  * `GET /api/audit-log` (`index.ts:584`)
* **Create is not fully open.** `POST /api/tenants` writes the tenant row, then forwards the caller's token to tokenisation's `generate-key`, which needs a platform role (`index.ts:139-150`, KS 175). A non-platform caller therefore gets a tenant without a confirmed key, which is the `keyPending` answer from KS 1240.
* **The gateway's gate:** `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:65-74`, `requireSuperAdmin`, an exact-match list of `'super_admin','SUPER_ADMIN','platform_admin','SYSTEM_ADMIN'`, on the proxies (for example the status and delete proxies at `platform.ts:395-431`). The proxies forward the caller's `Authorization` header (`platform.ts:289-295`). That list differs from the shared `isPlatformRole`: it admits `platform_admin` and does not fold case. KS 1536 tracks the role-vocabulary drift.
* **Reachability by repo config:** the service listens on 4022. `docker-compose.yml:2081-2083` keeps the host port unpublished (pen-test F-04; it was `"6022:4022"`), so the service is reachable from inside the compose network. The deployed hosts are not measured.
* **Related:** KS 1860 and KS 1861 (the status and delete handlers' behaviour) are being fixed separately. This ticket is only about who may call these routes.

## Recommendation

* Gate every `/api` route in tenant-provisioning with the shared `isPlatformRole` straight after `jwtAuthenticate()`, the KS 1845 / KS 1881 shape, with red-first cells per route.
* Decide first whether the gateway's `SUPER_ROLES` list and the shared helper must agree (KS 1536). As things stand, a `platform_admin` or lowercase `super_admin` token that the gateway admits would be refused by the service.

Found by Seat S 9th while writing the KS 1860 / KS 1861 option sets, 2026-10-31. Searched before filing (title or description, team KS): `requireSuperAdmin` 1 (KS 1773, a different route); `SUPER_ROLES` 3 (KS 1536, KS 1535, KS 1472, none naming this service); the 25 tickets whose description names `tenant-provisioning`, filtered for a missing role check: none own it.

title: The gateway answers four admin and verify routes from stand-ins registered before the proxy: fixed audit-log arrays, an always-empty verification queue, and certification verify that always says verified:false
description:
**BLUF:** The api-gateway answers four routes itself, from stand-ins registered before the proxy to the real service, with no environment guard around them: `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` and `GET /api/security/audit` return fixed arrays of fabricated rows (actor `admin` at `test.local`), `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` returns an array nothing ever writes to (so it is always empty) and its action route answers `success: true` for any id without changing anything, and `POST /api/certifications/{id}/verify` always answers `verified: false` with a hard-coded issuer `test-issuer`. The real database-backed handlers in originate are never reached for the first three. Read from code; not probed on a running stack.

Found while re-verifying the platform-k docs for KS-1807 (PR-2, document lifecycle, status codes, error envelope). The docs and the published spec describe these as real operations; the code comment on the queue says "in-memory, development only" but nothing enforces that.

## Evidence

* **Registration order:** `app.use(createAdminRoutes(...))` and `app.use(createVerificationRoutes(...))` in `services/api-gateway/src/index.ts` come before `app.use(createProxyRoutes(...))`, so a route defined in `routes/admin.ts` or `routes/verification.ts` answers before the `/api/admin/` proxy to originate is reached. The only environment check in `routes/admin.ts` is the demo-seed flag; none wraps these handlers.
* **Audit logs:** `router.get('/api/admin/audit-logs', requireAdmin, ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/admin.ts` filters a literal 4-row array (`evt-1` to `evt-4`, actor `admin` at `test.local`) by `action` and `resourceType` and returns `{ success, logs, events, total }`. `router.get('/api/security/audit', ...)` does the same with a literal 3-row array. Originate has the real handler (`adminConfigRouter.get('/audit-logs')` in `services/originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts`); it is shadowed.
* **Verification queue:** `const mockVerificationQueue = []` ("in-memory, development only") backs `GET /api/admin/verification-queue` (always `items: []`, `total: 0`) and `POST /api/admin/verification-queue/{id}/action`, which validates the action word, updates the array entry only if one exists, and answers `{ success: true, id, action, ... }` for any id. Originate's database-backed `GET`/`POST` for the same paths (`adminConfig.ts`) are shadowed.
* **Certification verify:** `router.post('/api/certifications/:id/verify', ...)` in `services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts` ("MOCK ... ENDPOINTS (for E2E tests)", "for test compatibility") checks that the certification exists, then answers `verified: false`, `status: 'issued'`, `issuer: { id: 'test-issuer', verified: true }`, `blockchain.anchored: false`, `confidence: 'pending-onchain'` whatever the certification is. Its comment says it is a stopgap "until the originate→anchoring rewire lands". Originate's own verify handler is never reached.
* **What the docs and spec say:** `QUICK-REFERENCE.md` lists all four as working endpoints (certification verify, the verification queue and its action, audit logs and the `security/audit` alias). The published spec declares only `GET /api/security/audit`; certification verify, `admin/audit-logs` and the two queue routes are live routes with no spec entry (0 hits for each path in `secuura-api.yaml`; control: `/api/billing/customers/by-email` hits).

## How to confirm

As a platform admin, call `GET /api/admin/audit-logs` on a stack with real audit rows and compare with the database; call the verification-queue action with a random id and read `success: true`; call certification verify on a real certification. Not run.

## Suggested direction (your call)

Per the ruling recorded on KS-1668 the docs lead and the code aligns; Kam decides which side moves. Either remove the gateway stand-ins so the proxy reaches originate, or gate them to test environments behind an explicit flag and document that they are test doubles.

Searched the board before filing: `verification-queue` and `audit-logs` are not covered by an existing ticket about the gateway stand-ins; KS-736 is about mount authentication, not these handlers. Control in the same session: `Connector keys are minted` returned KS-1433.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events: any tenant user can record a lifecycle event on any document and trigger its anchor emission
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/lifecycle-events` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:2757-2877` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the action vocabulary, the payload's shape and the caller's tenant, and nothing about the caller's role or relation to the document. Any authenticated user in the tenant can record a lifecycle event on any document. The route then calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), which posts to the anchoring service with the caller's bearer. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No `isAllowedByRoleOrScope`, no owner check and no creating-connector check between :2757 and :2877. `getDocument` scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* It writes an event row (`createLifecycleEvent`, :2809), records connector provenance for a connector caller, and calls `emitLifecycleAnchor` (:2843), then stores the anchor id on the event.
* `emitLifecycleAnchor`'s comment (:1349-1362) says anchoring is idempotent per (document, network): re-anchoring an already-anchored document returns its existing anchor id. For a document with no anchor row, whether the call submits a new transaction (and spends a fee) is UNMEASURED; I did not read anchoring's `POST /api/anchors` wallet path.
* The vocabulary includes `delete` and `restore` (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:38-46`).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's checks do not apply unchanged. A terminal-status refusal would break `restore` on a deleted document. Platform S sends this route under the owning organisation's connector key (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19), and which humans should be allowed is not settled, so it needs its own predicate.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates the document's record (an event row) and may cause an anchoring submission.

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; the fee question above is unmeasured.

title: POST /api/documents/:id/sign: any tenant user can sign any document, can turn a revoked document into signed, and no signature is verified
description:
**BLUF:** originate `POST /api/documents/:id/sign` (`Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:1271-1346` at develop `d7ddfa1f6433`) checks authentication, the request body, the caller's tenant and the signing nonce, and nothing about the caller or the document's state. It then appends a signature and writes `status: 'signed'` (:1326-1329) through `updateDocument` with no options, so a revoked or deleted document is written back to `signed`. The signature itself is not verified: `isValidSignature` (:1313) accepts any string that starts `mock_signature_` or is longer than 50 characters, in every environment. Found in the KS-1814 sibling sweep. Read, not run.

**What I read**

* No role or scope gate, no owner or signer check and no terminal-status check between :1271 and :1346. `getDocument` (:1294) scopes the lookup to the caller's tenant only.
* The nonce (:1299-1311) ties the call to a `POST /:id/sign/request` for the same document id, and that route is open to any authenticated user in the tenant (filed separately).
* `updateDocument(id, tenantId, { signatures, status: 'signed' })` passes no `preserveTerminalStatuses`, so documentRepo's KS-521 guard (it keeps `revoked` and `deleted` only when asked) is off for this write.
* `isValidSignature = signature.startsWith('mock_signature_') || signature.length > 50` (:1313): no cryptographic check and no environment guard. KS-627 is the wallet-connector analogue (`POST /api/wallets/verify`), not this route.
* Callers: the issuer UI's Sign button posts here (`frontend/issuer/src/components/DocumentDetail.tsx:252`); the api-gateway mounts it with `authenticateToken(true)` and `blockPendingApproval` only (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:1026`). Platform S does not list this verb among the ones it sends (KS-1688, comment of 2026-10-19).

**Why it is not fixed in the KS-1814 pull request:** the anchor route's predicate (a write role or scope, then admin, owner or creating connector) does not apply unchanged here. A signer is not necessarily the owner or a write-role holder, so who may sign is this route's own policy question. A terminal-status refusal would apply, but on its own it does not close the route.

**Priority 2:** the route mutates a document (its signatures and its status).

**Not done:** no request against any box; no test written; whether any environment relies on the `mock_signature_` prefix today is not measured.

title: anchoring: the in-lock confirmed write omits the transaction hash, so a same-payload upsert can leave a confirmed row with a NULL hash
description:
**BLUF:** Inferred from the code, not reproduced. The in-lock `confirmed` write carries no `transactionHash`, the front-door upsert overwrites the stored hash on conflict, and guard 2 treats a row without a 64-hex hash as "no known submission". A same-payload upsert that lands during the roughly 27-minute in-lock confirmation poll could therefore leave the row `confirmed` with a NULL hash, and the queued call would build and submit a second transaction. Money-class; ruled High by Wednesday.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/anchorSubmission.ts:490-499`: the `confirmed` update sets status, confirmations, block number, slot, block hash, `confirmedAt` and `expectMetadataPayload`, and no `transactionHash`; the earlier `submitted` update (`:482`) does set it.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:1454-1456`: the front-door insert is `ON CONFLICT (document_id, network) DO UPDATE SET status = EXCLUDED.status, transaction_hash = EXCLUDED.transaction_hash, ...`.
* `anchorSubmission.ts:430-432` (guard 2 re-reads the row inside the lock and returns "already" only if `knownChainSubmission` yields a hash) and `:244-251` (`knownChainSubmission` needs status submitting, submitted or confirmed AND a 64-hex `transactionHash`).
* The poll length comes from Seat R 61st's arithmetic on KS-1816 (27.2 to 28.2 minutes); I did not recompute it.

## What I did not run or read

* No reproduction, no database, no box. I did not read the compare-and-set in `anchorStatusUpdate.ts` or whether `expectMetadataPayload` would restore the hash on the `confirmed` write.

## Source and searches

KS-1384 design rev4 section 18.20 (/Volumes/DevMASTER/!CODING/Secuura/Blockchain/5_Project_History/2026-10-29_seatW-9th/KS-1384-per-event-anchor-DESIGN-rev4.md). Board, archived included: "knownChainSubmission" 1 hit (KS-726, archived; its description says guards 1 and 2 need a populated hash, which is this finding's premise); "NULL hash" 6 hits, read KS-1384: no match for this finding.
Register note: this belongs to security work-stream D (KS-489, blockchain / anchoring integrity). KS-489 is archived, so it is not revived; the finding is recorded here and in one facts-only comment on KS-485.

title: nft-certificate is handed the same platform wallet mnemonic as anchoring, and POST /api/nft/mint has no role check
description:
**BLUF:** The nft-certificate service is configured with the same `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` as anchoring, so two processes can spend one wallet with no shared lock, and `POST /api/nft/mint` has no role check, so any authenticated caller can trigger a real mint when the chain keys are set. The double-spend race (the KS-535 class) is inferred, not reproduced. High, security and money.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:1311` (anchoring) and `:1694` (nft-certificate): both set `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC=${PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC:-}`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/cardano/index.ts:30-42`: with `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` set it initialises the real wallet; without them it runs in mock mode. Submission goes through `blockfrost.txSubmit` (`cardano/provider.ts:84`).
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/nft-certificate/src/app.ts:44`: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate({ publicOps: [the two verify operations] }))`, so the mint is authenticated only. `routes/nft.routes.ts:62` (the mint handler) has no role check; the only role check in that file is on `PUT /admin/platform-fee` (`:687-693`).
* A search of the service's non-test source for walletlock, mutex and advisory finds 0 hits. `minting.service.ts:224` and `:410` set `userId: 'user-id'` with the comment "Would come from auth context".

## What I did not run or read

* Whether the service runs, or has the chain keys set, on any box: UNMEASURED. Whether `mintNFT` checks that the certification belongs to the caller: not read. No request was sent.

## Source and searches

Board, archived included: "nft/mint" 5 hits (all spec-sweep tickets, none about authorisation); "nft-certificate" is too broad to read (67 hits); the KS-1384 text has no match for PLATFORM_WALLET or nft-certificate.

title: anchoring POST /api/anchors/thread-mint spends the platform wallet outside withWalletLock for any authenticated caller (fee drain)
description:
**BLUF:** `POST /api/anchors/thread-mint` has no role check, and a non-dry-run call signs and submits a mint transaction from the platform wallet without taking `withWalletLock`, which the anchoring paths use. By the source, any caller with a valid token that reaches the anchoring service can spend the platform wallet's funds, and its spend can race the anchoring queue for the same UTxOs (the failure class KS-535 recorded; the race is inferred, not reproduced). High, security.

## What I read (develop 6d41673e0f79)

* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/index.ts:470`: `app.use('/api', jwtAuthenticate())`, so the route is authenticated, nothing more.
* `index.ts:1008-1089`: the handler validates the body, then (when `BLOCKFROST_API_KEY` and `PLATFORM_WALLET_MNEMONIC` are set) imports `mintAndLock` (`:1052`) and calls it. It reads no caller, role or tenant, and runs no database query.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/anchoring/src/cardano/threadTokenMint.ts`: `mintAndLock` picks a seed UTxO from the platform wallet (`:262-266`), builds, signs and calls `signed.submit()` (`:339`). `dryRun: true` returns before the submit (`:322`).
* `withWalletLock` appears 0 times in `threadTokenMint.ts` and in the handler. Control: 5 times in `anchorSubmission.ts`, and the batch path calls it at `index.ts:1991`.

## What I did not run or read

* No request to any box or process. Whether the gateway routes this path to outside callers: not read. How much each call costs (I did not read `threadTokenMint.ts:262-340` beyond the lines above): not measured. Whether the race with anchoring happens in practice: not reproduced.

title: Claude Code sessions have no secret-file guard on platform-k: add the PS-1361 hook with PS-1387's local-only exemption, covering every systemTest env and secrets file (and .env.stripe is not git-ignored)
description:
## BLUF

platform-s blocks a Claude Code session from printing a secret file ([PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule)), and is about to let through files that hold only local values ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot), [Secuura/platform-s#1199](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-1387-secret-file-guard-lets-local-only-values-through-55c48feacc56), In Review). **platform-k has neither.** At `develop` `bd6697e07` the repo's tracked `.claude/` holds only `skills/secuura-test-discipline/SKILL.md`: no `settings.json` and no hook. Nothing stops a session from running `cat`, `grep` or `diff` on `Blockchain/Dev/.env` (PII keys, JWT keys, datastore passwords), `.env.local` (OAuth and IdP credentials) or any systemTest secrets file. The only protection is a rule the session has to remember. [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) exists because that failed on platform-s on 26 Oct 2026 (`terraform fmt -check -diff .` printed every dev-ps secret).

Separately, `.env.stripe`-style files, which are planned, are **not git-ignored** on platform-k today (measured below).

## Verified (28 Oct 2026, K `develop` `bd6697e07`)

**K has no guard:** `git ls-files .claude` returns only the skill file.

**systemTest env and secrets files: tracked templates, and the real file each produces (all git-ignored, checked with** `git check-ignore` **on the file path):**

| Real file (git-ignored) | Template (tracked) | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `systemTest/playwright/.env` | `systemTest/playwright/.env.example` | Playwright credentials and targets |
| `systemTest/akto/.env` | `systemTest/akto/.env.example` | Akto harness env |
| `systemTest/akto/docker.env` | `systemTest/akto/docker.env.example` | Akto container env |
| `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/akto/config/secrets.example.yml` | Akto role credentials |
| `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.yml` | `systemTest/performance/config/secrets.example.yml` | k6 credentials |
| `systemTest/schemathesis/.env-slot<N>` | written by `scripts/run.py setup` | per-slot API token |
| `.env-*` slot credential files ([KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs), root `.gitignore:14-16`) | written by tooling | slot-scoped credentials |

`systemTest/performance/config/environments.yml` is tracked. Whether it may name a secret value is not established.

**platform-k product code: env and credential files the services, frontends and deployments read.** Each was checked with `git check-ignore` on the real file path, 28 Oct 2026, `bd6697e07`.

| Real file | Template (tracked) | Ignored? | Holds |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env` | `Blockchain/Dev/env.example` (canonical, [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap)); also `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` | yes | PII encryption and lookup keys, JWT keypair, datastore passwords, `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, `GATEWAY_VOUCH_SECRET` |
| `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local` | `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` (also `env.local.example`) | yes | OAuth / IdP client secrets |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/<svc>/.env` for analytics, anchoring, api-gateway, auth, billing, governance, guardian, kyc, m365-integration, nft-certificate, originate, prism, queue, referral, security, staking, timestamping, transfer, vc-issuer, wallet-connector (20 services) | `services/<svc>/.env.example` | yes, all 20 | per-service secrets (billing: Stripe keys; m365: Microsoft app secret; kyc: provider keys) |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/` real file for its second template | `services/billing/env.example` | **not established**: the real file name for this no-dot template is unknown | Stripe keys |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/azure/.env.staging` | `deployment/azure/env.staging.example` | yes | Azure staging deployment values |
| `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/cardano/.env` | `deployment/cardano/env.example` | yes | Cardano node / wallet configuration |
| `Blockchain/Dev/frontend/{admin,issuer,verifier}/.env.development` | none tracked | yes | frontend local overrides |
| `Blockchain/Dev/test-wallet.env`, `Blockchain/Dev/*.wallet.env` | none | yes (`.gitignore:133-135`) | wallet seed phrases |
| `Blockchain/Dev/docker/nginx-gateway/ssl/*.pem`, `*.key` | none | yes (`.gitignore:70-72`) | TLS private keys |
| `.keys/`, `credentials.json`, `*-credentials.json` | none | yes (`.gitignore:93`, `:138-139`) | key material, service-account credentials |
| `USER_TESTING/Testing Harness/handoff/` | none | yes (`.gitignore:185-186`) | super-admin login handoff |
| `observability/.env`, `observability/config/alerting.env` | `observability/.env.example`, `observability/config/alerting.env.example` | yes | alerting webhooks and tokens |
| `Blockchain/Dev/services/billing/.env.stripe` (planned style) | none | **NOT ignored** | would hold Stripe keys |

Every row except the last belongs in the hook's refuse list, and none qualifies for the local-only exemption: these are product secrets, not systemTest targets. The "Holds" column is from the template names and the service's purpose, not from opening any real file.

`.env.stripe` **is not git-ignored:**

```
K  systemTest/.env.stripe          NOT-ignored
K  Blockchain/Dev/.env.stripe      NOT-ignored
```

K's root `.gitignore` names `.env`, `.env-*`, `.env.local` and a fixed list of `.env.<stage>` names, not `.env.*`. A Stripe file created today could be committed.

## Proposed scope (for the owner to decide)

1. **A PreToolUse hook for Bash, Read and Grep**, `onFailure: block`, modelled on platform-s's `.claude/hooks/block_secret_reads.py`:
   * it refuses any reader (cat, grep, sed, diff, jq, base64, …) pointed at the files above, plus Terraform state, plans and tfvars, and an unformatted `docker inspect` or `docker exec … env` on K containers;
   * it allows a command that only names a file (`ls`, `stat`, `test -f`, `git check-ignore`);
   * it allows a single-field `docker inspect --format`, which the K build proof uses for `org.opencontainers.image.revision`.
2. [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)**'s local-only exemption, if Kamil agrees.** A systemTest env file whose every URL / base-URL key points at `localhost` / `127.0.0.1` is readable. Anything remote, missing or unreadable stays secret. `Blockchain/Dev/.env` **and** `.env.local` **stay guarded whatever their URLs**, because they hold real PII-encryption, JWT and OAuth material.
3. **A** `.gitignore` **rule for** `.env.*` **env files** (`.env.stripe` and successors) that keeps every `*.example` template tracked.
4. **A contract test pinning what the hook refuses and allows**, as platform-s's `SecretReadHookContractTests` does. Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.

**Why it matters for running the suites.** Building K, building S and running every systemTest suite need these files created and merged from their templates. With a guard on K, the exemption in item 2 decides which K files a session can merge blind. That needs settling before the guard lands, or the env-setup step breaks the same way.

## Runs on a developer's Mac, as platform-s#1199 does

platform-s#1199 ([PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot)) is written for a developer's own Mac running local stack slots. The platform-k guard should take the same shape:

* **Where it runs.** A Claude Code `PreToolUse` hook on the Mac, registered in `.claude/settings.json` as `python3 "$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR/.claude/hooks/<name>.py"`, `onFailure: block`. `python3` ships with macOS (Xcode Command Line Tools), so no install is needed. `$CLAUDE_PROJECT_DIR` is the session's project folder, normally the root checkout, not a ticket worktree. A guard change therefore takes effect once the root checkout is on a `develop` that contains it.
* **What "this machine" means.** As in #1199: `localhost`, `127.0.0.1`, `::1`, `[::1]`. A systemTest env file is exempt only while every URL / base-URL key in it points there. That covers the local slots `SECUURA_STACK_SLOT` 1–4, gateway `6882 + 100·(N−1)`. A file pointed at Kintsugi, demo-pk, Container Apps or any remote host stays secret, and so does a missing or unreadable file.
* **Still guarded on the Mac, as in #1199:**
  * a bare `env` / `printenv`, because the developer's shell holds real tokens;
  * the product files in the table above, which are real keys even on a laptop;
  * Terraform state, plans and tfvars.
* **K slot containers (**`secuura-s<N>-*`**, and slot 1's** `secuura-*`**).** Unlike platform-s's slot containers, they are **not** exempt. Their environment comes from `Blockchain/Dev/.env` and `.env.local` (PII and JWT keys, OAuth secrets). An unformatted `docker inspect`, or `docker exec … env` / `printenv`, is refused. A single-field `docker inspect --format '{{ index .Config.Labels "org.opencontainers.image.revision" }}'` and `--format '{{.RestartCount}}'` stay allowed, because the build proof needs them.
* **macOS tools.** The rules match on command text, so they must hold for BSD `sed`, `grep`, `stat` and `xargs` as well as GNU forms.
* **A search pattern that names a secret file is not a read** (the #1199 false-positive fix). For example, `grep -E 'tfvars|tfstate' .gitignore` is allowed. A secret file as a file operand, or as the value of `-f`, is still refused. This session's own grep of K's `.gitignore` was refused by platform-s's guard for exactly this reason.

## Acceptance criteria

1. **An automated test, offline on macOS.** A contract test, run by the K preflight and the pre-push hook with no stack up, drives the hook through `python3` on the Mac. It covers:
   * a refused and an allowed case for every file in the tables above;
   * a localhost, a remote-URL and a missing-file case for each exempt systemTest file;
   * the K-container `docker inspect` / `exec` rules;
   * a search-pattern-only grep (allowed);
   * a `.env.stripe` file that is git-ignored while its `.example` is not.

   Fixture files go in a temp folder, never the real ones.
2. **Docs:** `CLAUDE.md` → security section, and `systemTest/CLAUDE.md`, name the guard, the exemption and the file list. `Projects Documents/Stack-Slots-How-To.md` is changed only if the env-setup steps change.
3. **systemTests:** no spec, page object or fixture change. The guard's test is a contract test. Each systemTest `.env.example` should say in a comment whether its real file is exempt.

## Related

* [PS-1361](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1361/block-claude-code-sessions-from-printing-secret-files-hook-rule) (the platform-s guard).
* [PS-1387](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1387/secret-file-guard-exempt-local-only-values-systemtestenv-local-slot) / platform-s#1199 (the local-only exemption, In Review).
* [KS-1608](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1608/akto-harness-writes-credentials-to-disk-and-into-reports-reportjson) (Akto credentials written to reports, Done).
* [KS-1098](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1098/k6-runner-echo-mask-enamevalue-and-qe-namevalue-still-print-the-value) (k6 echo mask).
* [KS-674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-674/playwright-documentsspects-3-cases-fail-whenever-their-slot-runs) (slot credential files).
* [KS-1081](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1081/config-drift-two-tracked-env-templates-disagree-by-39-vars-bootstrap) (env template drift).

Raised from the [PS-1381](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-1381/systemtest-a11y-keyboard-journey-power-user-keyboard-enter-on-the) session. **Not assigned:** the `.claude/` tooling owner on platform-k is undecided. The systemTest parts are Peter's, the rest is Kamil's.

title: systemTest (Schemathesis): run the object_level_authorization leg with peers in two different tenants (split from KS-1674)
description:
> ⛔ **Blocked by** [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) (2026-10-27). Parked until [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers a supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack. No work starts here before then.

**BLUF:** [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) made Schemathesis's `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906, ST402) run in its own `[auth.wfc]` leg, but with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant. This ticket is the remaining part of [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)'s scope: peers in two **different** tenants, so cross-tenant exposure is measured rather than inferred. It is blocked by [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack), which asks for a supported way to put a user in a second tenant.

## Today (develop, after PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), `5671d5115`)

* Peers: `["owner", "ownerPeer"]`, both OWNER in the default tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`; actors in `systemTest/fixtures/actors.ts`, provisioned by `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`).
* Why: no local route places a user in a second tenant. The reasons are in [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack).

## Scope (once [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) lands)

* Provision a peer in the second tenant through the route [KS-1740](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1740/no-supported-way-to-put-a-user-in-a-second-tenant-on-a-local-stack) delivers (API only; no direct database writes).
* Point the leg's peers at the cross-tenant pair. Whether to keep the same-tenant pair as well (two leg runs, or three peers) is decided in the plan.
* Update the comment above the leg config, which today records the cross-tenant pairing as remaining scope on [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under).

## Acceptance criteria

1. Red/green proof: a stub API that leaks one tenant's object to a peer in another tenant is reported as ST402 / WFC 906 on every surface (console, JSON verdict, NDJSON, HTML report), and is missed when the cross-tenant peer is removed.
2. A live run on a slot shows peer replays between the two tenants (the leg's peer-replay count, not the NDJSON check matrix, which records `success` even when the check does not run; see [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under)).
3. Every new pair from the first live run is triaged: an existing ticket ([KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object), [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a)) or a new KS ticket, never masked or baselined without an owner.
4. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` and both `Projects Documents` HTML docs updated.

Split from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). Peter owns systemTest security work ([KS-492](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-492/review-g-systemtest-all-tools-security-regression-coverage) G).

title: No supported way to put a user in a second tenant on a local stack — needed for cross-tenant systemTest peers (split from KS-1674)
description:
**BLUF:** systemTest needs two ordinary (non-super-admin) users in two **different** tenants on a local slot, so the Schemathesis `object_level_authorization` check (BOLA/IDOR, WFC 906) can test cross-tenant isolation. On develop there is no supported route that does this. This ticket asks for that capability; how it is built is your call. The systemTest side is a separate ticket, blocked by this one.

## Why it is needed

[KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) (PR [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#1673](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-1674-schemathesis-object-level-authorization-runs-in-its-own-aec22065af81), merged as `5671d5115`) runs `object_level_authorization` with two OWNER peers in the **same** tenant (`systemTest/schemathesis/config/schemathesis_tests.yaml:650-668`). The ticket asked for peers across two tenants. Without them, cross-tenant exposure on findings such as [KS-1703](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1703/security-seven-get-by-id-routes-serve-any-authenticated-callers-object) is inferred, not measured.

## Why the existing routes do not work (read on develop `5f6899918`; nothing run)

1. **Self-registration lands in the default tenant.** `POST /api/auth/register` takes the tenant from `x-tenant-id` / `x-tenant-slug` (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:217-218`), but the gateway strips client-sent trust headers (`services/api-gateway/src/index.ts:309-330`). A tenantless token is then given `DEFAULT_TENANT_ID` (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:503`).
2. **Tenant from email domain at login is off, and would not persist.** `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:549-586` runs only when `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED=true` (defaults to `false` in `docker-compose.yml`). Its own comment says the `UPDATE users SET tenant_id` is a no-op under fail-closed RLS ([KS-458](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-458/rls-fail-closed-flip-guc-on-checkout-flip-the-consolidated-tenant)).
3. `X-Tenant-Override` **applies only to super-admin roles** (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/auth.ts:515-521`). A super-admin can read every object, so it cannot act as a peer. (The override is also partly broken: [KS-1704](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1704/security-two-cross-tenant-isolation-regressions-fail-on-develop-a).)
4. **Invited stub then register keeps the stub's tenant** (`auth.ts:237-242`, [KS-74](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-74/pending-invite-ux-post-apicertificationsissue-accepts-holderemail-and)), but `POST /api/users/stub` takes the tenant from the caller's own verified token (`services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:398`). A caller can only mint stubs in a tenant they are already in.
5. **Not verified:** a connector token carries its own tenant (`services/auth/src/middleware/authenticate.ts:116`) and is accepted on `/api/users/stub`. If a connector can be issued for a second tenant, that may already be a route. Worth checking before building anything new.

## Acceptance criteria

1. A documented, supported sequence of API calls, runnable on a local slot without editing the database by hand, that (a) creates or selects a second tenant and (b) leaves a named, non-super-admin user (OWNER or another self-service role) whose verified token carries that tenant's id.
2. The user can log in and is scoped to that tenant on later requests (the gateway forwards its `x-tenant-id`, not the default).
3. The sequence is described here, or in the relevant service docs, so systemTest can call it from `systemTest/fixtures/provision-actors.ts`.

Raised from [KS-1674](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1674/schemathesis-object-level-authorization-4310-never-runs-under) at Peter's request (2026-10-26). The systemTest follow-up is assigned to Peter and blocked by this ticket.

title: Node 26's semver-major Readable.read() change truncates every synchronous cbor.encode() to its first byte on host test runs - images pin node:24 and are unaffected
description:
**Node 26.0.0 removed the behaviour** `cbor`**'s synchronous encoder depends on, so on a Node 26 host every** `cbor.encode()` **of a value longer than one byte returns only its first byte. Host-side test runs are affected; the deployed images are not. The failure mode is fail-closed.**

## The mechanism

Node commit `fadb214d95` / PR 60441, *"stream: readable read one buffer at a time"*, is listed **semver-major in the v26.0.0 changelog** (2026-05-05): `Readable.prototype.read()` with no size argument no longer concatenates the internal buffer, it returns one queued chunk. Deliberate, to avoid the cost of merging buffers — **so this is not a bug and no Node patch will restore the old behaviour.** *(Commit, PR and changelog entry identified via web search, not read at source.)*

`cbor`'s synchronous `encode()` / `encodeOne()` / `encodeCanonical()` are all `_encodeAll` (`encoder.js:595-602`):

```js
_encodeAll(objs) { const bs = new NoFilter({…}); this.pipe(bs); … this.end(); return bs.read() }
```

`NoFilter.read(size)` (`nofilter@3.1.0`, `lib/index.js:285`) delegates straight to `super.read(size)`. Its own documented contract is "no size argument → return all the data in the internal buffer", which is exactly what Node 26 withdrew.

## Measured on this host (Node v26.8.1, `cbor@9.0.2`)

| value encoded | returned | correct |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `['Signature1', …]` | `84` (1 B) | \~90 B |
| `'Signature1'` | `6a` (1 B) | `6a5369676e617475726531` |
| `Buffer.alloc(4,0xab)` | `44` (1 B) | `44abababab` |
| `Map{1:-8}` | `a1` (1 B) | `a10127` |
| `Map{1:1,3:-8,-1:6,-2:<32B>}` | `a4` (1 B) | \~45 B |

Not container-specific — **every** value whose encoding exceeds one byte is truncated. `7` and `Map{}` come back correct only because they are one byte already, which is what makes this quiet. Decoding a truncated value throws `Insufficient data`.

Scoped to the synchronous path: `cbor.encodeAsync` **is correct** (`83010203`) and **the decoder is healthy** (`decodeFirstSync('83010203')` → `[1,2,3]`).

## It is the runtime, proven with zero dependencies and a second runtime

Pure `stream.PassThrough`, 4 bytes written as 3 chunks, no packages involved:

|  | Node v26.8.1 | Node v24.22.1 |
| -- | -- | -- |
| 3 chunks, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| 3 chunks + `end()`, `read()` | `83` | `83010203` |
| one 4-byte chunk, `read()` *(control)* | `83010203` | `83010203` |
| `read(4)` explicit size | `83010203` | `83010203` |

The control discriminates, so the zero is a real zero. Successive `read()` calls on Node 26 return `83`,`01`,`0203` in order — the bytes are all present, merely no longer concatenated. `read(readableLength)` is the documented approximation and was verified on Node 26.

Node 24 runs were in throwaway `docker run --rm node:24-alpine` containers from an image already present on the host; nothing was installed, downloaded or built. This laptop has **only** Homebrew `node@26` (v26.8.1) — no Node 24, no nvm/fnm/volta/asdf.

## Items

### (a) Remedy options — no choice made, this needs a ruling

1. **Pin the dev/test runtime to Node 24**, which is what every image already ships: tighten `engines.node` (today the root is `>=18.0.0`, which *permits* Node 26) and add a runtime file (`.nvmrc` / `.node-version`) so host runs match the images. There is currently **no** `.nvmrc` in the repo and `packages/shared` declares **no** `engines` **at all**.
2. **An upstream fix in** `cbor` **and/or** `nofilter` — have `_encodeAll` read the whole buffer (`read(readableLength)`, or drain in a loop and concatenate). Not filed upstream by this investigation; `cbor`/`nofilter` issue trackers were **not** searched.
3. ⚠ **Not an option: bumping** `cbor`**.** `cbor@10.0.12` **is broken identically — measured**, not assumed, against an on-disk copy under `@meshsdk/provider`: all four cases truncate the same way. **The open dependabot PR 635 (**`cbor` **9.0.2 → 10.0.12) does NOT fix this.**

### (b) KS-1727 is the first known symptom

`packages/shared/src/__tests__/wallet-signature.test.ts:47-49`, the file's only positive cell. `verifyMessageSignature` exits at `wallet.ts:372` (`CIP-8: failed to extract Ed25519 public key from COSEKey`) because the COSEKey the test hands it is the 1-byte `a4`. **Both** `wallet.ts` **and the test are correct**; the four negative cells pass only because all four assert `false`, which a verifier that always returns false satisfies. On Node 24, same cbor bytes from the same disk, the positive cell `RETURNS TRUE` **(**`wallet.ts:418`**)** and the negative exits at `:391` (payload mismatch), so the KS 278 payload binding is intact.

### (c) Related — flagged, not investigated

* **KS 1734** — `services/security`, 11 of 33 test files fail on the first run after `npm ci`; records Node v26.
* **KS 1729** — vc-issuer unit suite cold-run skips; records Node v26.
* **KS 1625** — the standing contradiction that admits a Node 26 host at all: declared Node floor `engines.node >=18.0.0` versus what the images actually ship.

None of these was examined for this cause. They are named because they share the runtime, not because a link was measured.

## Scope — deployed services are NOT affected

* **All 32 Dockerfiles pin** `node:24-alpine` (75 `FROM` lines, zero exceptions), `originate` included — the service hosting `/sign-wallet`. Node 24 encodes correctly, so no deployed route carries this. **No deployed route was called.**
* The only synchronous `cbor.encode` in tracked production source is `wallet.ts:397`; the other five occurrences are inside the test file. Two `decodeFirstSync` sites, both on the healthy decoder.
* Where it would bite on a Node 26 host, it **fails closed**: a real wallet supplies a properly-encoded COSEKey, so the failure lands at `:397` and surfaces as `Ed25519 signature verification failed` — valid signatures rejected, never invalid ones accepted. **Not a forgery surface.**

## Searched first

By symbol, file path and error string, titles + descriptions, `includeArchived: true`: `cbor.encode`, `nofilter`, `Readable.read`, `_encodeAll`, `encodeAsync`, `readableHighWaterMark` — **0 hits each**. `verifyMessageSignature` → 2 hits, KS-1727 and KS 1229 (Done). Control: the same instrument returns 25 hits for `node:24-alpine` and 3 for `Node v26`, so it can fire.

## UNMEASURED

* Whether the transitive `cbor` consumers (`services/anchoring`, `services/nft-certificate`, `frontend/issuer` lockfiles, `@meshsdk/provider`) call the synchronous encode internally — not traced.
* Whether `cbor` or `nofilter` upstream has a fix or an open issue for Node ≥26.
* Which other packages on this laptop depend on the same withdrawn `read()` contract — the repo-wide blast radius of Node 26 beyond CBOR.
* When host runs first moved to Node 26, and when KS-1727's cell began failing (develop was not bisected).

Evidence: `5_Project_History/2026-10-26_seatV-2nd/` — 8 probes, 19 output files, secret-scanned.

title: ks1557-verify-trusts-certification-evidence.integration.test.ts: 3 cells go red when TZ=Australia/Sydney (timezone-dependent test or code)
description:
## BLUF

Under `TZ=Australia/Sydney`, 3 cells of `Blockchain/Dev/services/originate/src/__tests__/ks1557-verify-trusts-certification-evidence.integration.test.ts` go red (reported by Peter, 2026-10-22). The cause is not yet established: it may be the test (a local-time assumption) or the code under test.
