title: The e2e-v2 harness is platform-k's only browser, portal and accessibility coverage — 222 tests, runnable by hand, named in no gate and absent from the gate inventory
description:
## BLUF

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/` holds **24 spec files and 222 tests** across four tiers — including every browser journey and the only accessibility coverage platform-k has — and it is wired into nothing. It is not in `.githooks/pre-push`, it has no row in the "Manual CI-gate equivalents" table that `KS-685` commissioned, and the workflow its own README points at (`.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`) does not exist on `develop`. Meanwhile the suite people *are* pointed at, `systemTest/playwright`, is API-only: 3 spec files, 11 tests, no browser. So the documented estate says platform-k has a Playwright tier, and the thing that actually opens a browser is the one nobody is told to run. Counted on `develop` `8ba2da02d`, 29 Sep 2026. Nothing was executed — this is about wiring, not results.

## What is there

Measured from the tree, not from the docs:

| Tier | Specs | Tests | What it covers |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `tier1-api` | 12 | 174 | API over HTTP |
| `tier2-smoke` | 5 | 43 | Smoke journeys |
| `tier3-e2e` | 4 | 40 | **Real browser journeys** — issuer, admin, verifier |
| `tier4-a11y` | 3 | 6 | **axe on admin, issuer and verifier** |
| **Total** | **24** | **222** |  |

It is runnable today. `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` declares `test`, `test:api`, `test:smoke`, `test:e2e`, `test:a11y`, `install:browsers` and `report`, and `playwright.config.ts` defines the four matching projects (`api`, `smoke`, `e2e`, `a11y`). `@axe-core/playwright` is a devDependency there.

## What is missing

1. **No gate names it.** `grep -rn "e2e-v2" .githooks/pre-push Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` returns nothing. The manual-gate table at `DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143` maps *former CI job → local command* for 13 rows and has no row for e2e-v2, and none for accessibility at all.
2. **Its README cites a workflow that does not exist.** `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` sends the reader to `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`; `git ls-tree origin/develop .github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml` is empty.
3. **The plan doc under-reports it.** `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` still says *"only the verifier portal has a tier-4 spec. Issuer + admin coverage is a follow-up."* That follow-up is `KS-44`, which is **Done** — there are three tier-4 specs in the tree today. The row understates the coverage that exists.

## Why it matters

* It is the whole UI answer. Without it the honest statement about platform-k is that no browser opens anywhere in the estate — `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` says so itself, and `DEV-PROCESS.md:141` spells it out: *"Despite the name, this suite drives no browser… Read a green here as '12 API assertions passed', not as 'the portals work'."*
* It is the whole accessibility answer. There is no `eslint-plugin-jsx-a11y` anywhere in the repo and no axe inside any frontend, so `tier4-a11y` is the only thing that would catch a regression against WCAG 2.2 / EN 301 549 — relevant to the same obligations the platform-s side tracks. WCAG 2.2: [https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/](<https://www.w3.org/TR/WCAG22/>) · EN 301 549 v3.2.1: [https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf](<https://www.etsi.org/deliver/etsi_en/301500_301599/301549/03.02.01_60/en_301549v030201p.pdf>) · EAA Directive 2019/882: [https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj](<https://eur-lex.europa.eu/eli/dir/2019/882/oj>)
* An ungated suite rots quietly. `KS-557` / `KS-560` are the precedent — the tier reported 126 failures, of which only 11 were real, and the cause was a harness defect that had gone unnoticed. `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` keeps that lesson as a standing rule.
* Actions being retired makes this the *only* route to the coverage, not a redundant one.

## Suggested shape

1. Give e2e-v2 a row in the `DEV-PROCESS.md` manual-gate table: the exact command, the pass criterion, and a measured wall-clock — matching the 13 rows already there.
2. Decide the tier split deliberately. `tier4-a11y` is 6 tests and needs only a running stack; it is the cheapest thing in the estate to make routine. `tier3-e2e` is slower and flakier (single-session collisions, `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md` § "Worker-session collisions") so it may belong in a nightly/manual tier rather than a per-push one.
3. Fix the two stale pointers: the dead workflow reference in `tests/e2e/README.md:4`, and the tier-4 row in `E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:324` that `KS-44` has already overtaken.
4. Say in `systemTest/CLAUDE.md` where the browser tier actually lives, so "Playwright" stops meaning two different things in the same repo.

## Acceptance

* `DEV-PROCESS.md`'s gate table has an e2e-v2 row (or rows) with a command and a measured time.
* A named person can run the a11y tier from the runbook without reading source.
* No document points at `.github/workflows/e2e-tests.yml`, and the tier-4 row reflects the three specs that exist.

## Decision needed before fixing — naming the three Playwright estates

Worth settling the naming in the same pass: `systemTest/playwright` (API-only, 11 tests) and `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2` (browser, 222 tests) are both "Playwright", and a third corpus sits at `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e` (`KS-734`, In Review — not a workspace member, cannot install from a clean checkout; `KS-1038`, Backlog — races its own lockout). Three Playwright estates with one name is the reason a reader can believe the portals are covered when the suite in the gate never opens a browser. One decision about which survives, which is gated, and what each is called would close this ticket and shrink two others.

## References

`Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e-v2/package.json` · `playwright.config.ts:29-73` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md:77-143`, `:141` · `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md:316-345` · `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/README.md:4` · `systemTest/playwright/playwright.config.ts:12-18` · `systemTest/CLAUDE.md:358` · related: `KS-1076` (Urgent, Todo — no Playwright e2e on a PR since 7 Sep), `KS-734` (In Review), `KS-1038` (Backlog), `KS-44` (Done), `KS-637` (Backlog), `KS-685`.

## Environment

Distributed_Secuura `develop` **8ba2da02d**, 29 Sep 2026. Static review — no stack started, no suite executed; all counts measured from the tree at that commit. GitHub Actions executes nothing on this repo (billing), so no workflow is a live alternative to the local route.

title: PR #1339's standalone locks were re-resolved from bare manifests: ~1,000 non-target moves, incl. runtime bullmq/msgpackr 2 and @azure/identity/msal-node 6
description:
Raised from **gate41's finding N-1339-2** (Major, non-blocking) on PR #1339 (KS-1378, the four-package advisory bump). Wednesday ruled this a ticket rather than a fold-in for round 2, because the only mechanism the gate's own fix-shape offers is `npm install --package-lock-only`, and host npm 11.5.1 dies with `Cannot read properties of null (reading 'edgesOut')` on this machine — measured by Seat B 43rd even on a bare `package.json` in an empty temp dir, so it is the host npm build and not the workspace layout.

## What happened

#1339's 13 standalone `package-lock.json` files were regenerated **from their bare manifests** rather than from their committed locks. That resolved every dependency afresh, so about **1,000 versions moved that the bump did not target**. All are inside their declared ranges, so nothing is a range violation — but nothing exercises them either: the suites run from the **root** lock, which moved **0** non-target versions.

## The moves that matter (gate-measured)

* `services/queue`: **bullmq 5.76.2 → 5.81.5**, pulling **msgpackr 1 → 2** — runtime.
* `services/m365-integration` and `packages/shared`: **@azure/identity 4.13.1 → 4.13.3**, pulling **@azure/msal-node 5 → 6** — runtime.
* `services/originate`: minimatch 3 → 10, plus dev-only eslint-cache majors.

## Fix-shape, quoted verbatim from gate41's report

> Fix-shape: regenerate each standalone lock FROM its committed lock (`npm install <pkg>@<ver> --package-lock-only`), or declare the drift and add a standalone-install smoke (build + boot) per service.

## The condition attached to #1339 merging without this

Wednesday's ANSWER to Seat B 44th, 2026-09-29T03:54:40Z: the two runtime moves above **get a clean standalone** `npm ci` **plus that service's own suite in the next gate**, so what ships untested by the root-lock suites is tested once. **Merged is not deployed:** no deploy carries these until this ticket is done or Kam says otherwise.

## Blocked on, and why it is not just "run the command"

`npm install` in any form is unavailable on this host. Seat B 43rd's workaround for #1339 was `node:24-alpine` (npm 11.19.0), mounted at `/src` — **never** `/dev`, which clobbers the container's `/dev/null` and dies rc 127 before starting. Whoever takes this needs either that container route explicitly permitted, or a working host npm.

## Neighbours (cross-reference only)

KS-1290 (an npm command inside a workspace member moves platform discriminators silently) and KS-1154 (the root lock carries only the darwin rollup binary) are the same family — lockfile regeneration doing more than it was asked to — but neither covers this drift.

Discovered 2026-09-29 by gate41 on PR #1339; ticketed by the Platform K build seat under Wednesday's ruling.

title: Security: certifications ends RLS FORCE with no tenant_isolation policy on every fresh database, permanently
description:
**Found by the gate39 QA pass over PR #1332 (N-G39-1, Major). Facts only.**

## What is wrong

On a **fresh bare database**, `public.certifications` ends with row-level security **ENABLED and FORCED but with no** `tenant_isolation` **policy**. RLS with no policy is **default-deny**, so the table is unreadable and unwritable by the application role — and unlike the defect #1332 fixed, **this does not heal on a later boot**. It is permanent for the life of that database.

Measured across all four head paths (gateway runner boot 1 and boot 2, `scripts/run-migrations.sh`, and both combined): identical, `4c59e2ebdc37`. The **merge-base differs** (`fd91b0ab5a48`) and **does** carry `CREATE POLICY tenant_isolation ON public.certifications` — so the merge-base heals it and the current tip does not. An app-role `INSERT` carrying the tenant GUC is **refused**.

## Why it changed

`migrations/038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` (added in #1332) creates `certifications` **before** 039 runs. 039 then finds the table present and applies its RLS `ENABLE`/`FORCE` block to it — but the branch of 039 that creates the `tenant_isolation` policy does not cover it on that path. Before #1332, `certifications` did not exist when 039 ran, so 039 skipped it entirely and a later boot created it with its policy intact.

## A FALSE CLAIM IN THE MERGED CODE, filed here deliberately rather than separately (N-G39-4)

`038a_ks1054_core_tables_before_039.sql` lines **16-17** describe this exact condition — `certifications` with RLS forced and no `tenant_isolation` policy — as one of the things the migration **fixes**. **It does not fix it; it is the cause of it.** The same header's claim that the schema equality is "proved … across … the docker/init seeded path" is also **wider than true**: the equality holds for `certifications` only, and fails for `oauth_apps` and `svc_webhooks` because of a pre-existing docker/init DDL difference (extra indexes and the `svc_webhooks_app_id_fkey` foreign key). Both header claims need correcting in the same change that fixes the policy, so the file does not keep asserting a fix it does not deliver.

## Fix shape (from the gate)

A migration numbered **after 039** that applies 039's `tenant_isolation` block to `certifications`, plus a **real-PostgreSQL cell driven as the application role** (`secuura_app`) asserting that an `INSERT` carrying the correct tenant GUC succeeds and one carrying a foreign tenant is refused. A source-text assertion is not sufficient here: the defect is a runtime default-deny, and only a driven app-role probe distinguishes "policy present" from "policy absent but table reachable as owner".

## Scope

Not fixed in #1332 — that PR was round 2 of 2 under the class cap and shipped GO WITH FINDINGS with this as named residue. No board ticket covered it before this one (searched by symbol: `certifications` + `tenant_isolation`, `tenant_isolation policy certifications`, `038a`, `certifications RLS force default-deny`, `certifications no tenant_isolation` — zero title-relevant results; three positive controls each returned their expected ticket first, so the search was working).

Refs KS-1054

title: api-gateway failed-login lockout is inert: createBruteForceProtection installs recordFailure, but no production code ever calls it — it can never block
description:
## Summary

For when you have a moment, Kamil. The gateway's failed-login lockout (`createBruteForceProtection`, `api-gateway/src/middleware/security.ts:146-192`) looks as though it never engages: it only blocks once `recordFailure()` has run, and nothing outside its own unit test seems to call it. The auth service's per-account lockout is still doing its job, so this is about the edge layer only. Either wiring it up or retiring it would be fine; whichever you prefer. Thank you.

+++ Evidence, and the two options

**What the code shows** (read-only, 2026-09-28)

* `security.ts:173-189` attaches `req.bruteForce = { recordFailure, recordSuccess }` and calls `next()`; nothing on the login's response path calls either helper.
* Searching `services/api-gateway/src` for `recordFailure` outside `middleware/security.ts` finds only `__tests__/security.test.ts:261`, which checks the helper exists.
* So `attempts` is never incremented, `blockedUntil` is never written, and the `429 "Too many failed attempts"` branch can't be reached.

**What the logs show**

* Slot 2's gateway, six hours of traffic including failed logins: **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_LOCKOUT`, **0** `BRUTE_FORCE_BLOCKED`.
* The lockout that does work is the auth service's (`services/auth/src/services/accountLockout.ts`: (email, /24), 5 failures in 15 min → 15-min lock). It answers **401** (`routes/auth.ts:339-342`).

**Why it came up:** [KS-1362](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1362/back-to-back-tiers-setup-logins-land-in-the-platforms-spent-60-second) first put some refused setup logins down to this lockout; on a closer look they were the global request window. It seemed worth recording that this layer isn't active, so no one leans on it.

**Options**

1. Wire it: call `recordFailure` / `recordSuccess` from the login proxy's response handling (401 / 2xx), with a test that shows a block after `freeRetries` failures.
2. Retire it: remove the middleware, its `bruteForce` config in `config/services.ts`, and the doc line at `security.ts:8`.

[KS-618](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-618/client-ip-is-invisible-platform-wide-on-demo-every-ip-keyed-control) (every IP-keyed control is shared behind one address) applies either way.

**Done means:** a test red on today's code shows N+1 failed logins from one address aren't blocked at the gateway; after the change they are — or the middleware and its claims are gone.

+++

title: POST /api/certifications/:id/verify forwards a revoked session's Bearer to originate: the gateway's session check never runs on this route
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/certifications/:id/verify` (api-gateway `routes/verification.ts:784`, mounted with no `authenticateToken`) forwards whatever `Authorization` the caller sent to originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` (`:788`). Measured in-process: a **REVOKED** session's JWT, alone or beside a valid connector key, reaches originate as that user's Bearer, because the gateway's session check never runs on this route. On `POST /api/documents/:id/verify` (`:488`, `authenticateToken(true)`) the same revoked JWT alone is refused 401 `SESSION_INVALIDATED`. What originate does with that token is **NOT measured**.

## Recommendation

Measure originate's `GET /api/documents/:id` with a revoked session's JWT. That sets the severity, which the gate graded Minor pending that measurement.

## Detail

* Surfaced by the #1070-#1076 gate (`2026-09-19-batch1070-1076-tier1-r1`, finding N76-2).
* Pre-existing, not introduced by that batch: api-gateway product bytes are identical at develop `51dbedd39` and at every head of the batch. `verification.ts` is unchanged at develop `f9c28a8b8`.
* How the gate measured it: in-process, the real gateway app with loopback doubles; not against a live stack or a real session store.
* Related: KS-834, the pending decision on whether this route stays public. KS-834's text says a caller who sends a token "is still scoped downstream"; this finding is that a *revoked* session's token passes the gateway here unchecked.
* Also related: the revocation property established on the authenticated mounts (KS-1207, KS-1215).
* Board search before filing (Secuura-PK, archived included):
  * literal title/description contains `certifications/:id/verify`: KS-834, KS-815 (archived, a control-byte guard);
  * `certifications/{id}/verify`: 0; `verification.ts:78`: 0;
  * `api/certifications/`: 38, none about Bearer forwarding;
  * `searchIssues("certifications verify")`, literal re-match: KS-834, KS-815.
  * None records the revoked-session forwarding.

title: Under multi-tenancy, auth's tenant-pool statements carry no tenant GUC: with fail-closed RLS every approve's level UPDATE matches 0 rows
description:
## BLUF

**With** `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` **on, auth's** `db.ts` **sends every statement that carries a tenant argument through** `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query()`**: a raw pool query with no tenant GUC.** Under fail-closed RLS, a tenant-scoped UPDATE then matches 0 rows.

* On the verification approve, develop answers a false **200 APPROVED while the level stays basic**. #1032's head instead refuses every approve (503, PENDING).
* **Major while that configuration runs; latent today.** The auth container in `services.bicep` does not set `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (read).
* **Evidence class:** MEASURED on the real `db.ts` and `TenantPoolManager` with `pg` faked and RLS MODELLED. Whether the runtime database role enforces RLS on that pool is unverified (no Postgres was run).
* Found by the #1032 round-2 QA gate (E-1, an escalation candidate).

## Recommendation

The owner's fix. Not built here.

* Route the tenant-pool branch through the GUC path (`queryWithTenantGuc`, with the GUC in the same transaction), or drop the tenant-pool branch while per-tenant databases are off.
* **Resolve the overlap first.** KS-174 (In Progress) step 1 plans this remedy: "Tenant-pool-manager (or a query wrapper) sets `set_config('app.current_tenant_id', tenantId, true)` per transaction". It never names `tenantManager`, `getPool` or auth's `db.ts`. KS-458 (Done) bundled the GUC for the default pool only. If KS-174 is the live home, merge this ticket into it; this one carries the measured location and consequence.
* **Census every** `query(…, tenantId)` **caller** before fixing. The gate's single-line grep found one, which is not a count.
* **Regression cell:** with multi-tenancy on and fail-closed RLS, an approve whose UPDATE carries the tenant either raises the level or is refused. Never a 200 over an unchanged level.

## Detail

* **Read at develop** `34cdcfb26`**,** `services/auth/src/db.ts:47-70`**:**
  * `query(text, params, tenantId)`: `if (tenantId && tenantManager)` returns `tenantManager.getPool(tenantId).query(text, params)` (`:53-60`). No GUC. The `try` does not `await`, so a rejected query is not caught by its fallback.
  * Only without a tenant manager does it use `runWithTenantId(tenantId, () => queryWithTenantGuc(getPool(), …))` (the KS-458 path).
* **When the branch is taken** (the gate's read): `initTenantManager` needs `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED === 'true'` and `PLATFORM_DATABASE_URL`. `TenantPoolManager.getPool` returns the default pool unless `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB === 'true'` and the tenant resolves to another database.
* **The gate's pool table** (approve, RLS modelled on):
  * manager on, no per-tenant DB: the UPDATE runs on the default pool with no GUC and matches 0 rows. Develop answers 200 APPROVED with the level basic (a false success). Head answers 503 PENDING basic, even with no fault.
  * a distinct tenant DB: the level UPDATE lands in the tenant database while the request row stays in the default database (a pre-existing split).
* **Callers read so far:** `getUserById(id, tenantId)` (`repositories/userRepo.ts:407`) and `updateUser`'s UPDATE (`:796`). The census is not done.
* **Config** (READ; unverifiable without `az`, not run):
  * the auth container in `services.bicep` has no `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` (the only bicep hit, `:798`, is originate's);
  * `env.dev.json` / `env.demo.json` set it `true` in a shared block (whether [deploy.sh](<http://deploy.sh>) consumes it was not re-read);
  * `docker-compose.yml` auth uses `${MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED:-false}`;
  * `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` is set nowhere in deployment or compose.
* **Related:** KS-1194 (where it was measured), KS-174, KS-458, KS-1055 (per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations).
* **Searched before filing** (Linear literal matches in titles, descriptions and comments, archived included, at most 6 pages of 50 fuzzy results per term):
  * `tenantManager.getPool`: 0 of 3 scanned.
  * `getPool`: 1, KS-213 (originate's per-tenant pool fan-out through pgbouncer; a different defect).
  * `applyTenantGuc`: 0, but the search returned no results, so that zero is the search's reach, not the board.
  * `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED`: 12, and `tenant GUC`: 19. The closest are KS-174 (above), KS-458, KS-468 (GUC not seeded on gateway proxy routes) and KS-1055. None names the tenant-pool branch in auth's `db.ts`.
* **Evidence:** #1032 round-2 gate report §7 and E-1: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-18-ks1194-1032-430672697-tier1-r2/report.md`.
* Refs KS-1194.

title: mcp-server POST /hash hashes any server-local file named by a caller-supplied filePath, with no auth - measure deployed exposure first
description:
## BLUF

**mcp-server's REST mirror** `POST /hash` **returns the SHA-256 of any server-local file named by a caller-supplied** `filePath`**, with no authentication.** On error it echoes `err.message`, which tells the caller whether a path exists. **Severity is UNMEASURED:** it depends on whether the deployed port is reachable by untrusted callers. Pre-existing, found by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #1022 (finding O1).

## Recommendation

1. **Measure the deployed exposure first.** On the VM demo (and any other deployed target), establish whether `mcp-server:4023` is reachable from outside the compose network or by any untrusted caller. **Set this ticket's priority from that measurement** (the gate: Major if reachable).
2. Then fix, for example by dropping the `filePath` branch from the HTTP mirror (it has no remote use: a remote caller has no business naming server paths), and returning a generic error message.

## Detail

**MEASURED (the QA gate, 2026-09-17, report** `2026-09-17-ks1211-1022-ff49d0242-tier1-r1`**):** `POST /hash` with `{"filePath": "<scratch file>"}` over HTTP returned **200** with the file's SHA-256.

**READ (this seat, develop** `ee40d3099`**):**

* `services/mcp-server/src/http-server.ts:41-64`:
  * `const { filePath, content } = req.body;` and, if `filePath` is set, `hashFile(filePath)`, which is `readFile(filePath)` at `src/hashing.ts:5-6`;
  * the catch at `:60-62` returns `{ error: { code: 'INTERNAL_ERROR', message: err.message } }`.
* `:29` `express.json` and `:33` `rejectNulBytes()` are the only middleware; no auth is mounted.
* A second `doc.filePath` → `hashFile` read is at `:93-94`.
* **The image runs this server:** `services/mcp-server/Dockerfile:73` is `CMD ["node", "dist/http-server.js"]`, with `EXPOSE 4023`.
* `docker-compose.yml` sets `MCP_HTTP_PORT=4023`. The host port mapping was removed (pen-test F-04; it was `"6023:4023"`), so by repo config the port is reachable **from inside the compose network**.
* **The gateway forwards only one mcp route:** `services/api-gateway/src/routes/proxy.ts:1237-1241` proxies `POST /api/mcp/generate-package` to `${MCP_SERVER_URL}/generate-package`, and no `/hash` route through the gateway was found.
* `docker/nginx-gateway/nginx{,-demo,-production}.conf`: 0 references to `mcp` or `4023` (control: 15 or 16 `proxy_pass` lines each).
* So by repo config the endpoint is internal-only. **The deployed hosts are NOT measured.** Any container on the same network, or a mis-published port, reaches it.

**Pre-existing:** the mcp-server source is identical at develop and at PR #1022's head (the gate's reading). Not introduced by the hono bump.

**Searched before filing** (Linear, team KS, title or description, archived included):

* `/hash` 12 hits;
* `filePath` 2;
* `http-server.ts` 2;
* `POST /hash` 0;
* `hashFile` 0;
* `mcp-server` 27.

The only mcp-related hits naming `/hash` are KS-713 (mcp-server scan coverage) and KS-104 (whether to expose mcp-server via the gateway), both Done and archived. Neither owns this finding; they are referenced here in text only.

title: workflow-approve persists the instance approved before the forward, so a refused forward strands it: re-approve and reject answer 400, no re-forward path, the kept document unusable until TTL (KS-1087 gate F2)
description:
## BLUF

`POST /api/workflow-instances/:id/approve` persists the instance `approved` (`services/api-gateway/src/routes/verification.ts:970-972`) BEFORE it forwards the pending document to originate. So after any refused forward the workflow is stranded:

* a retry answers 400 "Workflow already completed" and never forwards (originate hits 0);
* reject answers 400;
* there is no re-forward path;
* the kept pending document stays unusable (403 `PENDING_APPROVAL`, relayed) until its Redis TTL.

The persist-before-forward predates PR #1008. Before #1008 the same input also reached `approved` and silently deleted the pending document; #1008 (merged `f7c2f4acb28875e3665a61c8eaaad5c54bd3aa55`) keeps the document and answers 502, which makes the strand visible and recoverable in principle.

## Recommendation

A design call beside KS-1087 item 2, not a fix round on #1008. Two shapes:

* persist `approved` only after originate answers 2xx; or
* add a re-forward / retry path for an `approved` instance whose pending document still exists.

Regression test (the gate's): a stateful store, originate 401 then 201 → the second attempt forwards and deletes exactly once.

## Detail

Found by the tier-1 QA gate (round 1) on PR #1008 (Part of KS-1087, item 1) at `dd7086d5aa574285beffc515f9371a438621f25d`, 2026-09-17. Report: `Testing Agent MAIN/projects/secuura/reports/2026-09-17-ks1087-1008-dd7086d5a-tier1-r1/report.md`, Findings F2 and item 3.

**F2, verbatim from the report's findings table:** "Stranded `approved` instance. After any refused forward the instance is `approved`, re-approve/reject 400, no re-forward path, and the kept document is unusable until its TTL. The persist at `:970-972` predates #1008; base reaches the same instance state and silently loses the document."

* Evidence class: MEASURED AT RUNTIME (stateful store); the downstream 403 is RELAYED.
* Gate severity: **Major** (product state; data orphaned). Reach NOT ESTABLISHED: it depends on workflow-gated document types existing, and on KS-1087 item 2 (originate answering 401 today is relayed from the #951 r2 report).

**Measured rows (item 3):** approve with originate 401, then originate fixed to 201 and approve again, then reject.

* stateful store, head / merged / production / development: 1st approve **502**, hits 1, delete 0, pending kept, instance `approved` · 2nd approve **400 "Workflow already completed"**, hits **0** · reject **400** "…cannot be rejected" · final: instance `approved`, pending document kept, never forwarded.
* stateful store, base `93629700c`: 1st approve **200**, hits 1, **delete 1** (document lost; originate refused) · 2nd 400, hits 0 · reject 400 · final: instance `approved`, no document, pending deleted.
* stateless stub (the shape the ks1087 test uses), head: 502, then 200 + delete 1, then reject 200. The stub reads a retry path that does not exist (gate F3).
* A second approve while the first hangs: 400, originate hits 1 in total.

**Not tested (report):** the downstream 403 `PENDING_APPROVAL` on sign/anchor/share and `GET /api/documents/:id` answering `pending_approval` for a stranded document (relayed from the drafter's read); the Redis TTL value (`TTL.workflow * 24` at `redis.ts:565/603` was read, `TTL.workflow` was not); true concurrency on the final step.

Related: KS-1087 (item 2), and KS-1183 (gate F1: the forward has no timeout).

**Dedupe before filing** (seat A successor, 2026-09-17): Linear `searchIssues` with archived issues and comments included, paged, then filtered to LITERAL case-insensitive matches over title + description + comments. Positive control: `ORIGINATE_FORWARD_FAILED` found KS-1087's comment.

```
TERM 'setWorkflowInstance': scanned 0 fuzzy results over 1 page(s); literal hits 0
TERM 'Workflow already completed': scanned 118 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 0
TERM 'PENDING_APPROVAL': scanned 116 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 1
    KS-440 [Done ARCHIVED] in comments :: Pre-merge sweep ambient baseline (~180 findings) is untracked — response-schema drift + fuzz 500s ta
TERM 're-forward': scanned 127 fuzzy results over 3 page(s); literal hits 0
TERM 'deletePendingDocument': scanned 2 fuzzy results over 1 page(s); literal hits 1
    KS-1087 [In Progress] in desc :: workflow-approve deletes the pending document and answers 200 "Document has been created" without re
```

title: A push whose pre-push gate runs past ~6 min dies with rc 141 after the gate PASSED — GitHub closes the idle SSH session git opened before the hook; the launcher's core.sshCommand has no keepalive
description:
## BLUF

**A Platform K push whose pre-push gate runs longer than ~6 minutes dies with** `rc 141` **(SIGPIPE) and** `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` **— after the gate has PASSED.** git opens the SSH session to read the remote refs BEFORE the pre-push hook runs, holds it through the hook, then writes the pack; GitHub closes the idle session during a long gate, and the pack write hits a dead socket. Nothing lands, nothing is refused, and the only tell is one line above `push rc=141`. The repo's `core.sshCommand` (written by `Launch_Claude.command`) carries no keepalive, and `~/.ssh/config` has none for [github.com](<http://github.com>). Measured 2026-09-14 on three pushes from the same box through the same hook shape.

## Measured (2026-09-13/14 UTC, darwin arm64, OpenSSH default keepalives = none)

| push | branch | gate duration | outcome |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| #903 | `kamilkreiser/ks-991-stale-local-develop` | 5 min 05 s (14 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #918 | `feature/ks-926-wire-unreachable-guards` | 5 min 44 s (15 legs) | landed, rc 0 |
| #925 attempt 1 | `feature/ks-1046-preflight-passed-…` | 6 min 17 s (15 legs, stacked) | gate PASSED (`PREFLIGHT INCOMPLETE — 12/15 legs ran, 3 SKIPPED. Nothing failed.`), then `Connection to github.com closed by remote host.` — **rc 141, origin unchanged** |
| #925 attempt 2 | same head, `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` = the same key + options + `-o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` | 4 min 35 s | landed, rc 0, `push_protocol.py verify` PROTOCOL-CLEAN |

So the idle cutoff sits between ~5:45 and ~6:15 of hook time, and the gate is only growing (leg 15 landed on two branches today; the shell suites are 30). `push_protocol.py verify` on attempt 1 read the tracking ref UNCHANGED = origin — a push that touched nothing; the failure is the transport, not the tree.

## Where

* `Launch_Claude.command:130` and `:135` — the two `core.sshCommand` lines the launcher writes into `2_Project_Files/.git/config` (`ssh -i <key> -o IdentitiesOnly=yes -o StrictHostKeyChecking=accept-new`); no `ServerAliveInterval`.
* `.githooks/pre-push` → `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` — the gate whose duration crosses the cutoff.
* Records: `5_Project_History/quarantine/2026-09-14-s214/push3-ks1046/` (`push.out` line 893, `verify1.out`, `INCIDENT_sigpipe_idle_ssh.txt`, `attempt2/`).

## Fix shape

Append ` -o ServerAliveInterval=30 -o ServerAliveCountMax=20` to the launcher's `core.sshCommand` value (the launcher is the owner; the fix is carded to Kam as `secuura-launcher-ssh-keepalive`). Until it lands, a seat whose gate is long retries with the same options on `GIT_SSH_COMMAND` for that one push — never an edit to the repo's `.git/config`. A control for the fix: a push whose hook is padded past 7 minutes lands with keepalives and dies without them.

## Why it matters

The failure prints no refusal and no `To github…` line; a seat reading only the gate's verdict reports a push that never happened. The two seats that pushed today with 5-minute gates were under the cutoff by chance.

title: CI-runner environment gaps (one class, two jobs): `Security Scanning` runs `audit:contract` with no install, so `audit-locks.mjs` dies on `Cannot find package 'semver'` (7 of 59 cases red); `PR Security Gates` runs the shell suites with no build, so `ks949_main_seed_idempotence` aborts on a missing `packages/shared/dist` — the jobs' setup, not the code
description:
## BLUF

Two CI jobs run test code whose runtime prerequisites the job never installs or builds. Both reds are **environment gaps on the runner**, not defects in the code under test — each suite is green locally on a tree that has a root `node_modules` and a built `packages/shared`. Recorded here as ONE ticket because one fix pass (an install/build step per job) proves both, and because both were surfaced by the same lane on the same day. **Fixing either is a** `.github/workflows/` **edit — Kam-class; nothing here is changed by the seat that filed this.** Filed on Wednesday's ADDENDUM of 2026-09-13T21:58Z; board searched first (`packages/shared is not built` 0 hits · `npm run build -w packages/shared` 0 · `Cannot find package 'semver'` 1 — the closed ticket that gave `scripts/audit/` its own `package.json`, Done + archived · `CI-runner environment` 0 · nonsense-token control 0).

## Checklist

- [ ] **(a)** `Security Scanning` **→ job** `Dependency Audit` **→ step** `Audit-contract suites`**:** `scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` **cannot start.**
  * Evidence: PR #940's run 34426409872 / job 102712486541 / step 7 — the first run where this step printed anything (PR #940 dropped `bash -e` from that step). `ℹ tests 59 · pass 52 · fail 7`; the seven reds are every `audit-locks:` case in `scripts/audit/gate-exit-codes.test.mjs` (`:91`, `:104`, `:113`, `:180`, `:192`, `:201`, `:208`), each "got 1" where 3 / 2 / 0 was expected. The `:192` case's assertion captured the child's output verbatim: `Error [ERR_MODULE_NOT_FOUND]: Cannot find package 'semver' imported from /home/runner/work/Distributed_Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/audit-locks.mjs` (Node.js v24.20.0).
  * Mechanism: the job deliberately runs **no install** — the comment above its `npm audit` step says advisories resolve straight from the lockfile so no `npm ci` is needed. That is true for `npm audit` and false for the next step's test suite: `audit-locks.mjs:50` imports `semver`, which is declared only in `scripts/audit/package.json` (a standalone member, intentionally outside the workspaces list; its own description names exactly this failure on any tree without a root install). Locally the hoisted root `node_modules` supplies it → 59/59.
  * Not the same defect as the closed root-declaration ticket: that one added the declaration; this one is the CI job never installing it.
  * Fix shape (for whoever makes it): an install in `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/audit/` (or a root `npm ci`) before `npm run audit:contract` in that job.
- [ ] **(b)** `PR Security Gates` **→ job** `Code Security Gates` **→ step 11** `All shell test suites`**:** `packages/shared` **is never built.**
  * Evidence: develop's own push run at `8861e6216` — run 34755906436 / job 103720115281: `=== Blockchain/Dev/scripts/__tests__/ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh ===` → `FAIL — packages/shared is not built (…/Blockchain/Dev/packages/shared/dist/index.js missing) — run: npm run build -w packages/shared` → `0 passed, 1 failed (of 27 cells) — aborted`; the step's verdict `shell suites: 27 passed, 2 failed (of 29)` (the other FAILED line is `manifest_readers_agree.test.sh`, a different cause with its own Backlog ticket).
  * Mechanism: the job's setup is checkout + setup-node only — no `npm ci`, no build (PR #942's body already records the no-install half for `tsx`). The suite's own guard at `ks949_main_seed_idempotence.test.sh:113` refuses to run without `packages/shared/dist/index.js`, exactly as designed. Locally the suite is 27/27 on a built tree (the merge seat's record for the PR that shipped it).
  * Fix shape: `npm ci` + `npm run build -w packages/shared` (or the workspace build) before `bash scripts/run-shell-suites.sh` in that job — the same lesson PR #887's advisory job learned in review ("build before test").
- [ ] Re-read both jobs' logs at the fixing PR's head and confirm the two FAILED lines are gone and the counts read `59/59` and `N passed, 1 failed` (the `manifest_readers_agree` red stays until its own ticket closes).

## Attribution rule while this is open

Any PR whose CI shows these two lines is carrying develop's red, not its own: READY FOR QA mails from the CI-workflows lane attribute them to this ticket by id. Neither is absorbed into #940, #941 or #942.

Related: KS-1075 (the CI-gates config ticket whose PR #940 made (a) legible).

title: POST /api/auth/register accepts a client-supplied organizationId with no existence or membership check — impact not traced
description:
## BLUF

* `POST /api/auth/register` **lets an anonymous caller choose the organisation its new account belongs to.**
  * `registerSchema` accepts `organizationId` as any UUID (`services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:139`).
  * The handler stores it on the new user unchanged (`auth.ts:233`, `organizationId: data.organizationId`).
  * Nothing checks that the organisation exists, or that the caller has any relationship to it.
* **Impact NOT traced.** What an account carrying another organisation's id can reach has not been established. That covers the token's `organizationId`, organisation-scoped reads and the KS-597 issuer binding. Nothing was exercised on any environment.
* **Found by s189** while measuring the public account-creation path for KS-1100, on develop `4554b25e2`, which is the code kintsugi runs.

## Recommendation

* **Trace every consumer of a user's** `organizationId` **before choosing a fix.** Then either drop `organizationId` from the public register schema, or bind it to a verified invitation or membership.
* **Do not exercise it on a running environment** without explicit authorisation. Registering under another organisation's id is testing an exploit.
* **Priority High:** it sits on the organisation trust boundary Kam ruled `bind` (card `secuura-org-trust-boundary-within-tenant`, shipped in #954).

## Detail

### Code (develop `4554b25e2`)

* `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:133-142` defines `registerSchema` with `organizationId: z.string().uuid().optional()` and `.strip()`.
* `auth.ts:156` is `authRoutes.post('/register', ...)`. It is unauthenticated, and the gateway exempts it from CSRF (`services/api-gateway/src/middleware/csrf.ts:85`).
* `auth.ts:221-243` builds the new `User`:
  * the role is fixed server-side as `OWNER`, and a client-sent `role` is refused (KS-82);
  * but `organizationId: data.organizationId` comes straight from the request body.
* `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:611-672`: `createUser` writes that value to `users.organization_id`.
* **Contrast:** `POST /api/users/admin/create` requires an ORG_ADMIN or SYSTEM_ADMIN caller and pins the tenant (KS-467). The public route has no equivalent check on the organisation.

### Not established

* Which reads, grants or attributions key off `users.organization_id`, or the token's `organizationId`, for an OWNER.
* Whether any downstream check already neutralises it. One candidate is originate's KS-597 binding (`services/originate/src/routes/documents.ts:454-469`).

### Dedupe

* **Method:** a literal, case-insensitive search over KS issue titles, descriptions and all comments, archived included. Run 2026-09-12 by s189.
* **Results:**
  * `registerSchema`: 3 issues and 4 comments, across KS-283, KS-202, KS-94, KS-266, KS-255 and KS-82. All are Done and archived, and none mentions `organizationId`.
  * `organizationId: data.organizationId`: 0.
  * `register accepts organizationId`: 0.
  * `self-assign organization`: 0.
* **Controls (the instrument can hit):** `getUserByIdWithPasswordHash` found KS-732 and KS-1005; `UUID_V4_RE` found KS-663.

### Related

* KS-1100: where this was found.
* KS-597: issuer organisation attribution (option B, #954).
