title: SECURITY (local test stack): akto-autoheal runs as root with /var/run/docker.sock RW — env-scoping is only as strong as who holds the socket
description:
**BLUF —** `akto-autoheal` **runs as uid=0 root with** `/var/run/docker.sock` **mounted read-write, which grants host-equivalent read of EVERY container's environment through the daemon API and therefore defeats environment-variable scoping as a security control — but it is confined to the local Akto test harness: it sits on network** `akto_default` **rather than the platform's** `dev_secuura-network`**, and it is defined only in** `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml`**, so it does not exist on demo or kintsugi.**

The bound is in that sentence deliberately. A reader who stops after the first clause should not walk away believing this is live on a VM, and a reader who stops after the second should not walk away believing it is nothing.

## What was measured

| probe | result |
| -- | -- |
| containers with a bind mount of `/var/run/docker.sock` | **1 —** `akto-autoheal` (`willfarrell/autoheal:1.2.0`), mount **RW=true** |
| its user | `uid=0(root) gid=0(root)`, `Config.User` empty |
| tooling present inside it | `curl` **PRESENT**, `wget` **PRESENT** (no `docker` CLI, which is not a mitigation — the daemon API is HTTP over that socket) |
| its networks | `akto_default` — **not** `dev_secuura-network` |
| defining compose file | `systemTest/akto/docker-compose.yml` only |
| occurrences of `autoheal` in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` (the file the VMs run) | **0** |

**Controls, so the zeros discriminate:**

* The bind-mount scan enumerates and prints **all six** distinct bind sources across the 38 running containers (`docker/init`, `docker/init-platform`, `docker/seed`, one `secuura-api.yaml`, one `nginx-demo.conf`, `/var/run/docker.sock`) — so it can see bind mounts, and the absence of a repo-root or `.env` mount is a real null.
* The `0` for `autoheal` in the VM compose file is measured against a positive control in the same file: `originate` returns **1**. So the grep matches when the string is there.

## Why this matters beyond the container itself

**It is the general case of the specific control being shipped in KS-1041 Step 2.** That work scopes a gateway-vouch secret to exactly two of 34 containers by declaring it per-service, and verifies the scoping by probing container environments. **Any container with root + RW** `docker.sock` **can read those same environments through the daemon regardless of how narrowly they were declared** — so env-scoping is a control whose strength is bounded by who holds the socket, and nothing today records that dependency.

That is why this is filed separately rather than inside the KS-1041 PR: a finding about the estate's secret-handling as a class, buried in another ticket's PR description, is discoverable only by someone reading that PR, and it outlives the change that surfaced it.

## Explicitly NOT proposed

No fix, no privilege change, no compose edit. Changing a test stack's privileges was outside the commission this was found under and outside the current deploy grant. **Scoped and evidenced only — the remedy is a decision for whoever picks this up.**

## Provenance

Found 2026-09-10 (seat s170) while measuring the blast radius of the KS-1041 Step 2 vouch secret, at Wednesday's instruction to establish who can read it before building a control that depends on it. All readings taken read-only against the running local stack; nothing was changed.

Related: KS-1041 (the specific control this generalises).

title: No Playwright e2e test has run on any PR since 2026-09-07 — the suite dies at a static lint gate before any browser opens, and the job name hides it
description:
**BLUF — no Playwright test has executed on any PR since 2026-09-07. The** `Playwright suite` **job goes red at a static lint gate that runs BEFORE any browser opens, so the red names the wrong subject and the coverage hole has been invisible for three days.**

This is a **test-coverage** ticket, not a CI-config ticket. It was found while measuring CI gate failures (KS-1075) but must not be closed as gate tuning: the gate is a symptom, the missing e2e coverage is the defect.

## What happens

`Playwright suite` (job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml`) fails at **step 6, "Quality gate — static (tsc/ESLint/Prettier/knip/audit)"**. That step runs `npm run format:check && npm run lint && …` ahead of the suite. It exits 1, so **the job stops before a single browser test runs.**

```
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @param "label" declaration  jsdoc/require-param
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @throws declaration         jsdoc/require-throws
  27:1  error  Missing JSDoc @example declaration        jsdoc/require-example
  48:1  error  Missing JSDoc comment                     jsdoc/require-jsdoc
✖ 4 problems (4 errors, 0 warnings)
```

All four in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts`. Prettier passes cleanly — it is the ESLint jsdoc rules alone. ESLint's own output says **3 of the 4 are** `--fix`**-able**.

## Why it hid — the part worth keeping

**The job's name names the wrong subject.** "Playwright suite :: failure" reads as *browser tests ran and failed*. Nobody re-reads a suite they believe is already running. The same shape as a wrapper printing a banner it did not earn: the red was true, and what it implied was false.

## Proven pre-existing, with controls

* Measured identically on **two unrelated PRs** — #938 (one nginx `location` block, zero service code) and #939 (TypeScript type declarations in one service): same rules, same line numbers, same count.
* `global-setup.ts` is touched by **neither** — 0 hits in each diff, against controls of 4 and 3 files actually touched.
* Last changed `42e778203`, **2026-09-07**, *"KS-969 round 2: a role collapse is not a success…"* — three days before either PR.

## What needs doing

1. Fix the four jsdoc errors in `systemTest/playwright/global-setup.ts` (3 are `--fix`-able).
2. **Then confirm the suite actually runs and report what it finds** — three days of unrun e2e may be hiding real failures. A green job after the lint fix is not the same as a suite that was green all along, and it must not be reported as one.
3. Consider whether a static lint gate belongs *ahead* of the suite in the same job at all: as configured, any lint error in the harness silently converts "e2e coverage" into "no e2e coverage" while still reporting a normal-looking red.

## Related

Found during KS-1075 (CI gate measurement, commissioned by Kam as `measure-then-decide`). KS-1075 covers the two *other* gate causes — a `bash -e` swallowed diagnostic and an empty npm-audit allow-list — and should not absorb this one.

title: Per-tenant databases never receive the file migrations — CORE_MIGRATIONS FORCEs RLS with ZERO policies, so a per-tenant DB is dark on 5 core tables from boot 1 (permanent)
description:
## BLUF

**Per-tenant databases receive** `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **and NEVER the file migrations — not on any boot.** Measured, not read. The consequence is not "039 is missing": `CORE_MIGRATIONS` **enables and FORCEs** row-level security on five core tables while **every policy for them lives only in** `migrations/*.sql`, so a per-tenant DB lands with **FORCE RLS and ZERO policies**. A non-superuser runtime role then reads **zero rows** from `documents`, `certifications`, `audit_logs`, `custody_events` and `shares` — unconditionally, with no GUC able to fix it — and the boot log reports `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

**Latent today, live the moment** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB=true` — i.e. the moment KS-160 Path A (per-tenant-DB isolation) ships. This is a landmine directly under that roadmap item.

## The defect, in source

`services/api-gateway/src/startup-migrations.ts`

* **:932** `applyFileMigrations(pg, dbUrl, 'main', fileMigrations)`
* **:939** `applyFileMigrations(pg, platformDbUrl, 'platform', fileMigrations)`
* **:1108** `migrateDatabase(pg, tenantConnStr, tenantDbName, CORE_MIGRATIONS)` ← the tenant loop, **no** `applyFileMigrations` **call anywhere in it**

`applyFileMigrations`' own signature makes it structural, not an oversight in one call: `dbName: 'main' | 'platform'`. A tenant database is not a value that type admits, and the routing inside it (`if (dbName === 'main' && m.isPlatform) continue`) has no third branch.

**The trap is the split:** `CREATE POLICY` appears **0 times** in the whole of `startup-migrations.ts` (control: the same grep finds **19** in `migrations/*.sql`), while CORE_MIGRATIONS runs `ENABLE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` + `FORCE ROW LEVEL SECURITY` at :439-440 (`custody_events`), :485-486 (`shares`), :551-552 (`documents`) and a `format()` loop at :633-634. **Enforcement ships in the array; permission ships in the files. Tenant DBs get only the array.**

The second path that can seed a tenant DB does not close the gap either: `services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:62` `createTenantDatabase()` applies `INIT_SCRIPTS_DIR` (`docker/init`, bind-mounted at `docker-compose.yml:2038`) — **12 .sql files, 0** `CREATE POLICY`**, 0** `tenant_scope_bypass` (control: `migrations/` has 17 files with `CREATE POLICY`, 3 with `tenant_scope_bypass`).

## Measurement

Disposable `postgres:15-alpine`, SSL enabled with a locally-signed CA so the product's hard-coded `?sslmode=require` tenant connection could genuinely succeed. Product's own `runStartupMigrations()` driven from source; `startup-migrations.ts` blob verified **identical on** `origin/develop` **and HEAD** (`6a1b53bafa1ad707e663814f95ed92a668e96280`), `migrations/` identical too. Platform DB + main DB + one genuinely separate tenant DB (`tenant_alpha`). Four boots.

| read on `tenant_alpha` after 3 boots | value |
| -- | -- |
| public tables (**connection proof**) | **27** — `documents`, `users`, `anchor_store` all present |
| `_secuura_migrations` table exists | **0 — the file stage never ran, once** |
| `pg_policy` rows | **0** |
| tables with RLS **enabled** | **5** — all also `FORCE` |

**Same reader on the main DB (positive control):** `_secuura_migrations` **48 rows**, `039_rls_fail_closed.sql` **recorded**, `pg_policy` **28**, RLS tables **25**.

### The consequence, measured as an action (not asserted)

`secuuraadmin` is a superuser and bypasses RLS, so the owner read proves nothing. Re-measured as `s163_app` — `LOGIN NOBYPASSRLS`, non-superuser, the KS-109 runtime-role shape:

```
tenant_alpha  documents / certifications / audit_logs   ->  0 , 0 , 0
tenant_alpha  documents WITH both GUCs the product sets ->  0    (no policy exists to satisfy)
tenant_alpha  organizations (non-RLS table, 1 row)      ->  1    <- NON-ZERO CONTROL: login + grants work
superuser, row_security=off, tenant_alpha documents     ->  1    <- the row DOES exist
secuura       documents, NO GUC set                     ->  0
secuura       documents WITH app.tenant_scope_bypass    ->  1    <- DISCRIMINATION CONTROL
secuura       documents WITH app.current_tenant_id      ->  1
```

The zeros on `tenant_alpha` are real zeros, not an unreachable database: the same role, in the same database, reads 1 from a non-RLS table.

## Scope — honest in both directions

**REFUTED for the configuration running today.** `PROVISION_PER_TENANT_DB` defaults false (`services/tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:245`), so every `tenant_config` row points at the shared app DB — which *does* get the file migrations via the `'main'` path. Confirmed in my own run: the 6 seeded tenants all carried `db_name = secuura`. **5 occurrences of the flag repo-wide, all code/comment, ZERO config sites** (control: `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED` appears in `docker-compose.yml`).

⚠ **NOT measured against demo or UAT** — both are held. The above is source + a local reproduction.

**CONFIRMED for per-tenant DBs.** Set the flag — or provision any tenant whose `db_name` differs from the app DB — and that tenant is dark on its five core tables from its first boot, permanently, with a success line in the log.

## Fix shape (not implemented here)

Give `applyFileMigrations` a tenant arm and call it from the loop before `migrateDatabase`, with the file corpus filtered the way `'main'` filters it. The `'main' | 'platform'` union is the thing to widen — an omission should stop compiling rather than be remembered. Any fix must also address the **ordering** KS-1054 documents (039 needs tables CORE creates), or a tenant DB simply reproduces the boot-1 window instead of the permanent one.

## Provenance

QA gate finding **F-928-3**, read-from-source and explicitly UNMEASURED, carried inside KS-1054. Measured here by s163 on 2026-09-09, local disposable containers only, removed at close. Demo, UAT and every shared database untouched.

---

## TLS: the tenant connection is VERIFY-FULL, and that is what makes F-928-4's counter load-bearing

**The product hard-codes** `?sslmode=require` **on the tenant connection string** (`startup-migrations.ts:1105`), and `pg-connection-string` **2.12.0 treats** `require` **as** `verify-full` — it says so itself at runtime: *"The SSL modes 'prefer', 'require', and 'verify-ca' are treated as aliases for 'verify-full'."* So the tenant loop does not merely want TLS; it requires a **CA-verifiable certificate chain and a matching hostname**.

**Proved both ways before any of the measurement above was trusted**, against the same container and the same connection-string shape:

```
no trusted CA   ->  "unable to verify the first certificate"
trusted CA      ->  connected, current_database() = tenant_alpha
```

That is why this ticket's zeros mean something: had I not stood the CA up, the tenant DB would have been unreachable and I would have measured my own container instead of the product.

**The consequence on a real deployment:** on any deployment whose tenant database does not present a CA-verifiable certificate, **the tenant loop connects to nothing at all** — and because of the counter defect below, the boot still logs `{migrated: N, skipped: 0}`.

### F-928-4 — the counter cannot report a failure under any condition (measured)

Registered a tenant pointing at `tenant_does_not_exist` — **proved absent** in `pg_database`, **proved present** in the loop's own `SELECT` — and booted:

```
[INFO] Tenant DB migrations complete {"migrated":8,"skipped":0,"total":8}
```

**Mechanism, to the line:** `migrateDatabase` (`startup-migrations.ts:800`) swallows every per-statement error in its own inner `try/catch` and returns `applied`, so it **never throws**, so the tenant loop's `catch` arm at `:1112` is **dead code**. And `new pg.Pool()` does not connect eagerly, so even total connection failure surfaces inside `pool.query` and is swallowed with the rest. `migrated++` therefore counts a tenant whose database does not exist.

### These three legs are ONE path, which is why they are on one ticket

**Tenant provisioning is broken and nothing reports it:**

1. a per-tenant DB arrives **deny-all** on five core tables (the body of this ticket),
2. it **cannot be connected to at all** without a CA-verifiable cert,
3. and the boot **reports success under every one of those failures**.

Filed together deliberately — as three separate tickets each one looks survivable on its own.

title: develop is RED on the services/originate jest suite and NOTHING catches it — the suite is a blocking gate nowhere automated
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **is RED on the** `services/originate` **jest suite right now, and no instrument in this repository objects.** Measured tonight: 2 of 4 cells in `ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts` fail on develop's own blob. **The suite is a blocking gate NOWHERE automated**, so the mainline can be red indefinitely and nothing says so.

Filed on Wednesday's ruling as a **new** ticket rather than folded into KS-961, because KS-961 is In Review and adding scope to an in-review ticket either reopens reviewed work or buries the new scope under a review that never covered it.

## The measurement

```
npx jest src/__tests__/ks444-webhooks-create-description-guard.test.ts   (in services/originate)
  2 passed   the two NEGATIVE cells (400s an object, 400s a null)
  2 FAILED   both POSITIVES - expected 201, received 500
  EXIT=1
```

Run on blobs verified byte-identical to develop: the test file is `229a3ccde` at both `origin/develop` and `b6884888d`; `routes/webhooks.ts` is `c88eb97db` at both. **PR #926 is the fix and it is open and unmerged**, blocked on an approval.

**Scope of the redness, which the QA gate did not measure:** the full service run is **48 suites / 509 tests, 1 suite / 2 tests failed** — the ks444 positives are the *only* failures in the whole service. ⚠ That run covers **48 of develop's 49** originate suites: it was executed on a tree missing `ks754-processed-by-widened.test.ts`, which is **unswept and named rather than rounded away**.

## Why nothing catches it — four instruments, each checked with a control

| instrument | originate/jest | control on the same file |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `scripts/preflight/preflight.sh` (13 legs, 428 lines) | **0 hits** | `step` -> 18 hits |
| `.githooks/pre-push` (244 lines) | **0 hits** | `preflight` -> 18 hits |
| 17 GitHub workflows | only `ci.yml` + `deploy-demo.yml` invoke workspace tests, **both** `workflow_dispatch`**-only** | 17 mention `test` |
| the 7 `pull_request`-triggered workflows | **none runs any service unit suite** | read their `run:` steps individually |

**This conclusion does not depend on the Actions billing state.** Even with Actions fully funded, no PR-triggered workflow invokes this suite. Actions being retired (Kam, 2026-08-27) is a second, independent reason.

## The actual gap

**The only instrument that would ever catch a red mainline is a human filling in a Test Evidence line — and it only fires if a PR happens to touch that service.** `docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` requires `**Unit suites (touched services):** run/result | not run + why`. A suite that is red on develop and untouched by the current PR is invisible to that, by construction.

## The precedent that makes this concrete

`DEV-PROCESS.md` **has already made this exact argument once, for a different subject, and acted on it.** Cross-cutting guards get their own Test Evidence line specifically because, under "run `npm test` in the touched service", they *"execute only when someone touches* `shared`*, which is the change least likely to add a fifteenth service error handler"* — and it concludes **"A guard on no path that runs is not a guard."**

**The same argument applies to a red mainline suite, and nothing currently makes it.**

## Fix shapes (not a ruling - the cheapest is probably the third)

1. A preflight leg that runs the touched service's unit suite, so a red mainline blocks the next push that goes near it.
2. A periodic mainline run whose only job is to answer "is develop green" - no PR coupling.
3. A **baseline-diff** rule in the Test Evidence block: the author records develop's own result for the suites they ran, so "2 failed" is visibly pre-existing rather than silently attributed to the change. This is the same shape KS-660 already applies to Schemathesis ("the failing SET ... + its diff vs the develop baseline set, never a bare count").

## Related

* **KS-961** - the aggregate workspace suite never runs on a PR. Adjacent, In Review, deliberately not extended.
* **KS-1046** - `PREFLIGHT PASSED` printed identically whether 13 legs ran or 10. Same family: a claim whose check did not run.
* **KS-927 / PR #926** - the fix for the red itself.

## Ask

**Kam or Wednesday to pick a fix shape** (or rule that the red simply waits for #926 and no instrument changes). Nothing here is urgent in the sense of a live outage - it is urgent in the sense that the next person to read a green board about `originate` will be reading a false one.

*Filed by s162 (Platform K), 2026-09-09, on Wednesday's ruling. Measurement is mine and reproducible from the commands above.*

title: No independent liveness signal for our own VMs — kintsugi was dead for 53 h and Azure health read `Available` the whole time
description:
## BLUF

`secuura02-kintsugi-vm` **was down for 53 hours and nothing told us. The first signal was Stuart's tooling — a person, not a monitor. And Azure's own platform health read** `Available` **for the whole 53 hours, which is why the one alerting surface we do have would not have fired either.**

Both halves are one logical path — *we have no independent liveness signal for our own VMs* — so they are one ticket per Kam's 2026-09-06 aggregation rule, not two.

## What happened

* Azure live-migrated the VM at **2026-09-07T03:56:13Z** (`PlatformInitiated`, *"paused 0.993s, memory-preserving"*). The guest did not survive it.
* The workload died at ~**04:00Z**. On-disk logs **stop at 03:55:01Z** with **zero** entries for 53 h (control: **53** entries in the same hour).
* It came back only because a person went looking on **2026-09-09**, and was force-reset at **09:31:45Z**.

## Half 1 — no liveness signal

Nothing watches whether kintsugi is serving. There is no uptime check, no synthetic request, no alert on absence of logs. Detection was **incidental**.

⚠ This is the same shape as **KS-670** (demo's on-chain verification down **6 days**, found by a person). Two incidents, same missing control. That is the argument for fixing the class rather than the instance.

## Half 2 — the alerting surface we DO have was lying

Azure marked the box **Available at 03:59:30Z** and said *"no additional action is required"* — while the guest was dead and stayed dead for 53 hours. `memory-preserving` migration means **no reboot**, so Caddy survived in memory and kept answering at the edge while sshd, the guest agent and dockerd were all gone.

**So a health check that trusts either Azure resource health OR a naive port-200 on the front door would have reported green throughout.** Any monitor built here has to make a request that actually traverses the app, and has to alert on **silence** (no logs / no successful synthetic) rather than on an error, because a dead guest produces no errors at all — it produces nothing.

## Why this is due now

The incident record is closed (`5_Project_History/HANDOVER-kintsugi-outage-CLOSED.md`). **Recurrence is not** — Azure live-migrates this box as routine platform behaviour and the guest does not survive one. Boot diagnostics / serial console is now **ENABLED**, so a repeat leaves evidence; nothing currently tells us the repeat *happened*.

## Suggested shape (not a decision — the approach is open)

1. An external liveness check per VM (demo + kintsugi) that traverses the app, not just the edge — the front door answered while the box was dead.
2. Alert on **absence** — no successful synthetic in N minutes, or no new log lines — not on error responses.
3. Do **not** key anything off Azure resource health alone. This incident is the counter-example, in our own record.

## What is NOT established

* Whether the demo VM has the same exposure — **not measured**; it is the same subscription and region and probably does, but I did not check.
* The remount-read-only theory for the guest's death is **strongly supported, not proven**: no kernel message survived, because it could not be written to the disk it was about.

## Provenance

Azure activity log (read in slices — the API truncates silently at 50), the guest's own journal, `df` 37% and a clean `fsck` refuting ENOSPC and corruption from inside. Recorded by s160, filed by s161.

title: tests/e2e auth-exhaustive races its OWN lockout — same commit gives 1 or 11 failures, so the suite cannot gate anything
description:
## BLUF

`tests/e2e/tests/auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` **is non-deterministic against an unchanged product.** It brute-forces logins, `playwright.config.ts` sets `fullyParallel: true`, and every run leaves **4** `lockout:*` **keys** in redis — so its own ordinary login cells race its own lockout. Until this is fixed the suite cannot be used as a gate, because a failure count carries no information.

## Measured — 2026-09-09, `develop` `b6884888d`, `lockout:*` cleared before EACH run

| run | command | result |
| -- | -- | -- |
| A | three specs | **23 failed / 54 passed** |
| B | three specs | **11 failed / 71 passed** |
| C | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **1 failed / 52 passed** |
| D | `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts` alone | **11 failed / 42 passed** |

**Nothing about the product changed between any of them.** Lockout keys were counted after every run: 4 each time, so the suite reliably creates them and unreliably outruns them.

**The flapping cells move as ONE block** — both 23-failure runs carried exactly the same 23, which is what rules out twelve independent flakes and points at a single shared cause. They are all in `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts`: 2.1.1–2.1.5, 2.2.8, 2.2.9, 2.8.1, 2.9.1, 2.9.2, 2.9.4, 2.9.5.

**The deterministic remainder is 10 recruitment/wallet cells** (red in 5 of 5 runs) plus `auth-exhaustive.spec.ts:734`, whose assertion is wrong rather than the app — filed separately.

## Suggested fix (not prescribed)

Either serialise this file (`test.describe.configure({ mode: 'serial' })` or a dedicated non-parallel project), or give the brute-force cells a **dedicated account** so they cannot lock the fixture persona the rest of the file logs in with. The second is likely better: it keeps the parallelism and removes the coupling.

## Class

This is the **KS-724** family — a harness that stops testing while still producing results. There, a scan evicted its own bearer; here, a suite locks out its own persona.

## Provenance

* the four runs, lockout counts, and the identical 23-cell block | measured live on the local stack, recorded in `Blockchain/Dev/tests/e2e/BASELINE.md` | 2026-09-09
* Filed from KS-734's baseline work (s160), which made the suite installable and could then measure it.

title: Reshape the advisory gate: it is NON-DETERMINISTIC on an unchanged tree — 8 advisories in 30 min, one appeared then vanished. Warn-then-fail, keyed on REACH and SEVERITY (window length is Kam's)
description:
## BLUF

**The advisory gate is NON-DETERMINISTIC ON AN UNCHANGED TREE.** Two runs of the same commit, minutes apart, give different verdicts — because it hard-fails on a dataset that a third party edits continuously and we do not control.

**That is a correctness problem, not a throughput one.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot distinguish *"this commit is unsafe"* from *"you ran it at the wrong minute"*.

**Kam ruled the reshape on 2026-09-09 (**`both`**): warn for a window, then hard-fail. The WINDOW LENGTH is explicitly reserved for him and is an open question at the foot of this ticket — it is not proposed here as a number.**

⚠ **And the design must be REACH- AND SEVERITY-AWARE, or it weakens the gate in the one case it exists for.** Detail in *The design constraint* below.

## The evidence — measured across three runs in about half an hour, 2026-09-09

```
run 1  ~21:4x   audit-locks  31 advisories match, 29 baselined   ->  2 missing
run 2  ~22:0x   audit-locks  32 advisories match, 31 baselined   ->  1 missing
run 3  ~22:15   audit-gate   37 reported,         34 baselined   ->  5 missing
```

**The arithmetic is closed, which is what makes this a measurement rather than an impression.** Between runs 1 and 2 exactly **two** baseline rows were added — 29 + 2 = 31, so the *baselined* count is fully explained. **The MATCH count still moved 31 → 32.** Nothing in the repo's dependencies changed: one JSON file was edited, touching zero `package.json` and zero lockfiles.

**Eight distinct advisories touched this repo in half an hour. Three were baselined. The gap widened while it was being closed.**

### 🔴 And one went the OTHER way — this is the part that makes it non-determinism

Between runs 2 and 3, `GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv` (colord) **stopped being reported by the root gate entirely**. Its own output:

```
CLEANUP (advisory): 1 baseline entry is no longer reported — remove:
  - GHSA-2wm5-q62r-hmrv (colord, KS-1024)
```

**An advisory that blocked every push fifteen minutes earlier was no longer reported at all** — with no change on our side. **The dataset does not only grow. It churns.**

## Why the obvious fix is a trap

Baselining the current five turns the preflight green **now**. Run 3 proves that says nothing about run 4. **A green preflight after a triage round is evidence that the external set was quiet for one run, not that the tree is clean** — and the same three runs above show how long "quiet" lasts.

**Triage cannot outrun publication.** That is the loop this ticket exists to break.

## ⚠ The design constraint — a FLAT window would weaken the gate

Written flat, *"warn for a window, then hard-fail"* lets a **production-reaching** advisory sit unblocked for the whole window.

**That is not hypothetical, and the counter-example arrived the same morning the option was drafted:** `GHSA-8m3c-c648-2xjj` — nodemailer's `resolveContent()` bypassing `disableFileAccess`/`disableUrlAccess` on the legacy signature — is a **production dependency of** `services/auth` **and** `services/originate`, the two services that send mail. It survives `npm ci --omit=dev` and reaches a runtime image. **A flat window would have left that unblocked.**

**So the window must key on the same discriminator that has decided every one of these triages:**

| class | behaviour |
| -- | -- |
| measured NOT to reach a shipped tree, **and** moderate or below | **WARN** for the window, do not block |
| reaches a shipped tree | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |
| **HIGH or CRITICAL**, wherever it lives | **HARD-FAIL immediately**, no window |

**This preserves the property Kam wants — nobody blocked for changing nothing — without buying it with the property the gate exists for.** It is deliberately the same test as the standing authority's own clauses: *what does this reach* is the only question that discriminated all morning.

**A necessary consequence, stated so it is designed rather than discovered:** the warn path needs the reach measurement to be **automatic**. Today it is done by hand, per advisory, by whoever is blocked. A gate that warns-or-fails on reach must derive reach itself, or the window just moves the manual step earlier.

## 🔴 OPEN QUESTION FOR KAM — the window length

**He ruled the shape, not the number, and it is not being chosen here.**

Recommendation offered as a recommendation only: long enough that a normal working day is not interrupted by a third party's publishing schedule, short enough that a warn cannot be ignored into permanence. **The data point this ticket can contribute is that eight advisories arrived in half an hour, so any window shorter than that is indistinguishable from no window at all.**

## What is NOT claimed

* **No root cause for the churn.** Whether the 31→32→37 movement is newly-published advisories, a registry re-index, or an `npm audit` dataset refresh is **NOT measured**. The *effect* is measured; the mechanism is not, and the reshape does not depend on which it is.
* **Whether we actually call the vulnerable nodemailer signature** — see the linked note; unmeasured at filing.
* **No claim that any current advisory is exploitable here.** Reachability has not been measured for any of them; that has been true of this baseline since KS-470.

## Provenance

Measured by s154, 2026-09-09, on `develop` `f9296f9e` while blocked from pushing KS-754 — the three runs are its own, and the arithmetic was closed before the conclusion was drawn. Ruled by Kam 2026-09-09 08:12 (`both`), confirmed *"Okay, go ahead with your recommendation."* The reach/severity split is Wednesday's design constraint. Related: KS-1024 (the triage that produced this), KS-470, KS-531.

title: The `require-pr-gates` ruleset survived the Actions retirement: 7 required checks that can never report, 0 required approvals, and ALWAYS bypass for admins
description:
## BLUF

`develop` **and** `main` **carry an ACTIVE ruleset that enforces nothing for an admin and is unsatisfiable for everyone else.** It requires seven status-check contexts whose workflows no longer exist, requires **zero** approving reviews, and grants `ALWAYS` bypass to org and repo admins.

The retirement of Actions is well tracked ([KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify), [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql)). **What is not tracked is the ruleset left pointing at it.** A branch that looks protected in the settings UI, and in the API reports `mergeStateStatus: CLEAN` on a PR with no reviews and no checks, is worse than one that is plainly unprotected — the reassurance is the problem.

Found while reviewing [Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), after asking the ordinary question "could this merge without an approval?". It can.

## What the ruleset actually says

`require-pr-gates` — `target: BRANCH`, `enforcement: ACTIVE`, conditions `refs/heads/develop` + `refs/heads/main`.

| rule | setting |
| -- | -- |
| `PULL_REQUEST` | required |
| — `requiredApprovingReviewCount` | **0** |
| — `requireCodeOwnerReview` | false |
| — `requireLastPushApproval` | false |
| — `requiredReviewThreadResolution` | false |
| — `dismissStaleReviewsOnPush` | false |
| `REQUIRED_STATUS_CHECKS` | 7 contexts (below) |
| — `strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy` | false |
| `DELETION` / `NON_FAST_FORWARD` | both on — these two DO work |

Required contexts: `Code Security Gates` · `Standalone locks pass clean-room npm ci` · `build / Build + push platform images (fresh)` · `Schemathesis suite` · `Playwright suite` · `Performance suite (k6 smoke)` · `Akto suite (PR)`.

Bypass actors, **both** `bypassMode: ALWAYS`: organization admins, and repository role `5` (admin).

## The three problems, separately

**1 — Seven required checks that can never report.** Every recent workflow run is `startup_failure` at **0s** (`gh run list`). The workflows producing these contexts were retired. So for a contributor without admin the ruleset is not strict, it is **unsatisfiable** — nothing they push can ever go green, and the failure reads as "waiting for a check" rather than "this check no longer exists".

**2 — Zero required approvals.** A PR is required; an approval is not. On `main` as well as `develop`, which is the part I would not have guessed. `main` is meant to be the releasable branch (CLAUDE.md → Branching Model), and it currently asks for no human sign-off at all.

**3 —** `ALWAYS` **bypass for admins hides both.** Anyone who could notice problems 1 and 2 is exactly the population the ruleset never applies to. GitHub computes `mergeStateStatus` for the viewer, so an admin sees `CLEAN` and no warning of any kind.

## The demonstration

[Secuura/Distributed_Secuura#805](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-726-write-ahead-the-cardano-tx-hash-so-a-lost-submit-reply-cannot-48dbfe970108), read 2026-09-08:

```
mergeable:         MERGEABLE
mergeStateStatus:  CLEAN
reviewDecision:    null      (no reviews of ANY kind ever submitted)
statusCheckRollup: 0 checks
```

Mergeable right now, by any admin, with no approval and no green check — and nothing on the PR page says so. That PR happens to be under active review, so no harm is in flight; it is the state that is the finding, not the PR.

## Reproduce

```
gh api graphql -f query='{ repository(owner:"Secuura", name:"Distributed_Secuura") {
  rulesets(first:5){ nodes{ name target enforcement
    conditions{ refName{ include exclude } }
    bypassActors(first:20){ nodes{ bypassMode organizationAdmin repositoryRoleDatabaseId } }
    rules(first:30){ nodes{ type parameters{ __typename
      ... on PullRequestParameters { requiredApprovingReviewCount requireCodeOwnerReview requireLastPushApproval requiredReviewThreadResolution dismissStaleReviewsOnPush }
      ... on RequiredStatusChecksParameters { strictRequiredStatusChecksPolicy requiredStatusChecks{ context } } } } } } } }'
```

Note the REST endpoints (`/branches/develop/protection`, `/rulesets`) answer **403 "Upgrade to GitHub Pro"** on this private repo, which is why this is easy to miss — the obvious check reports nothing rather than reporting the truth. GraphQL answers fine.

## Suggested shape — not a decree, and deliberately not one change

These are three decisions, not one, and they belong to different owners:

1. **Drop the seven dead contexts** from the ruleset, or repoint them at whatever replaced Actions. Leaving a required check that cannot report is the worst of the three states. *(Cheap; no policy decision.)*
2. **Decide the approval count deliberately**, for `main` and `develop` separately. If 0 is intended on a 4-seat team, say so in CONTRIBUTING and this ticket closes on that; if it is a leftover, 1 on `develop` and 1 on `main` is the obvious floor.
3. **Reconsider** `ALWAYS` **bypass.** `pull_request` mode instead of `ALWAYS` keeps admins able to unblock an emergency while still surfacing the state to them.

**(1) is worth doing regardless of how (2) and (3) land.**

## Relationship to what is already tracked

* [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) (Todo, High, Peter) — *"require all systemTest PR suites + pre-merge to block merges on failure (branch protection + sign-off)"*. Points **forward** to the gate we want. This ticket is the **residue behind us**: the ruleset that already exists and no longer means anything. They should probably be sequenced — clean this up, then build [KS-412](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-412/ci-require-all-systemtest-all-tools-pr-suites-pre-merge-to-block) on the cleared ground.
* [KS-789](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-789/contributingmd-justifies-the-hooks-degradation-and-its-no-verify) — CONTRIBUTING justifies the hook's `--no-verify` bypass with *"CI is the hard gate"*. This is the same sentence, one layer down: the ruleset also asserts a gate that is not there.
* [KS-910](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-910/preflight-leg-12-executes-zero-suite-cells-it-is-a-reachability-check), [KS-926](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-926/17-of-20-check-sh-guards-run-from-no-live-entry-point-including-sql) — the Actions retirement itself and its orphaned guards. Cause; this is effect.

## Not claimed

I have not checked whether any merge to `develop` or `main` has actually gone in unreviewed — only that nothing prevents it. Nor have I touched the ruleset; changing it needs org-admin rights and is a decision, not a fix.

*Raised by Peter's session, 2026-09-08, from the #805 review. Read via GraphQL against the live repo, not from documentation.*

title: 95 archived tickets sit in NON-TERMINAL states — measure whether a cascade put them there
description:
## BLUF

**97 archived tickets on the KS+PS boards are in non-terminal states.** Two were archived today (mine, restored the same session). **The other 95 predate this session and nobody has established how they got there.**

```
Backlog     83
Todo         6
In Progress  4
In Review    3
Blocked      1
```

**This is a hypothesis with evidence, NOT an asserted cause.** [KS-995](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-995) established that `issueArchive` cascades onto sub-issues — including non-terminal ones — and that the parent-side check reads clean afterwards. **That mechanism would produce exactly this population, silently.** It may also be that some were archived deliberately.

## The measurement that would settle it

For each of the 95: **is its parent archived, and does the parent's** `archivedAt` **match the child's to the millisecond?**

That is the same discriminator that disproved a wrong third-party attribution during today's pass, applied backwards:

* **match → decisive for cascade.** One batch, one cause.
* **mismatch → closes nothing.** It was archived separately, which is consistent with a deliberate act.

One-directional, and that limit should be carried into whatever the measurement concludes — a mismatch is not evidence of intent.

## 🔴 Do NOT unarchive anything on the strength of this ticket

**83 tickets reappearing in Backlog changes what the team sees.** A restoration is as much a board change as an archive, and it is Kam's call on a measurement — not a tidy-up. **Measure first, report, then ask.**

## Items

- [ ] **1. Run the parent/timestamp measurement** across all 95 and report the split.
- [ ] **2. For any confirmed cascade victim, establish whether the work is still live** — an In Progress ticket archived by accident is different from a Backlog item nobody was going to do.
- [ ] **3. Only then** put a restoration proposal to Kam, with counts by state.

## Why it matters beyond tidiness

Every count taken with a default query has been wrong on this board today — *twice*. `Tested Not Deployed` read 24 when it was 29, and a Duplicate census read 4 when it was 5 because the query capped at 250. **If 95 live-state tickets are invisible, every "what is open" number anyone has quoted is short by some part of 95.**

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, alongside KS-995.

title: Archiving a ticket silently archives its sub-issues, including NON-TERMINAL ones — and the parent-side check cannot detect it
description:
## BLUF

`issueArchive` **cascades to sub-issues.** Archiving 23 terminal tickets on 2026-09-08 also archived **KS-918 (Backlog)** and **KS-920 (In Progress)** — children of **KS-490**. Neither was in any target list. **In Progress is live work.**

**And the obvious verification cannot catch it:** once archived, the parent's `children` connection returns **nothing**. Asking the parent what it took with it reads clean.

Both were restored the same session. This ticket is about the mechanism, which is still live.

## Measured

```
child -> parent    KS-918.parent = KS-490      ✅ reveals the link
                   KS-920.parent = KS-490      ✅
parent -> children KS-490.children = 0         ❌ shows NOTHING
```

**The timestamps are what identified it as a cascade rather than a concurrent actor:**

```
KS-490  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-921  (mine, targeted)      archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z
KS-918  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
KS-920  (NOT targeted)        archivedAt 2026-09-08T00:41:09.467Z   <- identical ms
```

Identical to the millisecond = one batch = one cause. **My own first diagnosis blamed a concurrent actor and was wrong; the timestamp disproved it.**

**Full accounting for the pass:** 33 intended + 2 collateral = 35 archived, measured 35. Only KS-490 had children, so the blast radius was bounded at exactly two.

## Why it went unnoticed until arithmetic caught it

The only reason anyone knows is the **census delta: −25 against an expected −23**. That is the shape most easily rationalised as a stale count. Every other signal looked clean:

* the archive calls all returned `success: true` — and they had, for the 23 asked;
* the parent-side `children` query returned **0**;
* no error, no warning, nothing in any response mentioning the children.

## The rule this produces

**Before archiving, query** `child → parent` **for the target's children and record the count. After, take a full paged census.**

```
expected delta = |targets| + |children found|
```

**If the delta is not exactly that, stop.** Asking the parent side for `children` is *the check that cannot fail* here — it reads zero both when there are none and when they have just been archived.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Make the children pre-check part of any archive procedure**, with the delta equation above as its pass condition.
- [ ] **2. Decide whether a cascade onto a NON-TERMINAL child should be refused outright.** Kam's standing ruling is that non-terminal work stays visible on the board; a cascade violates that silently.
- [ ] **3. Measure the historical population — see the sibling ticket** on the 95 pre-existing archived non-terminal tickets. This mechanism would produce exactly that.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the archive pass that hit it.

title: A deploy that rsyncs the OpenAPI spec and does not restart api-gateway ships a silently stale published contract — rsync breaks the bind mount by inode
description:
## BLUF

**The demo redeploy runbook can ship a stale published API contract with every check passing.** `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` is a **file-level** bind mount into `api-gateway` (`docker-compose.yml:542`, `:ro`). `rsync` **writes a temp file and renames it, so the updated file gets a NEW INODE** — and a Docker file bind mount resolves to the inode at container-create time. The container goes on serving the **old** file indefinitely.

It is not stale cache. The container is looking at a **different file on the same path**.

## Measured during the 2026-09-08 deploy (632f16dfe → 400517aaf)

After the rsync, before any restart:

|  | md5 | bytes |
| -- | -- | -- |
| host `docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `7e43a8d89afb…` | 1332983 (new) |
| inside `api-gateway` `/app/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` | `c014b2fce71c…` | 1329831 (**old**, dated Sep 7 03:45) |
| served `GET /api/docs/openapi.yaml` | — | 1329831 = the container's copy |

After `docker compose restart api-gateway`: container md5 `7e43a8d89afb…`, identical to the host; served bytes 1332983; the new text `BOUND TO THE` went **0 → 1** and `DIFFERS FROM the ACTING` **0 → 2**, with `organizationUuid` **1 → 2** as a control and an impossible string at 0.

## Why this is worth a ticket rather than a note

**The failure mode is exactly KS-978's**, which this same deploy shipped the fix for: *the published contract says something the route does not do*. KS-978 was a wrong sentence in the source. This is the **delivery mechanism** producing the same outcome from a correct source — and it is quieter, because every signal an operator would check looks right:

* `rsync` exits 0 and reports the file transferred ✅
* the file on the VM disk **is** correct ✅
* rebuilding the image does nothing (the spec is mounted, not baked) — so "I rebuilt it" feels like the fix and is not ✅
* the container is healthy, the endpoint returns 200 ✅

Nothing surfaces the divergence except comparing the md5 **inside** the container against the host.

## Items

- [ ] **1. Add the gateway restart to the runbook as a required step**, not an optional one — `Blockchain/Dev/deployment/DEPLOYMENT-ARCHITECTURE.md` §Redeploy runbook. Wording should carry the mechanism (inode), because "restart to pick up the spec" reads as cargo-cult and gets dropped.
- [ ] **2. Correct the existing guidance.** The current understanding recorded in project notes is "a rebuild does not publish it, a restart does" — true but incomplete, and it does not say the container will serve the old file *forever* until something re-resolves the mount.
- [ ] **3. Add a post-deploy assertion** that fails loudly: compare `md5sum` of the host spec against `docker exec api-gateway md5sum` of the mounted path, and refuse to call a deploy complete when they differ. This is the check that would have caught it with no human judgement involved.
- [ ] **4. Audit for other file-level bind mounts with the same exposure** — `nginx-demo.conf` is the known sibling. Directory mounts are not affected; only single-file mounts are.

## Not a live defect right now

The 2026-09-08 deploy restarted `api-gateway` and the served spec is verified correct. This ticket is about the **next** deploy, by whoever does not know.

Filed by s149, 2026-09-08, from the deploy itself.

title: Neither credential guard can see a value in a .env.example — one scans the wrong roots and extensions, the other excludes the file and self-tests the exclusion
description:
**Two credential guards run on every push and NEITHER could see the one that mattered.** KS-966 F1 was a live exposure — `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` shipped a value for `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, and `docs/DEPLOYMENT.md:381` plus `services/api-gateway/src/docs/developer-portal.html:382` both instruct `cp .env.example .env`, so the documented setup path seeded the platform SYSTEM_ADMIN **ACTIVE and loginable** on a credential published in this repository. It sat there through a full round-1 gate.

**This is the guards' blind AXIS, not a bug in either implementation, and it was not introduced by #888.** Both behave exactly as written. That is the problem.

### Measured, from the scripts themselves

**1.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh:28-32` — cannot reach the file on two independent axes:

```
grep -rEn --include='*.ts' --include='*.tsx' --include='*.js' \
     --exclude-dir=__tests__ --exclude-dir=tests --exclude-dir=scripts \
     ... services/ packages/
```

* **Extension:** `.ts` / `.tsx` / `.js` only. A `.env.example` is not scannable by construction.
* **Root:** `services/` and `packages/` only. `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` is above both.

Either one alone is sufficient to miss it. Widening one and not the other changes nothing.

**2.** `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/preflight/no-tracked-credentials.sh:37-38` — excludes it *deliberately*:

```
EXCLUDE_RE='\.(example|sample|template)$'
```

with the comment at `:34-36` explaining that 25 `.env.example` files are tracked on purpose and are the documented way to describe required config. **And its own self-test at** `:51-53` **asserts the exclusion holds**, naming `Blockchain/Dev/.env.example` as a probe that MUST be excluded:

```
for probe in "Blockchain/Dev/.env.example" "svc/config.example"; do
  echo "$probe" | grep -Eq "$EXCLUDE_RE" || { echo "SELF-TEST FAIL: did not exclude $probe"; ok=1; }
done
```

So the guard is not merely blind here — **it is tested to be blind here.** Any fix has to change that self-test too, consciously, or it will be reverted by the next person who reads it as a regression.

### Why the exclusion is right and still leaves a hole

The exclusion exists for a good reason: an example file must be allowed to *name* `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD`, or it cannot document the variable at all. **The distinction the guards do not draw is between naming a key and assigning it a value.** `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=` is documentation. `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD=<something>` is a credential. A file-level exclusion cannot tell those apart; a line-level rule can.

### Shape when picked up

A check over tracked `*.env.example` files that fails on **a non-empty assignment to a credential-shaped key**, rather than on the file's existence. Keys named, not pattern-guessed — the pattern-guessing is what produces the false positives the current exclusion was written to avoid.

### Interim cover — real but partial, and it must not be mistaken for this ticket being done

#888 round 2 adds a cell (`services/auth/src/__tests__/ks949-platform-admin-seed-identity.test.ts`, the `KS-966 F1` block) that walks the tree for `*.env.example` and fails on a non-empty `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` / `TEST_ADMIN_PASSWORD`. It is red-proved (restoring a value gives 2 red of 23 executing).

**It covers two key names in one service's test suite.** It is not a push-time gate, it does not run when only non-auth code changes, and it says nothing about any other credential-shaped key. The gap this ticket names is the guards' coverage axis, and that is still open.

title: The default-password CI gate catches one shape and calls it clean — 16 published passwords are exempt by design, and 4 of 5 canaries walk past it
description:
## The finding

`Blockchain/Dev/scripts/check-no-default-passwords.sh` is a **live CI gate** (`pr-security-gates.yml:63`, `security-scan.yml:422`). It is far blinder than its name suggests, and the documented exemption is the *small* half.

## The exemption (known, by design)

Line 34 is `| grep -v 'seedPw(' \`. With **only that line deleted** (sha-asserted both ways and restored), the lint exits 1 with **16 flagged lines — sixteen other seeded accounts' published default passwords**, invisible to it by design.

## The blind spots (not by design)

Five canaries planted through the real script:

| plant | result |
| -- | -- |
| `services/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | **SEEN** — positive control, the instrument is live |
| `services/`, `.ts`, not ending `123` | MISSED — any other password shape |
| `frontend/`, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `services/` and `packages/` are scanned |
| `services/`, `.sql`, ends `123` | MISSED — only `.ts/.tsx/.js`; **the seed SQL that** `fixtures.ts` **cites as source-of-truth is invisible** |
| `scripts/` subdir, `.ts`, ends `123` | MISSED — `--exclude-dir=scripts,tests,__tests__` |

So the gate catches exactly one shape — a `*123` literal, in a `.ts/.tsx/.js` file, under `services/` or `packages/`, not in an excluded directory, and not behind `seedPw(`.

## Why this is worth its own ticket

A guard with a documented exemption is a guard with a hole of a **known** size — and the hole never appears in the guard's own green result. This one passes today, passed before [KS-949](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-949), and would have passed with the real-person account and its published password still in place. It is a live gate that gives false assurance in CI.

- [ ] Widen the file-type and directory scope, or state the scope in the gate's own output so a green result says what it actually covered
- [ ] Decide whether the `seedPw(` exemption should survive at all now that one account (the platform admin) is held to a stricter rule than the lint enforces
- [ ] A password shape that is not `*123`

## Provenance

The exemption and the `docker-compose.yml:755` default were disclosed by the filer while doing KS-949 and **confirmed at source** by the tier-1 QA gate on PR #885 (2026-09-06T21:29:45Z); the 16-line count and the five canaries are the gate's measurement, not the filer's.

*Filed by s143 (seat A), 2026-09-07.*

title: Launcher: the assembled boot prompt is asserted by no cell — KS-907's fix can vanish at 18/0, and the seat sentence misled a live seat tonight
description:
**Nothing asserts what the boot prompt actually SAYS.** The launcher computes `$GIT_SYNC_STEP`, the suite reads it from a standalone marker, and the prompt the session actually receives is checked by no cell. Two consumers have now been proven wrong through that gap in one night.

## Item 1 — `$GIT_SYNC_STEP` never reaches an assertion (QA FINDING 1, MAJOR)

The `DRY_RUN` markers at `L659` print the variable **directly**. The boot prompt consumes it **separately** at `L483`. Two independent consumers of one variable; the suite reads only the first.

QA evidence — a one-line tamper (`887c3c23`) replacing `${GIT_SYNC_STEP}` at `L483` with literal text, marker untouched:

```
suite result:  18 passed, 0 FAILED   — every cell green
boot prompt:   199 lines -> 191 lines, "pull latest on the current branch" GONE
```

Proven with an instrumented pair (shipped + tampered, each printing `$INITIAL_PROMPT` under dry-run): shipped YES, tampered NO.

**Impact:** a future edit near `L483` — a 200-line block that is edited often — silently reverts KS-907 while the guard stays 18/0. KS-907 exists because a second seat's boot fast-forwarded a live branch under the first seat, before that session had read the brief telling it it was a second seat.

## Item 2 — the seat sentence reads as an assignment, and it misled a live seat tonight

Seat A was told by its boot prompt that its working copy was `worktrees/seat-b` — **this seat's worktree.** Seat A measured the pane mapping, disbelieved the launcher, and proceeded correctly as seat A; nothing was written into the wrong tree. A seat that trusted the line would have written into another live session's worktree.

Seat A's measurement, verbatim:

> pane %130 -> pane_pid 1790 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain" (no -B) = SEAT A = me
> pane %129 -> pane_pid 89454 -> cockpit label "Secuura/Blockchain-B" = SEAT B = s140e,
>             live since 22:24:23, PID 89456, working in worktrees/seat-b

**⚠️ The mechanism is NOT what it was handed to me as, and the correction changes the fix.** It was relayed as "the seat registry decides which worktree a pane is told to use, and no cell asserts the assignment is right." Measured here: **there is no assignment mechanism at all, and the registry has nothing to do with it.**

```
L344-346:  SEAT_WORKTREES="$(ls -1 "$PROJECT_DIR/worktrees" | sed 's|^|worktrees/|' ...)"
L363:      Sync YOUR OWN working copy instead${SEAT_WORKTREES:+ (this project has: ${SEAT_WORKTREES})},
```

`SEAT_WORKTREES` is a plain directory listing, **byte-identical for every pane**. `grep -c SEAT_WORKTREES` = 3, all three above. The sentence states a true fact — but its subject is *"YOUR OWN working copy"*, so a one-entry list reads as an assignment. With exactly one worktree present, that misreading is at its maximum.

The launcher says so itself at `L261`: *"The cockpit passes NOTHING that distinguishes the seats — both panes invoke a byte-identical command line."*

So this is a **wording defect plus a missing capability**, not a wrong computed value — nothing computed the wrong seat. The existing mitigation is the very next clause (*"if you have not been told which one is yours, ask before writing anywhere"*), and it worked: this seat asked, seat A measured.

**Fix shape (two options, the first is trivially safe):**

1. Reword so the list cannot read as ownership — e.g. *"this project contains the following worktrees: …; if you have not been told which is yours, ask."*
2. Actually derive the pane's seat. The cockpit label **is** reachable — it is in the parent shell's command line, which is how both seats identified themselves tonight (`ps -o command` on the launcher's own parent shows `[cockpit] Secuura/Blockchain-B exited`). That is a feature, not a guard, and it should not be attempted while two seats are live.

## Item 3 — the premise the whole registry rests on is asserted by no cell (QA NOT-TESTED 2)

The QA agent rated this **above FINDING 1**. The launcher registers `$$` and its `lstart` believing `exec` **replaces** the process, keeping pid and start time. The dry run `exit 0`s instead of exec'ing, so the entry it writes is stale the instant it is written. `exec claude … "$INITIAL_PROMPT"` (`L663`) is the only line below the dry-run exit and **is exercised by nothing** — not the suite, not the QA pass.

If that line were ever changed to anything that forks (a wrapper, `claude &`, `bash -c`), every registry entry would be invalid on arrival, the guard would silently stop working, and all 18 cells would stay green.

## Why these are one ticket

All three are the same mechanism: **a value the launcher computes correctly, consumed somewhere no cell looks.** Items 1 and 2 are literally the same variable's journey into `$INITIAL_PROMPT`; item 3 is the assumption that the prompt is ever `exec`'d at all. One fix — emit the assembled prompt behind a `DRY_RUN_INITIAL_PROMPT` marker and assert its **text** — makes all three assertable.

## Regression tests

Two cells against the assembled prompt, not the marker: empty registry -> prompt contains PULLTEXT; one live seat -> contains ROTEXT and **not** PULLTEXT. Red-proof by deleting the `L483` interpolation and requiring exactly those cells to fail. Item 2 adds a third: the prompt's named-worktree text against the pane's own cockpit label.

⚠️ **Do not fix the launcher while two seats are live.** It is live on disk under a by-hash gate; a relaunch is gated. `.pre-` restore copies exist for both files.

Sources: QA verdict `[QA -> Wednesday] Secuura SEAT B KS-911 + KS-912 (launcher, by hash)` 2026-09-06T12:18:53Z, read whole; item 2 from Wednesday's addendum quoting seat A, with the mechanism re-measured in this seat and corrected. Follows [[KS-911]] / [[KS-912]].

title: S revokes that emit no lifecycle event, or emit share-permission-change, are indistinguishable on K from a document that was never revoked
description:
## BLUF

**K cannot tell a revoked document from one that was never revoked, when S's revoke path emits no lifecycle event — and cannot tell a revoke from an ordinary permission change when S emits** `share-permission-change` **instead of** `share-revoke`**.** Both are silent on the K side. Raised from Stuart's PS-749 split (PS-764/765/766/767) as the **K-side** question those S-side findings imply; no S-side work is proposed here.

Measured read-only on `develop`, 2026-09-04. Nothing was written.

## The two cases, and what K actually sees

| S behaviour | K row | Can K distinguish it from "never revoked"? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| emits `share-revoke` | `action='share-revoke'` | **Yes** — this is the working path |
| emits `share-permission-change` (two Edit-dropdown paths) | `action='share-permission-change'` + free-form payload | **No** — not without parsing a payload K does not own |
| emits nothing (Outlook add-in revoke, PS-765; and the Share Now **reuse path **`:402-420`, which applies permission and expiry changes and records neither) | **no row at all** | **No — identical by construction** |

## Why K cannot distinguish them — the mechanism, not the symptom

**1. K validates the verb and never the detail. **`migrations/037_document_lifecycle_events.sql:34` states the contract in its own words:

> Verb-specific detail (e.g. rename's new display name, share-revoke's share id). **Free-form by design — the vocabulary owns the verb, S owns the detail.**

So on a `share-permission-change` row, whether the permission moved *to NoAccess* (a revoke) or from view→download (a routine change) lives entirely in a `payload JSONB` K neither schemas, validates nor documents. K has **no basis** to reclassify one as the other.

**2.** `share-revoke` **and** `share-permission-change` **are SEPARATE entries in K's own closed vocabulary** (`services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts:40-41`, `docs/VOCABULARY.md:45`). K already has a verb that means *revoked*. A revoke arriving as `share-permission-change` is therefore not merely under-detailed — it is **mislabelled against K's own contract**, and K's graph will read it as a permission edit forever.

**3. There is no gap detection, so an absent event is undetectable. **`document_lifecycle_events` holds `id, tenant_id, parent_document_id, action, payload, actor_user_id, anchor_id, created_at` — **no sequence number and no previous-event pointer**. Reads are *"events for this document, newest first"*. An event S never sends leaves no hole to notice.

**Worth flagging on its own:** migration 037's header says *"K's lineage view of these events now mirrors S's PreviousChainId chain." ***The schema does not do that.** It attaches events to `parent_document_id`; it stores no chain link between events. The comment claims a property the table cannot provide, and it is the property that would have made an omission detectable.

**4. No reconciliation exists.** The only reconciler in the tree is KS-584's **stuck-anchor** reconciler (`services/anchoring/src/reconciler.ts`) — it reconciles K's own anchor submission state against chain, not S's event stream against K's. Grep for `reconcil` across `Blockchain/Dev/services/` returns that and nothing else.

## Controls

* *The vocabulary grep can find things* — `share-permission-change` returns non-zero across 10 files, against `share-revoke`'s 20.
* *The absence of a sequence column is real, not a missed migration* — `037_…lifecycle_events.sql` is the only lifecycle migration in the tree, and no later migration adds one.
* *The* `PreviousChainId` *mirror does not exist in K* — the only matches in the K tree are the migration comment, the OpenAPI description and the repo/route prose. No column, no code.

## Why this matters

Anchoring is the product claim. A provenance record that reads identically for *"this share was revoked"* and *"this share was never revoked"* is not a weaker record — for that question it is a **wrong** one, and the reader has no way to know. It also means K's own `share-revoke` verb currently under-counts real revokes by an unknown amount, so nobody can measure the size of this from the K side either.

## Done when

1. **Decide the contract**, with S: does a revoke-to-NoAccess emit `share-revoke` (K's own vocabulary), or does `share-permission-change` carry a payload field K agrees to schema and read? Either is defensible; the current state — where it depends on which S UI path the user clicked — is not.
2. **If the payload route is chosen**, K stops treating this one payload as free-form: a declared shape, validated at the route, documented in `VOCABULARY.md`.
3. **Correct migration 037's header** so it stops claiming a `PreviousChainId` mirror the schema does not implement — or implement the chain link, which is what makes an omission detectable at all.
4. **Decide whether K should be able to detect an omission** (a per-document event sequence, or a periodic S↔K reconciliation). This is the bigger of the two and may well be its own ticket; recording the question here so it is not lost.
5. **Measure the current divergence** once the contract is agreed — how many `share-permission-change` rows are in fact revokes.

Nothing here is actionable without S. Filed as a line in the **KS-772** S↔K integration-contract stream.

## Provenance

* The S-side behaviours that raise the question | Stuart's PS-749 review split (PS-764/765/766/767) and his own 2026-09-03T23:33:13Z correction retracting two of four, relayed via Wednesday | not independently verified — S-side, and out of this ticket's scope
* Every K-side statement above | read-only on `origin/develop` at `492152a81`: `migrations/037_document_lifecycle_events.sql`, `services/originate/src/lifecycleActions.ts`, `services/originate/src/repositories/lifecycleEventRepo.ts`, `docs/VOCABULARY.md` | read 2026-09-04

title: Review stream: S<->K integration contract
description:
**Review stream for Stuart — one review, one test pass, 20 tickets.**

## The one test pass — run from Platform S against Platform K

The acceptance here is an S-side behaviour, so this is the only stream whose pass the K-side author cannot run alone:

Plus the K-side `systemTest` **Integration mode** that KS-608 already names (`GET /api/anchors/{id}` and verify must not contradict each other).

## Why these twenty

Seventeen come from the *Integrate S with K* project. Three come from *Anchoring & Chain Integrity* — **KS-721** (platform-s's opaque identityCommitment), **KS-683** (a consumer repolling anchors K reports as terminally failed) and **KS-735** (what verify shows the user after a rename). title: Review stream: API contract and the four platform suites
description:
**Review stream for Peter — one review, one test pass, 19 tickets.**

## The one test pass

1. Regenerate the OpenAPI spec, then **restart** the api-gateway container. The yaml is bind-mounted, so a restart publishes it and a rebuild does not.
2. `cd systemTest/schemathesis && python3 scripts/run.py pre-merge --base-url http://localhost:6882` — **13.4 min measured** (~2,016 cases over 318 operations). Report **the failing SET of operation ids and its diff against the develop baseline set**, never a bare count.
3. `node scripts/preflight/spec-auth-conformance.mjs --base http://localhost:6882` (seconds) — every bearer-authed operation must reject unauthenticated.
4. `cd systemTest/playwright && npm run quality:static && npm run test:unit && npm run test:e2e` — **3.8 s measured**, all three must pass.
5. `cd systemTest/performance && npm run test:smoke` — **53 s measured**. Read **the printed** `Status:` **line, not the exit code**, which is 0 either way.

## Two traps that make this run lie

* **A second back-to-back Schemathesis run fails at *setup* with 401**, not on a finding: the fuzz tiers change the test persona's password. `docker restart secuura-auth` re-seeds it. The `Run validity: OK` line does not catch this — it counts schemathesis operations, not pytest setup errors.
* **A partial stack produces a confident FALSE RED. **`docker-compose.local.yml` defines 38 services; when some are down the gateway answers `502 BAD_GATEWAY` and the suites score it as a defect indistinguishable from a real one. Run `docker compose -f docker-compose.local.yml ps` first and confirm every service is up.

Commands and wall-clocks are quoted from `Blockchain/Dev/docs/DEV-PROCESS.md` section *Manual CI-gate equivalents*.

title: Wire up the opaque refresh token that createSession already mints — one write site, zero read sites (KS-329 ruling (a) prerequisite)
description:
**BLUF —** `createSession` **has minted an opaque refresh token on every session since the session service was written, and nothing has ever read it. One write site, zero read sites, measured with a control. Wiring it up is the prerequisite Kam's KS-329 ruling (a) actually names, it is not PQC work, and it can ship without committing to ML-DSA at all.**

**Recommendation:** do this first, on its own; leave KS-329 to be the algorithm swap, which gets materially smaller once the refresh path carries no signature.

### The measurement

`services/auth/src/services/session.ts:143`:

```
refreshToken: crypto.randomBytes(32).toString('hex'),
```

* Write sites for `session.refreshToken`: **1** — `session.ts:289`, inside `rotateSessionRefreshToken`.
* Read / compare sites across all of `services/`: **0**. The only other occurrence of the identifier anywhere is a comment at `routes/auth.ts:635`.
* **Control:** the same grep against `session.isActive` — a field that genuinely is compared — returns **6** read sites (`session.ts:265, 304, 346, 357, 363`, `oauth.ts:391`). The search can find comparisons; the zero is real.
* `session.token` (`session.ts:142`, same `randomBytes(32)` shape) has **zero** read sites too.

The code already says it. `routes/auth.ts:634-635`:

> `// The session-record rotation alone is not enough — nothing in the`
> `// /refresh path compared the incoming JWT against session.refreshToken.`

The other half of the ruling is already live: `POST /api/auth/refresh` does a server-side session lookup at `routes/auth.ts:606-607` (`verifyRefreshToken` → `getSession(payload.sessionId)`). Both halves exist. What is missing is the wire between them — the cookie carries the JWT, the lookup keys off a claim *inside* that JWT, and the opaque handle sits in Redis unread.

### Why it stands on its own merits, independent of PQC

* **It removes a signature from a path that does not need one.** The refresh token is presented to exactly one endpoint, which already loads server-side state. A signed 942–1071 B JWT is doing work a 64 B handle does better.
* **It makes the size ceiling disappear permanently.** Measured on develop `8c9559cfd`: an ML-DSA-65 refresh token signs to **5018–5147 B** on real payloads against **3976 B** of usable cookie value (RFC 6265 §6.1 counts name + attributes; the exact options at `auth.ts:644-650` cost 120 B). Over by 1042–1171 B. ML-DSA-44 fits by **14 bytes** on the widest real profile — a coincidence, not a design. A 64 B handle leaves 3912 B spare for any future algorithm.
* **It simplifies reuse detection.** Today's A-05 control is sound — `denylistRefreshJti` throws rather than skips when Redis is down (`refreshDenylist.ts:30-35`), and the TTL matches the token's own remaining life — but a handle compared against the session record gives the same guarantee by construction, with no `jti`, no denylist and no TTL arithmetic.

### Scope

1. Redis reverse index `refresh:<handle> → sessionId`. Sessions are keyed `sess:<id>` and `user_sessions:<userId>` — there is currently no way to find a session *by* refresh token.
2. `POST /api/auth/refresh` — look up by handle, compare against `session.refreshToken`, rotate; drop `verifyRefreshToken` from the path.
3. The three cookie-set sites carry the handle instead of the JWT: `routes/auth.ts:394` (register), `:565` (login), `:644` (refresh).
4. `routes/oauth.ts` — `:242` and `:289` emit `refresh_token` in the body, and `:254-271` runs its **own** refresh path with its own `verifyRefreshToken` + denylist check. It moves in the same change or it becomes the bypass.
5. `shouldEmitRefreshTokenInBody` (`auth.ts:100-102`) — native/api clients take the token in the body and are not cookie-capped, but they should carry the handle too rather than leaving two token formats to verify forever.
6. **Transition, and this is the decision worth making explicitly rather than discovering:** live cookies hold JWTs. Either accept both formats for one refresh lifetime (7 days) then drop the JWT branch, or accept a single forced re-login across the estate.
7. `generateRefreshToken` / `verifyRefreshToken` / `generateTokenPair` shrink or go.

### Sizing

**1–2 days**, dominated by item 6 (the transition window) and item 4 (oauth's parallel path), not by the handle itself. Failing-test-first; the reverse index and the both-formats window each want their own test with a negative control.

### Provenance

Measured 2026-09-02 (session 110) against develop `8c9559cfd` — a read of the working tree plus local signing runs with the tree's own `jose` 6.2.3 on Node v24.7.0. No code changed, no platform writes. Full numbers, the per-profile size table and the nginx buffer check are in the KS-329 design note (comment `a9c84d3b`).

Prerequisite for KS-329. Ruling: Kam, 2026-09-02 19:35 AEST, decision card `secuura-ks329-refresh-token-size` (KS-329 comment `f62f6761`).

title: Verify results show the user nothing about what was registered — a renamed file confirms green with no explanation (PS-723)
description:
## BLUF

**A verify result shows the user nothing about what was registered, so a renamed file confirms green with no way to notice the rename.** Stuart hit this on PS-723 and ruled the direction: *"it should be explained to the user, otherwise confusion will result… b should also have the note to the user that the filename has changed."*

The API is not the problem — it already returns the registered `title`, `issuer` and `certifiedAt`. **The portal never displays them**, because it reads a nested shape the backend does not emit. And the portal already sends the presented filename, which the backend silently discards. So both halves of the comparison exist today and nothing joins them.

## RECOMMENDATION

Render the registered metadata beside the confirmation, plus a plain-language line that verification is **content-based** — a rename neither breaks nor fakes it. Where the presented filename differs from the registered title, say so explicitly rather than leaving the user to spot it.

One decision is **not mine and should be made before any code**: the flat-vs-nested contract question in §2. That is Peter's call.

## 1. What the verify response actually returns

Measured live, `POST /api/verification/verify` with `contentHash` — the path a renamed-file verify takes:

```
verified: true
title: "E2E Test Certificate"     <- the REGISTERED title
issuer: "demo"
documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt
certification: { certifiedAt, certifiedBy, certifierOrganizationId }
checks: { documentExists, hashValid, integrityVerified, ... }
```

So the metadata Stuart wants shown is already on the wire.

⚠ **The OpenAPI schema understates this. **`VerifyResponse` declares 20 properties and **none** is `title` / `originalFilename` / `registeredAt` / `registrant`; the live response carries `title` and `issuer` anyway. Same declared-vs-actual family as **KS-712** — worth fixing in the same pass so the contract stops lying about this endpoint.

## 2. Why nothing renders — the mechanism

`frontend/verifier/src/components/ResultPage.tsx:423` guards the entire "Document Details" card:

```tsx
{result.verified && result.document && ( ...Title... Issuer... )}
```

* The API returns `title` and `issuer` **at the top level** and emits **no** `document` **object** (measured top-level keys: `verified, documentId, title, documentType, status, contentHash, certifiedAt, issuer, blockchain, certification, checks, verifiedAt`).
* `result.document` is therefore undefined, the guard is falsy, and **the card never renders**.
* The portal references `result.document.*` **5** times and `result.title` **0** times. Control: `result.verified` matches **14** times, so the grep discriminates.
* The data is **not** lost in parsing — `VerifyResponseSchema` is `.passthrough()`, so the top-level `title` survives into the parsed object and is simply never read.
* The schema *does* declare `document: DocumentSummarySchema.nullable().optional()` carrying `title` + `issuer`. **The frontend was written against a nested shape the backend does not produce** — one side moved and the other did not.
* Confirmed on the path in use: all three verifier call sites hit **v1 **`/verification/verify`. v2 is a different shape entirely (`count, hash, matches, verifiedAt`) and the portal does not use it.

### The contract question — Peter's call, not to be decided in the fix

Either the **frontend reads the flat fields**, or the **backend nests them** under `document` to match the schema the client already expects. Both work; they differ in blast radius (the backend shape is consumed by the Outlook add-in and issuer too). Naming it rather than picking it.

## 3. `fileName` is already sent, and silently discarded

`frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx:127` sends `{ contentHash, fileName: file.name }` and `:138` threads `fileName` into the result object. So the **client already holds both halves** of the comparison — presented name and registered title — and needs no new input to detect a mismatch.

Server-side, however:

* `VerifyRequest` declares only `documentId, hash, title, contentHash` — `fileName` **is not in the contract.**
* **No backend route handler reads it**: 0 files under `services/*/src/routes/` reference `fileName`, against a control of **8** referencing `contentHash`.

So the field is sent on every verify and thrown away. Either consume it (and declare it) or stop sending it — the current state is a silent no-op.

## 4. Scope — three surfaces, per Stuart, not just the verifier portal

His comment names them: *"This affects Outlook plug ins, and Verify functionality in 'Views' and directly from the menu."* Verify call sites in the tree:

| app | file |
| -- | -- |
| verifier portal | `frontend/verifier/src/components/VerifyPage.tsx`, `ResultPage.tsx` |
| **Outlook add-in** | `frontend/outlook-addin/src/utils/api.ts` |
| issuer portal | `frontend/issuer/src/services/api.ts`, `components/admin/ConnectorsPage.tsx` |

Whatever wording is agreed should land on all of them, or the same confusion simply moves to whichever surface is left out.

## 5. Design constraint — the KS-695 erasure interplay

**KS-695 item 2 brings** `documents.title` **INTO erasure coverage**, because S sends the real filename as `Title` on originate (`CardanoAnchorService.cs:407`). For S-originated documents that field **is** the original filename — exactly what this ticket wants displayed. Item 3 goes further: connector-scoped dissolution blanks all connector documents' titles.

So the two pull opposite ways: PS-723 wants the registered name shown; KS-695 makes that same field erasable PII that can legitimately be blank. Both are correct on their own terms.

**This must be specified, not discovered:** decide what a verify result shows for a document whose title has been erased — a blank, or an explicit *"registered name erased"* state. Rendering empty silently would recreate today's confusion in a new form.

## Not in scope here
