No fix in this ticket — it is the specification and the evidence. No change to PS-723, which is Stuart's.

## Related

* **PS-723** — *Verify still confirms if filename has changed* (Stuart, 2026-09-01). The originating report and his ruling.
* **KS-712** — the declared-vs-actual spec gap this endpoint also exhibits.
* **KS-695** — `documents.title` erasure coverage; the design constraint in §5.

title: test:pr never re-imports the OpenAPI spec, so Akto scans a collection that has drifted from it — a declared operation is not a scanned one
description:
> **Origin.** Parked on [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) comment `718362a9` (2026-08-28T22:30:04Z) under "Related, found today and unfiled for the same reason" — `issueCreate` was refusing workspace-wide. Filed 2026-08-29. **No new measurement was taken for this ticket**; the numbers are the ones recorded on 2026-08-28 against PR [#762](<https://github.com/Secuura/Distributed_Secuura/pull/762>).

## BLUF

**Declaring an operation in the OpenAPI spec does not put it in Akto's scan collection. **`test:pr` does **not** re-import the spec — only `test:pre-merge` runs `feed-har` — so the collection Akto scans drifts away from the spec silently, and a PR that adds operations gets an Akto result that never touched them.

This is the [KS-712](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-712) premise reaching one step further than that ticket states it. KS-712 says: an operation absent from the spec is invisible to both tools. This says: an operation **present** in the spec can still be invisible to Akto.

## Measured

On PR #762, which declares four operations (`GET`/`PUT` on `/api/privacy/settings` and `/api/settings/notifications`):

| operation | occurrences in the Akto report |
| -- | -- |
| the two endpoints #762 declares | **0** |
| control endpoint A | 105 |
| control endpoint B | 7 |

The two controls are what make the zero readable: the report was produced, it was parsed, and it does contain occurrence counts — the declared endpoints simply are not in it. Without the controls, `0` and "the grep could not have matched" are the same reading.

## Why it is worth a ticket rather than a note

The failure is **silent and it points the wrong way**. An author who declares a new operation, runs `test:pr`, and sees no Akto finding on it will reasonably conclude the operation was scanned and is clean. Under the current wiring that conclusion is unsupported: the operation was never in the collection. Every "Akto clean" claim in a Test Evidence block on a spec-adding PR carries this caveat, whether or not the author knows it.

This sits directly against the merge flow adopted 2026-08-25, where the **Test Evidence block carries the testing claim**. A block that says "Akto FAIL 3, none on a touched route" is true and still misleading if the touched routes could not have been scanned.

## Not fixed, and why

Re-importing the spec into Akto **mutates harness state** — the collection is shared, and @PeterObeden has live work on it ([KS-717](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-717)). Doing it unilaterally mid-review would corrupt someone else's measurements to fix a reporting gap. It belongs with the harness owner, alongside [KS-716](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-716).

## Possible shapes (for whoever owns it — not a design commitment)

1. Have `test:pr` re-import when the spec's hash has changed since the last import — cheap, and the common case is no change.
2. Fail `test:pr` loudly when an operation touched by the diff is absent from the collection, rather than reporting a clean scan of it. This is the honesty-guard shape already used elsewhere in the harness.
3. Leave `test:pr` alone and have the Test Evidence template require the author to state Akto collection coverage explicitly, so the gap is visible rather than assumed away.

Option 2 is the one that fails closed, but it is the harness owner's call.

title: The whole super-admin surface is silently unscanned — no system_admin block means the HAR replay fallback never fires (0 of 16 endpoints, incl. KS-694's GDPR routes)
description:
## BLUF

Every **super-admin-only** endpoint is invisible to Akto on a stock local checkout, and nothing says so. `config/secrets.yml` carries no `system_admin` block — `config/secrets.example.yml` documents one — so `resolveReplayTokens()` returns `adminToken: null`, the issuer→admin fallback never fires, and each endpoint `ISSUER_ADMIN` cannot get a 2xx from stays a spec-imported placeholder (`responseCode: -1`) that `api_selection_filters` excludes from **every** BOLA/BFLA/authz template.

The bias is the problem: the endpoints that are hardest to authenticate to are the privileged ones, so the harness systematically skips the surface where an authz defect matters most — and reports green.

## Measured — 2026-08-29, local slot-1 stack, Akto 2.22.2

```
collection 56068490 "OpenAPI Secuura API": 323 endpoints
  absolute (scannable)  : 307
  relative (unscannable):  16

endpoints scanned, BOLA run:
  relative : 0 / 16
  absolute : 46 / 80 sampled     <-- discriminating control
```

The 16 that never get scanned:

```
/api/admin/audit/export      /api/analytics/activity        /api/analytics/certifications
/api/analytics/governance    /api/analytics/overview        /api/analytics/revenue
/api/analytics/users         /api/analytics/verifications   /api/audit-log
/api/billing/customers/by-email  /api/gdpr/consent/check    /api/gdpr/deletion-log
/api/m365/callback           /api/oauth/authorize           /api/onedrive/files
/api/system-errors
```

The 7 `analytics` paths are excluded on purpose (`VOLATILE_PATH_RE`, KS-357). **The other 9 are not excluded by anything — they are simply unreachable by the replay persona.** They include `/api/gdpr/deletion-log`, `/api/gdpr/consent/check` and `/api/system-errors` — the exact routes **KS-694 (Urgent)** just put a role gate on, and `/api/oauth/authorize`.

Note the tell: an unscannable entry is stored as a bare path (`/api/audit-log` — the tenant-provisioning upstream path) while a scanned one is a full gateway URL (`http://localhost:6882/api/documents`). That difference is a cheap, reliable detector.

## Proof of causation

Adding the documented `system_admin` block to local `secrets.yml` (gitignored; seeded `admin@secuura.com`, per `secrets.example.yml`):

```
captured 2xx samples : 71 → 79
audit-log in api_info: /api/audit-log  →  http://localhost:6882/api/platform/audit-log
ADD_USER_ID on it    : 0 rows → 1 row
```

That change is what made **KS-708** reproducible at all. Before it, `ADD_USER_ID` reported *"188 tested, 0 vulnerable"* while never touching the endpoint under investigation.

## The documentation understates it

`secrets.example.yml:30-34` says `system_admin` is *"optional. Only needed to seed the locked-account test-role… Absent ⇒ that one role is skipped (best-effort), and* `AUTH_BYPASS_LOCKED_ACCOUNT_TOKEN_ROLE` *keeps skipping honestly."*

That is not the whole consequence. Absent, it also removes the entire super-admin surface from HAR replay, and therefore from every similarity-based authz template. Nobody reading that comment would expect it.

## Suggested shape

1. **Warn loudly when** `adminToken` **is null** — name the count of endpoints that will consequently have no 2xx sample. Silence is the actual defect; a skipped endpoint should never be indistinguishable from a clean one (the KS-700 / KS-709 principle, applied to coverage rather than results).
2. Correct the `secrets.example.yml` comment to state the coverage consequence.
3. Consider failing `test:setup` when the block is absent, or defaulting it to the seeded local admin.

## Done means

1. A run without a system-admin token says so, with the affected endpoint count.
2. `secrets.example.yml` states the real consequence.
3. The relative-vs-absolute URL split is asserted somewhere, so this cannot silently regress.

title: Akto pr-scan is non-deterministic — three runs on near-identical code gave 1 HIGH / 1 HIGH (different endpoint) / 0 HIGH
description:
## BLUF

**Three Akto** `test:pr` **runs tonight, same harness, same command, gave three different answers — and none of the three carried a captured request or response.** A gate that answers differently on identical input cannot be read either way: its PASS is not evidence of absence, and its FAIL is not evidence of a defect until re-derived by hand.

## Measured — 2026-08-27, all three within ~20 minutes

| run | target | HIGH |
| -- | -- | -- |
| baseline (s76) | `develop ca5b643e0` | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on a **GDPR** route |
| KS-694 fix branch | `develop` + the KS-694 role-gate fix (touches `gdpr.ts` + `systemErrors.ts` only) | **1** — `BOLA / ADD_USER_ID` on `GET /api/documents` |
| 17-PR integration stack | `develop cc65abad5` + 17 open PRs | **0** — `verdict: PASS`, 804 clean, 2 known-FP |

The middle run is the one that rules out "the code changed": that branch touches two route files and cannot have introduced or removed a finding on `/api/documents`.

## The `/api/documents` finding does not reproduce

Derived by hand rather than trusted:

* `?userId=` **injection changes nothing.** The identical document set comes back with no `userId`, with another user's, and with a third user's.
* **Cross-tenant isolation holds.** A default-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 18 documents, an oxford-tenant `ISSUER_ADMIN` sees 70, **full-id overlap 0**. (An earlier probe of my own appeared to show a shared document — that was an 8-character id truncation in my script, not a leak. Recording the false alarm so nobody re-derives it.)

## Why this matters now

Since 2026-08-27 the four local suites are the **only** merge gate (Kam: *"billing will not be fixed"*). Akto is one of the four. **Two of tonight's three runs would have produced a different merge decision on the same code.** That is the same failure mode `KS-519` names for permanently-red checks, arriving from the other direction.

## Related, already known

`KS-694` came out of the first of these runs — the finding was real but its **label** (`BOLA / ADD_USER_ID`) was wrong, and re-deriving it produced a more precise and more serious defect. Same pattern: the scanner points at something; the label and the endpoint are both unreliable.

## Suggested next step

Establish whether the variance is in the scan (endpoint sampling / timing / auth state) or the reporting, by running `test:pr` N times against a frozen commit with the stack untouched between runs, and recording the HIGH set each time. **Not started** — filed so tonight's measurement is not lost.

title: Anchor-status standoff: a consumer repolls anchors K reports as terminally failed — K's labelling is already honest (KS-587), so the fix is terminal-state handling, not a new K signal
description:
## BLUF

**The standoff is real, but its stated mechanism is wrong — and measuring demo inverted the ownership.** The premise going in was *"K reports simulated anchors as* `confirmed`*; Platform S's honesty rule refuses a* `mock_tx_` *hash; S repolls forever."* Measured on demo tonight, **K does not report them as confirmed.** All 83 simulated anchors on demo are flagged `simulated = true`, `status = failed`, carrying the explicit error `KS-587: simulated placeholder — never on chain; marked …`. **Zero rows on demo are** `simulated = true` **and** `confirmed`**.** K already fixed this — that is what **KS-520 → KS-522 → KS-587** were.

So the accurate statement is: **a consumer is polling anchors that K reports as terminally** `failed`**, forever.** That is not a labelling defect on our side. It is a missing terminal-state rule on the consumer side.

## Recommendation

1. **Layer 1 — the actual fix, PS-side (Stuart's):** treat `status: failed` as **terminal** and stop polling. No new K signal is required; the one already published is sufficient and has been since KS-587 deployed.
2. **Layer 2 — K exposes** `simulated` **machine-readably: ALREADY DONE. This is a no-op, closed here, and no work should be raised for it.** Verified in the **shipped** demo image, not just the source tree.
3. **Layer 3 — env hygiene (Stuart's call):** whatever is polling demo from `52.74.18.212` should not be pointed at demo at all.
4. **Layer 4 — per-environment Blockfrost keys:** still open, still pending the credential question below.

## Detail — what was measured, on demo, read-only

**Demo is not simulating.** `SIMULATE_ANCHORING` is **absent** from the anchoring container's environment (0 matches against a 22-line env, so the read itself is proven). Boot logs: `Cardano integration active — real blockchain anchoring enabled`, `cardanoMode: "REAL (Blockfrost)"`, network `preview`.

`anchor_store` **composition — 285 rows total:**

| shape | `simulated` | `status` | n | first | last |
| -- | -- | -- | -- | -- | -- |
| real 64-hex | false | **confirmed** | **194** | 2026-07-08 | 2026-08-14 |
| `mock_tx_*` | **true** | **failed** | **83** | 2026-07-31 | 2026-08-01 |
| NULL | false | failed | 6 | 2026-07-11 | 2026-08-05 |
| real 64-hex | false | failed | 2 | 2026-08-04 | 2026-08-10 |

Crosstab, stated plainly because it is the whole argument: `simulated = true` appears **only** with `status = failed`. **There is no (**`simulated = true`**,** `confirmed`**) row on demo.** Controls: `simulated` is never NULL (0 of 285); totals reconcile 194 + 83 + 6 + 2 = 285.

**The loop's corpus is fully resident on demo — the cross-instance hypothesis is dead.** All **71** distinct anchor ids the loop requests are present in demo's `anchor_store`: **71 present / 0 absent**. Controls both fired: a fabricated id `anchor_0000…0000` matched **0**, a known-real id matched **1**. So these anchors were minted **on demo**; they were not minted on a simulated instance elsewhere and verified here.

**And every one of them is a failed anchor:**

|  | n |
| -- | -- |
| `simulated = true`, `failed`, mock hash | **68** |
| `simulated = false`, `failed`, NULL hash | **3** |
| **confirmed** | **0** |

That is the finding. The loop is polling **71 anchors that can never succeed**, 68 of which K has explicitly labelled as simulated placeholders that were never on chain.

**The** `simulated` **flag is machine-readable, and it ships.** In the **running** demo image (`/app/dist/index.js`, and `docker inspect` shows **no bind-mounts**, so the image *is* what serves):

* `...(simulated ? { simulated: true, simulatedTxRef: rawTxHash } : {})` — 3 emit sites
* `verified: !txView.simulated && anchor.status === 'confirmed'`
* a placeholder hash is moved to `simulatedTxRef` and `transactionHash` is set to **null**, so a mock hash is never presented as a transaction hash

Control: a nonsense token grepped for in the same file returned 0. Source agrees (`services/anchoring/src/index.ts` `honestTxView`, `anchoring.openapi.ts` `simulated: z.boolean().optional()` + `simulatedTxRef`).

**The Blockfrost split — both "zero Blockfrost calls" and "quota exhausted" are true at once.** They describe **different routes**:

| route | behaviour | last 60 min |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `GET /api/anchors/{id}` | **pure DB read**, ~1 ms, no Blockfrost | **1,970 × 200** |
| `GET /api/anchors/verify/{hash}` | **live Blockfrost** | **608 × 200 · 460 × 500** |

**457** of those 500s carry Blockfrost's own string `"Usage is over limit."` (against 3,935 total anchoring log lines). So Stuart's agent's *"zero Blockfrost calls in two hours"* is **correct for status GETs** — that is exactly what they observed, and it is a real property of the code. Our *"quota exhausted"* is **correct for verify-by-hash**. Neither observation refutes the other; the earlier reconciliation hypothesis (creation-simulated / verify-live) was the right shape but the wrong axis — it is **status-read vs verify-by-hash**, not creation vs verification.

**Traffic, for scale.** Last 6 h at demo's edge: **23,515 requests from** `52.74.18.212`**, of 23,515 total — 100.0%** of demo's inbound. Split: `POST /api/verification/verify` 11,620 · `GET /api/anchors/{id}` 9,704 · `GET /api/documents/{id}` 2,190 — **all 200 at the gateway.** ~3,919/hr, consistent with the ~3,850/hr measured on KS-670 across 08-14 → 08-21.

## Attribution, corrected gently

Stuart's agent read the honesty rule as **S's**. The record says the honest-labelling rule was implemented **in K**: **KS-520** (Urgent, Done) — anchoring fabricated a `tx_sim_` hash and marked the document anchored under `SIMULATE_ANCHORING`; **KS-522** (High, Done) — a simulated anchor presented as genuinely verified, no honest-labelling signal; **KS-587** (High, Deployed to UAT) — *"84 demo anchors carry* `mock_tx_` *hashes but are flagged* `simulated=false` *+ confirmed"*. KS-587 is the direct ancestor of this ticket: it found **84** mis-flagged rows and remediated them. Tonight demo holds **83** rows carrying its remediation message. **The defect Stuart's agent describes is one K already found and fixed** — which is worth saying clearly, because it means no K change is needed and the polling behaviour is unaffected by anything we ship.

Credit where due: their diagnosis of the *mechanism* — a consumer refusing a mock hash and retrying forever — is correct and is what made this tractable. Only the direction of the labelling defect was off, and their own caveat (which K instance they queried was unstated) is what prompted the measurement that found it.

## What their numbers describe

Their **1,638 anchors, all simulated** is **not demo** — demo has **285** anchors, of which 83 are simulated. Since all 71 polled ids resolve on demo, the polling target is demo; the 1,638-row instance they inspected is a different K (most likely one of the local development stacks). **Not asserted, and it does not change the finding:** the fix is terminal-state handling regardless of which K holds the larger simulated corpus.

## Still open

* **The credential question, unanswered since 2026-08-20:** does the local K stack hold **demo's** Blockfrost key or its own? If demo's, per-environment key scoping becomes the durable fix, and Kintsugi (its own free-tier project per environment) is the working precedent.
* **The Blockfrost allowance *period* is still unverified** — nothing here should be sized on a 50k/day assumption.

## Provenance

* Demo measurements | read-only SSH to `secuura02-demo-vm`, 2026-08-21 10:26–10:40Z | container env, `docker logs`, `psql` SELECTs, and one `docker inspect`. **No writes, no config change, no key action, no restarts.** Two scratch files created under the VM's `/tmp` during extraction were removed in the same command.
* Loop corpus | demo nginx gateway logs, 6 h window | two of my own extraction patterns were wrong on the first pass (`doc_` vs `doc-`, and verify hashes ride in the POST body rather than the URL); both corrected before any figure here was written down.
* KS-520 / KS-522 / KS-587 / PS-522 | live Linear reads, 2026-08-21 | `PS-522` returns nothing; `KS-999` used as a not-found control.

title: #568 publishes 17 URLs on secuura.io — an unresolving, seemingly unowned domain (KS-669 class; no guard rule covers URLs)
description:
## BLUF

**#568 publishes 17 URLs on** `secuura.io` **— a domain that does not resolve and that we do not appear to own.** This is the same class as [[KS-669]] (`exports.secuura.com`, an unowned for-sale domain in the published spec), three weeks on, and it is back because **no guard rule covers URLs** — E1 splits on `@` and only sees email addresses.

Filed separately from KS-669 rather than as a comment on it, deliberately: KS-669 is In Progress with its own scope (17 of its 18 URLs are still open work) and its operative defect is that it is **unassigned**. Folding a second, differently-sourced class into it makes it bigger, not more actionable. Cross-linked both ways.

**Stated fairly in both directions: #568 is a net improvement here.** It *removes* all **3** `demo@secuura.io` addresses that `develop` publishes today — E1 doing exactly its job. The URL class is the part nothing checks.

---

## Evidence

**DNS, with a control set** (2026-08-21):

| Domain | rcode | NS | SOA |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `secuura.io` | **NXDOMAIN** | none | none |
| `secuura.ai` | NOERROR | `dns2.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.net` | NOERROR | `dns1.registrar-servers.com.` | present |
| `secuura.com` | NOERROR | `ns4.afternic.com.` | present |

The three controls resolve, so the resolver works and the NXDOMAIN discriminates.

⚠ **A limit on this evidence, stated rather than glossed:** `whois secuura.io` falls through to IANA and returns the `.io` **TLD** record, so its `status: ACTIVE` describes the TLD, not the domain. **I am reporting DNS only — NXDOMAIN with no NS and no SOA. I am not claiming a registration status.** Someone with registrar access should confirm ownership before this is closed either way.

**Occurrences in the published spec** (`Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml`):

| Pattern | `c114ceddd` (#568) | `origin/develop` |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `example.secuura.io` | **17** | **0** |
| `demo@secuura.io` | **0** | **3** |

Repo-wide on #568 the string appears **35** times across 7 files — the 17 published ones plus 18 in the generating sources (`auth`, `billing`, `m365-integration`, `originate`, `prism` `.openapi.ts`, and `synthesize.ts`). Fixing the source fixes both.

**The 17, by field** — these are not all cosmetic:

* `redirectUri` ×1 · `webhookUrl` ×1 · `successUrl` ×2 · `cancelUrl` ×2 · `siteUrl` ×1
* `serviceEndpoint` ×5 · `url` ×3 · bare array items ×2

`redirectUri`, `webhookUrl`, `successUrl`/`cancelUrl` and `serviceEndpoint` are all fields an integrator may copy into a working configuration. A published spec that points them at an unregistered domain is a domain anyone can register.

**Source** — `Blockchain/Dev/scripts/openapi-examples/synthesize.ts:203`:

```ts
case 'uri':
case 'url':
    return 'https://example.secuura.io/resource';
```

Every `format: uri` / `format: url` field gets this one literal.

---

## Fix direction

Use a domain reserved for the purpose. `example.com` **is reserved by RFC 2606 / RFC 6761** and can never be registered by anyone — which is the same guarantee the email side already relies on (E1 permits `example.com` addresses). `https://example.com/resource` is a one-line change at `synthesize.ts:203`, plus a regeneration.

**Then close the hole that let it back in:** add a URL rule to the guard — an example whose value parses as a URL must have a host in the reserved set (`example.com`/`.org`/`.net`, `localhost`), or be allowlisted with a reason. Without it this class returns a third time. That rule belongs with the guard-coverage work in the sibling ticket.

---

## Calls needed from @PeterD

1. **Do we own** `secuura.io`**?** If we do, this drops to "point it somewhere real or use `example.com` anyway". If we don't, it should not be in a published spec at all.
2. Is `example.com` acceptable as the synthesised URL host, or do you want a real owned host (e.g. under `secuura.ai`)?

---

**Verified by:** @kamil.kreiser, 2026-08-21 — DNS with control set, occurrence counts on both refs, source line read. Working tree untouched. Related: KS-669 (same class, `exports.secuura.com`), KS-256/#568, KS-665.

title: Compose seeds published *123 credentials by default, and the 11 rotation vars never reach the auth container from .env — every compose deploy (local, demo VM, Kintsugi)
description:
## BLUF

**Any compose deploy of this platform comes up seeding the published** `*123` **credentials, and the documented way to rotate them silently does nothing unless you happen to put them in the one undocumented file.** Two halves of the same asymmetry in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

* the single variable that **enables** published default passwords is interpolated from `.env` and **defaults to** `true`;
* the eleven variables that **replace** those passwords are not interpolated at all, and reach the container only via `.env.local` — which no example file and no doc mentions.

So the natural path (`.env`, which is what `env.example` and the deploy docs use) gives you: seeding **on**, published credentials **live**, and your rotation **ignored** — while the seeder logs that it updated the accounts.

Blast radius is **every compose deploy**: local, the demo VM, and Kintsugi. `docker-compose.local.yml` `include:`s `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`, so the canonical local stack inherits it, and the demo VM + Kintsugi run that file directly.

## Recommendation

Two small changes, both in `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`:

1. Flip the default: `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-false}`, and set it explicitly to `true` in the local-dev path that actually wants it. Opting in should be an act, not an omission.
2. Interpolate the eleven rotation variables in the `auth` service's `environment:` block the same way every other secret is (`- DEMO_USER_PASSWORD=${DEMO_USER_PASSWORD:-}` …), so `.env` — the file everyone edits — is a working channel. Then document them in `env.example`.

Neither is a code change to the auth service; the seeder's logic (`userRepo.ts:965-995`) is correct as written.

## A — the gate defaults to ON, and its stated premise is dead

`Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:626`

```yaml
- ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=${ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS:-true}
```

The pen-test **F-05** fix gated the demo seeder on this variable. The auth service states the premise the gate rests on, at `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:987-991`:

> *"The hardcoded fallbacks remain only because the seeder itself is now gated on* `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true` *(above) — i.e. **a deploy that doesn't explicitly opt in never sees these strings**."*

That premise is false for every compose deploy, because the compose file opts in on your behalf.

The justification for the default is at `:623-625`:

> *"Defaults to true here ONLY because docker-compose.yml is the local-dev compose; production is on Container Apps where this env var is unset and the gate stays closed."*

**That reasoning died with the KS-414 VM pivot (2026-07-08).** The Container Apps estate was deleted on 2026-07-31. Since the pivot, `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml` is not "the local-dev compose" — it is *the* deployment artefact for the demo VM and now for Kintsugi as well. The comment describes an architecture the project no longer has.

Measured on the running local stack:

```
$ docker exec secuura-auth sh -c 'echo $ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS'
true
```

## B — the eleven rotation variables never reach the container from `.env`

Derived from source rather than from any prior write-up — every `seedPw()` call site in `services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts`:

`ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_APEX_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_BUPA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_DELTA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_GREENFIELD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_OXFORD_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_SECUURA_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` · `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD`

| check | result | control |
| -- | -- | -- |
| occurrences of each of the 11 in `docker-compose.yml` | **0 / 11** | `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` → **1** |
| present in the running `secuura-auth` container | **0 / 11** | gate present, value `true`; 95 env vars total |

Both zero-results carry a control that fires independently, so they are real absences and not a grep that could never match.

The code's own rotation instruction (`userRepo.ts:992-993`) is:

> *"For per-tenant rotation, set* `DEMO_<TENANT>_PASSWORD` *env vars in Azure Key Vault and **surface them to the auth container**."*

"Surface them to the auth container" is the whole problem — it names no channel, and only one of the two obvious ones works.

## The correction — this is NOT "rotation is impossible"

An earlier write-up of this (KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a`) concluded the documented rotation *cannot work*. **That over-claims, and the correction matters because it changes the fix.** The `auth` service does declare an env_file:

```yaml
env_file:
  - path: .env.local
    required: false
```

Tested rather than assumed: of the **66** variables declared in `.env.local`, **66** are present in the running container. `.env.local` is a fully working injection channel.

So the accurate finding is an **asymmetry of channel**, which is worse than a flat "it doesn't work" because it fails silently in exactly one direction:

| variable | channel | reaches container from `.env`? | effect |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS` | `${…:-true}` interpolation | **yes**, and defaults **true** | published `*123` credentials get seeded |
| the 11 `*_PASSWORD` vars | `.env.local` env_file only | **no** | rotation silently ignored |

`.env` is the file `env.example` is copied to, the file the setup instructions name, and the file compose reads for `${…}` interpolation — but it is *not* an env_file for `auth`, so values placed there are invisible to the seeder. Neither `env.example` nor `.env.local.example` mentions any of the eleven, or the gate.

## Why it fails convincingly

Recorded on Kintsugi during the KS-601 Stage C build (2026-08-20) — **this half is that session's on-box measurement; I have not re-run it here**, because reproducing it locally means changing `demo@`'s password and breaking the preflight persona:

Setting the eleven in `.env` and recreating the auth container printed `Demo user updated to match seed config` account after account — on a code path that genuinely does execute an `UPDATE … password_hash`. **The old password still authenticated.** Only a negative control (attempting a login with the *old* credential and expecting it to fail) caught it. Fixed on that box with a compose override making all 11 visible, then verified both directions: old `demo123` → **401**, new credential → **200**.

That is the part worth carrying: the failure produces success-shaped log output, so anyone rotating credentials and checking the logs will believe they succeeded.

## Scope note

Not in scope here: whether the demo VM *should* keep its seeded public credentials. Those are deliberate, documented sample logins for public demos (project `CLAUDE.md`). This ticket is about a deploy coming up more permissive than its operator intended, and a rotation that reports success without doing anything.

## Evidence

* `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml:570-666` — `auth` service; `:626` the gate; `:623-625` the dead premise; `env_file` at `:576-578`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts:965-995` — the F-05 gate, the `seedPw()` helper and its rotation instruction.
* `docker-compose.local.yml:33-35` — `include:` of `Blockchain/Dev/docker-compose.yml`.
* `Blockchain/Dev/env.example`, `Blockchain/Dev/.env.local.example` — neither names the eleven or the gate.
* KS-601 comment `4ada1e3a` — the Kintsugi on-box record (superseded on the "cannot work" point by the correction above).

## Suggested owner

Unassigned deliberately. Compose/deploy topology rather than service logic — @peter or @stuart to route; happy to take it myself if neither has context loaded.

title: KS-78 drift check is wrong three ways — reports 7 commits of drift where 212 exist, labels `develop` as `main`, and anchors to a stock redis image
description:
## BLUF

**The KS-78 local-drift check reports a number that is real but labelled with the wrong branch, anchored to the wrong containers, and computed from the wrong kind of timestamp.** Today it printed **7 commits** of drift. The drift that actually exists, measured against the oldest code image in the running stack, is **212**.

Three independent defects, all in `Launch_Claude.command:465-481`. Diagnosed 2026-08-17 (session 43) after **two consecutive sessions (41, 42) flagged the warning as unreconcilable and moved on** — s42 recorded it in project history as an open question handed forward. That is the cost: *two sessions discounted a TRUE warning because its label pointed at a branch that had not moved.*

## Defect 1 — the label says `main`; the code measures `HEAD`

```sh
# Launch_Claude.command:475
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$EARLIEST_START" 2>/dev/null | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
# Launch_Claude.command:476-477
printf '[KS-78 drift warning] %s commit(s) on main since the running stack was built (%s).\n' "$DRIFT_COUNT" "$EARLIEST_START"
```

`git log` is invoked with **no revision argument**, so it walks `HEAD` — the currently checked-out branch. The word `main` is hardcoded in the `printf` and has never been measured.

**Discriminating control**, all against the same baseline instant `2026-08-17T00:52:38.647560758Z`:

| what was run | count |
| -- | -- |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S>` (exactly what the launcher runs) | **7** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> develop` | **7** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> main` | **0** |
| `git log --oneline --since=<S> origin/main` | **0** |
| `git symbolic-ref --short HEAD` | `develop` |

The no-rev form agrees with `develop` and disagrees with `main` — that is the discriminator, not an inference.

**Why it was ever right:** KS-78 closed **2026-05-15**, when `main` *was* the working branch. Git Flow (KS-137) made `develop` the integration line on **2026-05-25** — ten days later. The check never measured `main`; it measured `HEAD`, which happened to be `main` on the day it shipped and silently became `develop` a fortnight after.

## Defect 2 — `StartedAt` is restart time, not build time

`EARLIEST_START` comes from `docker inspect --format '{{.State.StartedAt}}'`. That is when the container process **last started**, which moves on any `docker start` / `restart` / `compose up` **without any rebuild**.

Proven on the live stack rather than asserted — `secuura-redis`:

```
Created    : 2026-08-12T21:42:23Z
StartedAt  : 2026-08-17T00:52:38Z   <-- 4 days later
RestartCount: 0
```

The container was not rebuilt and not auto-restarted, yet its baseline moved forward four days.

**The practical false negative:** `docker compose down && docker compose up -d` (no `build`) sets every `StartedAt` to *now*, so `DRIFT_COUNT` becomes **0** while every image on disk stays exactly as stale as it was. The check goes silent in precisely the situation it exists to catch.

## Defect 3 — the baseline is anchored to containers that hold no repo code

`EARLIEST_START` is the **minimum** `StartedAt` **across every** `secuura-*` **container**, and that set includes stock upstream infrastructure images. Today the anchor is `secuura-redis` → `redis:8-alpine`, **image built 2026-06-22**; the oldest image of any kind in the stack is `postgres:15-alpine`, **built 2026-02-26**. Neither contains a line of this repo.

Meanwhile the oldest **code** image actually running is `secuura-website-frontend`, built **2026-07-19T00:15:56Z**.

**Measured consequence:**

| baseline used | commits on `develop` since |
| -- | -- |
| what the check used (earliest `StartedAt`, from a stock redis) | **7** — what it printed |
| oldest **code** image build time (`website-frontend`, 2026-07-19) | **212** |

**The check understates real drift by roughly 30x.** It answers "how long since you last ran `compose up`", not "how stale is the code you are running".

## Suggested fix (not applied — see below)

Compute the baseline from **image build time of code-bearing containers only**, and name the branch it actually measured:

```sh
BRANCH="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" symbolic-ref --short HEAD 2>/dev/null || echo HEAD)"
# oldest .Image .Created across containers whose image is locally built (not a registry tag)
DRIFT_COUNT="$(git -C "$GIT_REPO_DIR" log --oneline --since="$OLDEST_IMAGE_BUILT" "$BRANCH" | wc -l | tr -d ' ')"
printf '[KS-78 drift warning] %s commit(s) on %s since the oldest running image was BUILT (%s).\n' "$DRIFT_COUNT" "$BRANCH" "$OLDEST_IMAGE_BUILT"
```

Filtering "code-bearing" is the one judgement call: `.Config.Image` for locally built services is `2_project_files-<svc>` (no registry host, no upstream tag), whereas infra is `redis:8-alpine` / `postgres:15-alpine`. That distinction is available without extra tooling.

## What I deliberately did NOT do

**No edit to** `Launch_Claude.command`**.** It is boot-path infrastructure for every session, it is **not under version control** (project root is not a git repo — git lives at `2_Project_Files/`), and there are **16 copies of the template across the workspace**, so a fix here fixes one of sixteen. Changing it is Kam's call, and Wednesday is carrying the fleet-wide fix on the WED board gated on his go-ahead, citing this ticket as the evidence.

## Acceptance

1. The warning names the branch it actually measured (or measures the branch it names).
2. The baseline is image **build** time, not container **start** time — verified by a negative control: `compose up -d` with no rebuild must **not** reduce the count.
3. Infra containers built from upstream tags do not set the baseline — verified by a positive control: the reported count matches the count computed from the oldest locally-built image.

title: The extranet test board has never shown a green run — 0 passed in 22, and the latest red is E2E 210/0 with Schemathesis producing no results
description:
## BLUF

**The team's own status board has never once been green.** The extranet Testing tab has recorded **22 Platform K runs since 2026-05-25: 17** `failed`**, 5** `error`**, 0** `passed`**.** Not one.

And the most recent red is misleading: **E2E passed 210/0**, and the run is marked failed because Schemathesis produced no parseable results.

A board that is permanently red is a board everyone learns to ignore — at which point it can never signal anything, which is the whole reason it was built ([KS-138](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-138), now Done and archived).

## Measured

`GET /api/tests/platform-k/runs` (22 runs, oldest 2026-05-25):

```
failed : 17
error  :  5
passed :  0
```

Latest dashboard (`GET /api/tests/platform-k/latest`, run of 2026-08-10T00:01:44Z, target "Azure Demo"):

```
✗ Findings to fix
  Schemathesis (API contract)   FAIL   — "No Schemathesis results parsed this run."
  End-to-end (e2e-v2)           PASS   — 210 pass · 0 fail · 10 skip · 2 flaky
```

So the one suite that produced results **passed cleanly**, and the red comes from the other leg producing nothing.

`platform-s` has **0 runs**, which is consistent and expected — [KS-139](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-139) (upload the S suite) is still open.

## A verdict bug in the generator, read rather than guessed

`secuura-extranet/ci/build-dashboard.mjs`:

```js
// :39
const schemathesis = (args.schemathesis || 'unknown').toLowerCase(); // success|failure|skipped|unknown

// :181
const schemathesisClean = smt.state === 'ok' ? realFail === 0 : schemathesis === 'success';
const overallPassed = schemathesisClean && e2e.ok;

// :190  — the BADGE, which handles 'skipped' correctly
pill(schemathesis === 'success', schemathesis === 'success' ? 'PASS'
     : schemathesis === 'skipped' ? 'SKIPPED' : 'FAIL');
```

**The badge and the verdict disagree about what** `skipped` **means.** Line 190 renders a skipped Schemathesis leg as `SKIPPED`; line 181 scores anything that is not exactly `'success'` as not-clean. The workflow passes `--schemathesis "${{ steps.schemathesis.outcome }}"`, and a skipped GitHub step reports `outcome: 'skipped'` — so **an e2e-only run is structurally incapable of reporting** `passed`, while its own dashboard says the missing leg was merely skipped.

Whether that is what happened on any given run I have **not** established — per-run dashboards return 404, so `latest` is the only one readable, and its badge says `FAIL` rather than `SKIPPED`, meaning that particular run's Schemathesis leg ran and failed rather than being skipped. **The verdict bug is real in the code either way**; it is not necessarily the cause of all 22 reds.

## Next action

1. **Fix the verdict/badge disagreement** — `skipped` should not fail a run, since the badge already says it does not. Small change, `build-dashboard.mjs:181`. *(Not done in this session: the extranet auto-deploys on push to* `main`*, and this session is under the deploy hold.)*
2. **Find out why Schemathesis produces no NDJSON** on the demo target — the artifact path is `systemTest/schemathesis/output/schemathesis-reports/schemathesis-output.ndjson`. This is the substantive half.
3. **Then** get one green run on the board, so a future red means something.

## The pattern

Fourth instance today of the same defect — **signals firing into channels nobody reads** — and the only one aimed at humans rather than CI:

* [KS-637](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-637) — nightly Internal Audit, 40 consecutive failures.
* [KS-636](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-636) — base-image watchdog flagged a CRITICAL, unread 13 days.
* [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) — a baseline exception expiring 2026-08-31 whose owner is archived.
* [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) — no gate runs the service unit suites.

This one is different in kind and worse in effect: the others are unread, **this one is read and disbelieved.**

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep, running the extranet skill's test-runner review that boot skipped.*

title: node:24-alpine carries a CRITICAL (CVE-2026-59873) — our own base-image watchdog flagged it on 2026-08-01 and the failure went unread
description:
## BLUF

**The base-image CVE watchdog fired on 2026-08-01 and nobody heard it.** Its scheduled run failed — which is, by the workflow's own design, the alarm — reporting `node:24-alpine`**: 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — CVE-2026-59873**. That is the base image for **all ten backend services**.

Thirteen days unread at the time of filing. The watch is monthly, so without intervention the next signal is **2026-09-01**.

## Evidence

`.github/workflows/base-image-refresh.yml`, run `30685775724`, `event=schedule`, `created 2026-08-01T05:24:40Z`, `conclusion=failure`. Failing step: **"Evaluate watch conditions"**. Job log:

```
=== Trivy scan (CRITICAL/HIGH) of fresh local bases ===
  node:24-alpine                            : 1 CRITICAL / 4 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2026-59873
  nginx:1.30-alpine                         : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  nginxinc/nginx-unprivileged:1.30-alpine   : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  edoburu/pgbouncer:v1.25.2-p0              : 0 CRITICAL / 2 HIGH
  redis:8-alpine                            : 0 CRITICAL / 0 HIGH
  postgres:15-alpine                        : 1 CRITICAL / 14 HIGH — criticals: CVE-2025-68121
```

The postgres critical is the known [KS-365](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-365) residual (local-dev surface only, upstream's to fix) and is **not** why the run failed. The run failed on **Case 2** of its own contract:

> The run FAILS in exactly two cases, both worth a human: … 2. any OTHER base reports a CRITICAL → a pinned base has re-accumulated a critical CVE; treat like KS-363 (refresh/bump + redeploy).

`node:24-alpine` is that other base. The workflow did exactly what it was built to do.

**Every pinned base also reported** `MOVED` — all six tags were republished upstream since the last pull, so the images we build on are behind their own tags regardless of the CVE.

## Scope

`node:24-alpine` is the `FROM` for **10 service Dockerfiles** (`nginx:1.30-alpine` for the other 2). So this is not one service — it is the whole backend, local and demo alike.

## What I have NOT established

* **Whether CVE-2026-59873 is exploitable in our usage.** I did not look it up: the project rule forbids fetching external URLs/changelogs unless asked. Someone should read the advisory before sizing this.
* **Whether it is still present today.** The scan is from 2026-08-01 and the tag has moved since. It may already be fixed upstream — a re-run answers it in minutes.

**Neither gap is a reason to leave it.** A critical on the base image of every service, flagged by our own watchdog and unread for a fortnight, is worth a human either way.

## Next action

1. **Re-run the watch now** (`workflow_dispatch` on `base-image-refresh.yml`) to get a current reading rather than a fortnight-old one.
2. Read CVE-2026-59873 and decide: rebuild on the moved tag, bump the base, or accept with a written reason.
3. If a rebuild is needed it lands behind the Kintsugi hold like everything else — it is a rebuild of every service image.

## The process defect, which is the more important half

**A failed scheduled run is this watch's ONLY notification channel**, and it is one nobody checks. The workflow header says so plainly: *"Scheduled-run failures notify via GitHub, which is the reminder."* That reminder went nowhere for 13 days.

Same shape as [KS-635](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-635) (an audit-baseline expiry whose owning ticket was archived) and [KS-634](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-634) (no gate runs the service unit suites): **we have signals that fire correctly into channels nobody reads.** Worth deciding once, for all three, where an unattended failure should actually land.

*Found during the 2026-08-14 backlog sweep while verifying KS-365.*

title: GET /api/anchors/{id} and verify report different statuses for the same anchor — 91 UAT anchors read "failed" while verify says confirmed
description:
Raised from the S side 2026-08-12 (S ticket: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>)). @kamil.kreiser — one authenticated call settles this; details below.

## The observation

Platform S polls `GET /api/anchors/{id}` to learn when an anchor confirms. On UAT, **91 transactions are stuck reporting** `failed` — while `POST /api/verification/verify`, asked about the same document's content hash, reports the **same anchor id** as confirmed on chain.

Concretely, anchor `anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2`:

```
POST /api/verification/verify  {"providedHash":"6ffa6a0d4378007a480af701b6113cc0252544bcfde93cf11c2654c8bbe2367e"}

  verified   : true              status  : anchored
  anchorId   : anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
  bc.status  : confirmed         txHash  : e64759a924ea314e…
  anchoredAt : 2026-08-09T06:18:39.090Z
  checks     : documentExists ✓ hashValid ✓ isCertified ✓ isAnchored ✓ integrityVerified ✓
```

S recorded its failure for that same anchor at **06:32:20** — **fourteen minutes after** `anchoredAt`. So this is not a race between a poll and a late confirmation.

A second sample behaves identically: document ref `doc-1785566174843-631e2310` (an originate/upload), `verified: true`, `confirmed`, txHash `38adf13132f6856a…`, while S has it marked failed.

## What has been ruled out on the S side

Both plausible S-side causes were eliminated before raising this:

* **Not a failed/unauthenticated read.** All six affected organisations are registered with connector keys, and each has rows that *did* confirm — org 6: 77 confirmed vs 58 failed, org 9: 39 vs 20, org 13: 8 vs 6. Reads plainly work for these tenants.
* **Not an S mapping bug.** For an `anchor_…` reference S takes the `status` field from `/api/anchors/{id}` **verbatim** — no interpretation layer is involved. S is reporting the exact word it is given.

Spread is across every verb (share 39, upload 16, share-attach-consent 13, certify 5, sign 5, watermark 4, and the share-edit verbs), so it is not verb-specific.

## The question

Does `GET /api/anchors/{id}` return a stale or different status than the anchor's true state?

Candidates worth checking:

1. The anchors read serves a row that `reconcileDocumentAnchorState` ([KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure)) later healed, without the anchors view reflecting the heal.
2. There are two anchor records and the endpoints resolve different ones — the [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so)/584 "answer from the row that evidences its claims" family, except here it is the *anchors* endpoint that looks wrong.
3. `/api/anchors/{id}` is correct and verify is optimistic — in which case S's reading is right and the bug is elsewhere.

**The one call that settles it:**

```
GET /api/anchors/anchor_0f9a2acf-756d-46ee-b257-762a245d6ca2
```

on demo-pk, authenticated. If it returns `status: failed` while verify reports that anchor confirmed with tx `e64759a924ea314e…`, the inconsistency is confirmed and the question becomes which is authoritative. I could not make this call myself — the endpoint requires auth — so the diagnosis above is inferred from S's behaviour plus the eliminations, not directly observed.

## Why it matters to S

1. Users see **"anchor failed" on documents that are anchored and confirmed on chain** — a false negative on a trust surface.
2. **S never collects the real transaction hash.** Those rows keep their `anchor_…` placeholder permanently, so the chain evidence K is holding is silently lost to S.
3. It makes S's anchoring-failure count unusable as an alert signal.

## What S has done meanwhile

S no longer takes a bare `failed` as final ([Secuura/platform-s#440](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ps-577-dont-take-anchor-failed-as-final-when-ks-own-verify-disagrees-4a8640ddf0ac), merged). When the anchors endpoint reports failed, S asks verify and prefers the evidenced answer **only** when verify names the same `anchorId`, reports it anchored, not simulated, and carries a real 64-hex transaction hash.

That is a mitigation, not a fix — it recovers the lost hashes and stops the false failures, but the two endpoints still disagree, and S is now quietly compensating for it. Worth resolving at source.

Related: [PS-577](<https://linear.app/secuura/issue/PS-577>), [KS-535](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-535/a-failed-on-chain-anchor-still-reports-statusanchored-async-failure), [KS-563](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-563/verify-api-iscertified-is-true-for-merely-anchored-documents-so).

title: BM-2: Verification is a configurable workflow via smart contracts — record the workflow path, not casual views
description:
## BLUF

**Verification is a CONFIGURABLE WORKFLOW, not a fixed function.** Clients configure verification workflows via smart contracts; Secuura does NOT prescribe compliance. The workflow PATH is verified against the smart contract and recorded; simple interactions like document VIEWING are NOT recorded on-chain (noise). A third-party verifier (e.g. recruiter verifying a university document) sees the inspectable steps (identity checks, domain matching). End-user sees a binary "verified"; audit/legal sees full rigor.

## Carried ruling (PS-556, Kam 2026-08-11)

A verification is a **public, repeatable READ** — it sits OUTSIDE canonical lineage (lineage = versions from certifications/modifications). If a verification act is recorded at all, **S records it for S's own reporting/lineage annotation — K does NOT become a source of record for verification acts.**

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam).

title: BM-1: Certification model — certification = attestation + signing + optional watermarking; any modification → new version → mandatory re-certification
description:
## BLUF

**Certification is an UMBRELLA term** = attestation + signing + (optional) watermarking. Attestation = a user attesting a document is correct — on-chain, distinct from the file itself. Watermarking is a distinct, optional element. **ANY modification (including watermarking) creates a NEW document version, tracked via document lineage, and requires mandatory RE-CERTIFICATION.**

## Scope note

Likely an epic: data model + lineage enforcement + re-certification triggers + API/spec surface. This is the parent ticket — split into sub-tickets when the build starts.

Source: 2026-08-11 technical weekly (Stuart, Phil, Kam) — load-bearing project clarification.

title: Architecture P1: defuse the MULTI_TENANCY registry upsert — it silently collapses registrations per (hash, tenant) if the flag is ever enabled
description:
**Ask:** In the same phase that touches registration (plan-sheet requirement — not later, not beside), defuse `platform_document_registry`'s armed landmine: UNIQUE `uq_pdr_hash_tenant (content_hash, tenant_id)` + `ON CONFLICT (content_hash, tenant_id) DO UPDATE` in `registerInPlatformRegistry`. Either re-key the registry on the document UUID, or explicitly remove/disable the upsert.

**Why it matters:** the code path is dormant ONLY because `MULTI_TENANCY_ENABLED !== 'true'` on local and demo (0 registry rows in both DBs). If that flag is ever switched on with today's code, the upsert wakes and silently collapses registration pointers — newest write wins per (hash, tenant) — which directly violates ruling (b): duplicate bytes = two registrations, distinguished by UUID. A landmine that has been found and left armed is worse than one nobody found.

**Spec:** `1_Project_Definition/architecture/2026-08-07_K-side-plan-sheet.md` ("The MULTI_TENANCY landmine — inside P1, not beside it").

title: Bulk re-key: one admin-authorised rotate across a named set of externalRefs
description:
## BLUF

@peter asked for **one** admin-authorised action that re-keys a named set of Organisations by `externalRef`, instead of N separate `register-connector` calls during an incident. The loop itself is **1–2 days**.

**It must not ship before** [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) **(revoke-on-rotate).** Built on today's additive rotate, a bulk re-key would hand out N new credentials, leave N compromised ones live, and *look* like recovery.

## Detail

Today's single-org path is `POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector` with `rotate: true` — `services/api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:476-729`:

* platform-admin only; guardrail 1 refuses a connector-authorised rotate with 403 (`:499-509`)
* resolves the org by `metadata->>'externalRef'` under platform scope (`:590-593`)
* mints a fresh `sk_` key via the security service (`:674-686` → `services/security/src/index.ts:800`)
* plaintext key returned exactly once (`:719-720`)

`runWithPlatformScope` (`packages/shared/src/db/tenant-guc.ts:102`) already handles the cross-tenant access, so multi-tenancy is **not** the hard part here.

**Scope**

* Extract `platform.ts:476-729` into a reusable per-org function; add a bulk route taking a list of `externalRef`s.
* Return a **per-ref result array** — partial success must be explicit. An incident operator has to know which refs failed and why.
* OpenAPI entry + `generate-openapi` regen + api-gateway rebuild (the gateway bakes the spec) + KS-380 preflight.

**Explicitly out of scope:** delivery of the key material for N keys. One response body carrying N live secrets is not the answer; that needs its own design and a security review (see the KS-480 sizing table).

**Cheaper alternative on the record** (raised because @peter asked not to have the manual path assumed away): a scripted loop over the existing admin endpoint gives one *operator action* today at near-zero build cost. It does not give one *authorisation*, which is the part actually being asked for.

**Done when:** an admin can re-key a named set of refs in one authorised call, each prior key is revoked per the [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) semantics, per-ref outcomes are explicit, and the [KS-583](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-583) rehearsal passes all four steps.

---

*Split from* [KS-480](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-480) *per @kamil.kreiser's ruling 2026-08-07.* [KS-579](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-579)*–*[KS-582](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-582) *are @peter's own candidates carried over unchanged;* [KS-577](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-577) *and* [KS-578](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-578) *are additions from the 2026-08-06 verification. Findings checked against* `develop` `c8ce65dca`*; Finding B confirmed live on the demo VM read-only.*

title: Sweeps 2026-08-05: untracked failures across 10 ops — response-schema recurrence (KS-498 residual), 3 genuine 500s, non-envelope 5xx on by-design-503 ops, undocumented status
description:
Findings from two runs on the same code, 2026-08-05: `full-2026-08-05T08-44-00Z` and `pre-merge-2026-08-05T09-18-45Z` (Schemathesis 4.24.3, 316/318 operations, 316/317 past auth, no health-check suppression, untruncated messages). Everything else in those runs maps to [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) / [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) / [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code). The operations below map to **no ticket**.

> **Read the counts as a FLOOR, not a total.** The two runs agreed on the failing *classes* but not the failing *operations* — five ops failed in pre-merge that were absent from the full sweep. Property-based generation samples; it does not enumerate. Verify a specific operation with a targeted probe, never by its absence from one run.

## 1. response_schema_conformance recurs on 4 NEW ops ([KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) residual)

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) is **Done** — closed 2026-07-29 having verified the class down to 2 ops, both [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) family. **None of these four are those two**, so this is a recurrence on different operations, not unfinished work. Filed fresh per the [KS-430](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-430/write-path-request-schema-contract-drift-across-60-operations-unmasked)→[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks)→[KS-497](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-497/write-path-raw-500-internal-error-recurs-on-4-platformtenants-ops-ks) precedent.

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/m365/connections/complete` | 14 | yes |
| `POST /api/presentations/verify` | 13 | yes |
| `POST /api/wallets/verify` | 4 | yes |
| `PATCH /api/security/events/{id}/resolve` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/oauth/apps/{id}/rotate-secret` — **added 2026-09-10** from `pr-ks-971-2026-09-10T16-31-45Z-slot1` (Schemathesis 4.25.x, `pr` profile, slot 1, develop at `688f4dded` + the [KS-971 (2/2): slot-isolate the k6 performance harness, and prove it by fault injection](https://linear.app/secuura/review/ks-971-22-slot-isolate-the-k6-performance-harness-and-prove-it-by-34bc0f07c5ba) systemTest branch). Runtime answers `200 {"success":true,"clientSecret":"scs_…","warning":"Store the new client_secret securely — it cannot be retrieved later."}`; the declared 200 schema requires `id`. Handler `services/auth/src/routes/oauth.ts:1079`; the route reached develop between the 2026-08-05 sweeps and 2026-08-28 ([KS-431](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-431/16-write-operations-return-raw-500-internal-error-unmasked-by-the-ks) oauth-apps work), which is why it is absent above. The 2026-08-19 baseline already lists its `positive_data_acceptance` pair ([KS-591](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-591/positive-data-acceptance-recurs-at-scale-734-failures-across-64-ops-ks)) but NOT `response_schema_conformance`, so this pair fails the gate until fixed or baselined. | — | pr: yes |
| `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/session/{sessionId}` — **added 2026-10-22** ([KS-1511](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-1511/audit-log-limit-follow-up-retire-the-stale-accepted-baseline-entry) control sweep `pre-merge-2026-10-22T11-15-40Z-slot1`, platform-k slot 1 on Peter's Mac, develop `f75b52721`, `pre-merge --seed 1511`). ST108 ×1: `"sessionId" is a required property` against the declared 200 schema (requires `sessionId`, `status`, `createdAt`). Same message as the sibling `GET /api/kyc/microsoft/result/{sessionId}`, already baselined under this ticket; whether both share one handler defect in `services/kyc/src/routes/microsoft-verification.ts` is not established. Not baselined, so it fails the triaged-baseline gate whenever drawn; seen intermittently before (before-only pair in a version-bump comparison, `systemTest/schemathesis/docs/known-issues-and-baseline.md` \~line 1099). | — | pre-merge: yes |

Three of the four **also** fail `negative_data_rejection` — likely one root cause ("nothing validated, so nothing shaped correctly"), not four independent drifts. Worth confirming before treating them as separate work. Fix per [KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444): runtime is truth, reconcile the declared response schema, regenerate with `npm run generate-openapi`, rebuild api-gateway on both targets (it bundles the spec).

## 2. Three genuine 500s on schema-compliant input

| Operation | Site | Mechanism |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/users/admin/create` | `services/auth/src/routes/auth.ts:177` | `data.email.toLowerCase()` with no type guard — a non-string `email` (e.g. `{}`) raises `TypeError` → 500 instead of a typed 4xx |
| `GET /api/users/admin/list` | `services/auth/src/routes/users.ts:344` **and** `:398` | `parseInt(req.query.offset as string) || 0` — `-1` is truthy so it passes through; Postgres rejects it (`OFFSET must not be negative`) → 500. The `|| 0` fallback only catches `NaN` |
| `POST /api/documents/{id}/transfer-custody` | not yet traced | 500 in the pre-merge run; absent from the full sweep |

**The negative-offset pattern is SIX sites across four services**, not the two the sweep reached:

* `auth/src/routes/users.ts:344`, `:398`
* `originate/src/routes/adminConfig.ts:1006`, `:1166` — raw `LIMIT ${limit} OFFSET ${offset}`, x4 queries
* `tenant-provisioning/src/index.ts:556`
* `api-gateway/src/routes/platform.ts:374` — `Math.min` caps the upper bound only, no negative guard

**Not an injection risk** — the raw-SQL cases use Prisma `$queryRaw` tagged templates (parameterised) and `parseInt(...) || 0` always yields a number. The defect is the unvalidated negative reaching Postgres as a 500. A fix touching only `users.ts:344` leaves five siblings exposed. Suggested fix: `.int().min(0)` on `offset` at handler entry.

```bash
TOKEN=$(curl -s -X POST http://localhost:6882/api/auth/login -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":"admin@secuura.com","password":"admin123"}' | jq -r '.data.accessToken')

curl -i -X GET -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" 'http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/list?offset=-1'
curl -i -X POST -H "Authorization: Bearer $TOKEN" -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -d '{"email":{},"password":"Str0ng-Passw0rd!","role":"OWNER"}' http://localhost:6882/api/users/admin/create
```

## 3. `integration_5xx_guard` fires on by-design-503 ops — non-envelope 5xx

| Operation | full | pre-merge |
| -- | -- | -- |
| `POST /api/timestamps` | 4 | yes |
| `POST /api/credentials` | 1 | yes |

Both are on `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS` in `systemTest/schemathesis/config/checks.py` (blanket `not_a_server_error` disabled because they 503 by design when their provider is unconfigured). The [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing)/[KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) guard replaces it and **passes** a clean declared-503 envelope — so a failure here means a 5xx that is **not** a proper 503 envelope, i.e. a genuine server error the exception list is demonstrably not hiding. Worth confirming whether it is a raw 500 or a malformed 503 body.

## 4. Undocumented status — `POST /api/referrals/apply` (6)

`status_code_conformance` fails: the operation returns a status not in its declared response set. Distinct from [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (`GET /api/documents/{id}/sig-json`, still open) — same class, different operation. Fix per [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code): either stop returning the undeclared status, or declare it — whichever reflects intended behaviour, per the "spec is the contract" rule.

## Not included here

* `POST /api/presentations` failing `not_a_server_error` — **already fixed** under [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) by adding it to `_UNCONFIGURED_503_OPS`; live-verified it 503s by design (`VC_SIGNING_KEY is required to sign a presentation. Refusing to emit an HMAC-signed presentation falsely labelled Ed25519`) when `holderDID` is present.
* New `negative_data_rejection` ops (`POST /api/platform/organizations/register-connector`, `POST /api/users/admin/create`) and the still-failing status-list trio — registered on [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data), whose register is live and In Progress.

## Please run the full sweep before closing

The fast PR gate covers none of these classes — it does not validate response bodies, does not generate negative bodies, and does not fuzz these write paths:

```bash
cd systemTest/schemathesis
python3 scripts/run.py full        # local stack on :6882
```

Full artefacts under `systemTest/schemathesis/output/reports/` for both run directories — NDJSON event stream (authoritative for check totals), VCR cassette, HAR, per-call metrics, replayable crash files.

## Related

[KS-498](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-498/response-schema-conformance-drift-recurs-on-5-ops-ks-430ks-444) / [KS-515](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-515/write-path-requestresponse-schema-drift-27-ops-ks-430-recurrence-new) (response schema) · [KS-518](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-518/schema-violating-input-accepted-on-10-operations-negative-data) (negative data) · [KS-508](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-508/get-apidocumentsidsigjson-returns-undocumented-400-status-code) (undocumented status) · [KS-268](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-268/localdev-coverage-for-503-by-design-integration-endpoints-billing) / [KS-499](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-499/unconfigured-provider-503s-on-7-write-ops-beyond-ks-268s-3-exclusions) (the 5xx guard) · [KS-188](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-188/stateful-testing-declare-openapi-links-operationid-so-postgetdelete) (stateful links — the majority class; 0 declared transitions with 104 producers available explains \~78% of the full sweep's failures) · [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) (the sweep that found these).

*Found by the* [KS-544](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-544/schemathesis-4242-4243-adopt-full-cli-parameter-surface-always) *sweeps, 2026-08-05. systemTest rule: refs as KS-NNN text, repro via local stack.*

## Summary

`systemTest/playwright/` covers **8 of 310** published API operations (2.6 %) and issues **no writes at all** — so no complete business flow exists anywhere in the suite. This ticket takes Playwright to full coverage of the published contract, driven by the documented product flows, reusing the personas the platform already seeds.

## Current state (measured 2026-07-24 — see R1–R3 for today)

|  |  |
| -- | -- |
| Published contract | `Blockchain/Dev/docs/openapi/secuura-api.yaml` — 278 paths / **310 operations** / 42 tags |
| Playwright today | 3 clients, 3 spec files, 11 tests, **8 operations** |
| Writes today | **zero** — read-only plus two unauthenticated 401/403 checks |
| Zero-coverage domains | Billing 21, M365 22, Governance 18, NFT 18, KYC 16, GDPR 15, Analytics 12, Staking 12, VC/VP/StatusList/DID 24, Webhooks 7, Tenants 6, Timestamps 6, API Keys 4, Sessions 2 |

Covered today: `POST /auth/login`, `POST /auth/refresh`, `GET /users/me`, `GET /documents`, `GET /documents/{id}`, `POST /verification/verify`, plus unauth-only checks on `POST /documents/{id}/verify` and `POST /notifications`.

> **Design verified against the Playwright docs for the pinned** `@playwright/test` **1.61.1** (2026-07-24). *Pin is now 1.64.1 — re-check per R6.* Every design decision cites its source in **Playwright references** at the end.

## Implementation principle — use Playwright's own primitives

**Never implement something ourselves if Playwright already provides it.** Anything the framework ships — polling, stepping, retries, parallelism, artifact attachment, context isolation — is used as-is. Our code exists only to express *Secuura's* domain (personas, flows, coverage classes) or to fill a capability the framework genuinely does not have. A hand-rolled equivalent of a framework feature is a review rejection.

| Need | Mechanism | Ours or Playwright's? |
| -- | -- | -- |
| Wait for an async outcome | `expect.poll` (`{ timeout, intervals, message }`) | **Playwright's.** `helpers/settle.ts` is a thin wrapper supplying the project deadlines **\[ref 8\]** |
| Ordered, named stages in a flow | `test.step()` | **Playwright's** |
| Per-persona session isolation | `playwright.request.newContext()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 2\]** |
| Persist an artifact + surface it in the report | `testInfo.outputPath()` + `testInfo.attach({ path })` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 6\]** |
| Parallelism, retries, sharding, reporters, tagging | runner config | **Playwright's** |
| Setup/teardown lifecycle | fixtures with `use()` | **Playwright's** **\[ref 7\]** |
| **Capturing API exchanges as a durable artefact** | `helpers/exchangeRecorder.ts` | **Ours — the framework has no equivalent** (upstream request closed unimplemented, **\[ref 5\]**). Built *on* `testInfo.attach`/`outputPath` |
| CSRF double-submit echo | `helpers/csrf.ts` | **Ours** — application-protocol concern |
| Coverage classification vs the OpenAPI spec | `coverage/*` | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |
| Persona catalogue, flow definitions | `config/`, `helpers/flow.ts`, specs | **Ours** — Secuura-domain concern |

## Stack isolation — Playwright runs on its own Docker instance

* ~~**CI**~~ *(moot — GitHub Actions retired 2026-08-27, see R4/R5)* — the `playwright` job in `.github/workflows/pr-platform-suites.yml` boots via `boot-platform-stack` with `stack_prefix: pr-playwright`, gateway **6982**, postgres 6532, redis 6479, pgbouncer 6533; pointed at by `API_BASE_URL: http://localhost:6982/api`. Distinct `COMPOSE_PROJECT_NAME` / `STACK_PREFIX` → separate containers, volumes, networks. Siblings sit on 6882 / 7082 / 7182.
* **Local** — the suite does not start or stop a server (`playwright.config.ts`); it attaches to whatever `API_BASE_URL` points at. Use its own instance for destructive flows (F14 erasure, F5 revoke).

Any environment posture we choose applies to Playwright alone. The only shared thing is the composite action's *source file*.

## Scope boundary

Playwright asserts **business outcomes of documented flows**. It does not re-test what the sibling suites own — see `Projects Documents/API_Security_Functional_Testing_Architecture_Flow_Diagrams.html` §2–3 and the Coverage & Scenario Matrix in `QA_Tool_Cheat_Sheet_Secuura_API_Testing.html`.

| Excluded from Playwright | Owner |
| -- | -- |
| Boundary values, negative **data**, fuzzing | Schemathesis |
| Status/header compliance, undeclared verbs, redirects, rate-limit headers, 429 | Schemathesis |
| RBAC matrices, cross-tenant, IDOR/BOLA | Schemathesis (+ Akto) |
| Unauthenticated 401/403 sweeps | Schemathesis + the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight |
| OWASP API Top 10, injection, SSRF, BFLA | Akto |
| Throughput, latency, saturation | Performance (k6) |
| Real Cardano chain integrity / anchor-vs-chain | anchoring Integration suite ([KS-489](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-489/review-d-blockchain-anchoring-smart-contract-integrity)-D) — see Risk 3 |

**A distinction that matters, because it looks like the excluded category but is not:** a *documented business outcome that is not success* — a verification returning **Expired**, a tampered document returning **Failed**, a certifier **Rejecting** a request — is in scope. Those are product states the stakeholder guides describe, reached with valid inputs. What is excluded is malformed **data** (missing fields, oversize values, type confusion). F6 and F7 exist precisely to cover the former.

Consistent with Playwright's Best Practices — *"Only test what you control."* — which is why provider-gated paths (Stripe, M365) record a by-design 503 rather than reaching for the third party. **\[ref 1\]**

**Two existing specs are duplicates and are retired in Phase 0**: `notifications.spec.ts` (both tests assert unauth → 401/403, already swept for every bearer op by the [KS-380](https://linear.app/secuura/issue/KS-380/harden-the-pre-release-gate-required-checks-on-develop-preflight) preflight) and the invalid-credentials / missing-email cases in `login.spec.ts` (negative data, owned by Schemathesis `test_authentication.py`).

## Persona policy

**Use the existing** `default`**-tenant personas first.** The seeder (`services/auth/src/repositories/userRepo.ts` → `demoAccounts`) provides 17 accounts across 7 tenants. A new persona is created **only where an existing one provably cannot serve**. Permissions on seeded accounts are **not** changed. Non-default tenants are not used.

### Existing personas — the working set (`default` tenant)

| Email | Role | Verification | Password env (fallback) |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `issuer@secuura.com` | ISSUER_ADMIN | ENHANCED | `DEMO_ISSUER_PASSWORD` (`issuer123`) |
| `admin@secuura.com` | SYSTEM_ADMIN | HIGH | `ADMIN_USER_PASSWORD` (`admin123`) |
| `demo@secuura.io` | OWNER | ENHANCED | `DEMO_USER_PASSWORD` (`demo123`) |
| `holder@secuura.com` | OWNER | BASIC | `DEMO_HOLDER_PASSWORD` (`holder123`) |
| `verifier@secuura.com` | VERIFIER | STANDARD | `DEMO_VERIFIER_PASSWORD` (`verifier123`) |

Seeding is gated on `ALLOW_DEFAULT_SEED_PASSWORDS=true`; the `config/environment.ts` getters must read the **same env names** with these fallbacks. `kam@secuura.ai` is a real person's account — **do not use**.

### Additions — three, each with a blocking justification

Created at runtime by F2 via `POST /api/users/admin/create` as `admin@secuura.com`. Confirmed viable: the handler assigns `role` from the body, and admin-created users are `emailVerified: true` / `status: ACTIVE`.

| Proposed name | Role / level | Flow | Why no existing persona works |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| `pw-approver-<run>@secuura-test.invalid` | ISSUER_APPROVER / ENHANCED | F3, F7 | **Role gap.** `ISSUER_APPROVER` is in the `UserRole` union (`services/auth/src/types/index.ts:8`) but no seeded account holds it |
| `pw-gdpr-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / BASIC | F14 | **Erasure is irreversible.** Running it on `holder@secuura.com` destroys a persona F9 and F20 depend on |
| `pw-kyc-subject-<run>@…` | OWNER / **NONE** | F15 | **KYC state is one-way.** A reused persona is already-verified on re-run, breaking determinism |

Plus one **non-user identity**: the platform API key (`SECUURA_PLATFORM_API_KEY`, already used by Akto) for **F8**'s machine path. Not an account; no new seed data.

### Deliberately not added

| Considered | Why not |
| -- | -- |
| Default-tenant ORG_ADMIN | `admin@secuura.com` performs the org/tenant operations; ORG_ADMIN-vs-SYSTEM_ADMIN is RBAC → Schemathesis |
| Second rights holder for F9 | Two OWNERs already exist in `default`: `demo@secuura.io` → `holder@secuura.com` |
| Two governance participants for F20 | The same two OWNERs serve; re-registration conflict handled as a valid state |
| Dedicated billing customer | Billing customer creation is 503-by-design locally; `demo@secuura.io` suffices |
| Any non-default-tenant account | Cross-tenant behaviour belongs to Schemathesis |

## ⚠ Two platform capabilities we do not have — needed by F6 and F13

Two flows assert a documented product state that **cannot currently be reached on demand**. Neither blocks Phase 0, but both block their own flow's plan from being finalised. Raised with @kamil.kreiser and @stuart.jamieson in the comments — **and probed ourselves first** (see Risk mitigation), because the capability may already exist.

| Need | Flow | Why it is needed | What "available" looks like |
| -- | -- | -- | -- |
| **Induce an expired certification** | **F6** | The Verifier guide documents **Expired** as one of five verification result states. Verifying it requires a certification that is *already* past its expiry. If expiry is purely wall-clock with no way to set a past date, F6's expired leg is unreachable and the state stays permanently untested | Either an issuance parameter accepting a past `expiresAt` (non-prod only), or a supported way to age an existing certification. A test must be able to produce one deterministically, in-run, without clock manipulation on the host |
| **Raise a system error on demand** | **F13** | F13's only real journey is *error → resolve*. Asserting it requires a system error to exist first. Provoking one by genuinely breaking a service is not acceptable in a shared or CI stack | A non-prod-only way to emit a synthetic entry into the system-errors surface with a known signature, so the test can find it, resolve it, and assert it reflects as resolved |

**If either already exists**, this is a documentation gap rather than a build ask. **If neither is feasible**, the affected leg is recorded as a documented coverage gap rather than quietly dropped: F6 keeps its tampered + not-found legs, F13 falls back to `positive-path` for the whole read surface.

## Flow catalogue

**Restructured 2026-07-24** and now supersedes the earlier 14-entry list. Three problems were fixed: two entries were *buckets* rather than flows (the old F13 carried 66 operations under a single criterion about one proposal; the old F9 carried 37 across seven unrelated domains), sizing was so uneven that "phase" was a meaningless unit of work, and three documented outcomes plus the entire partner/machine path had no home. Each entry below is now **one actor goal, one acceptance criterion, 4–25 operations**, sized so a child plan can be written per flow.

Flows are transcribed from the product docs — the five `Projects Documents/Stakeholder-Guide-*.md`, `Blockchain/Dev/docs/E2E-TESTING-PLAN.md`, `USER_TESTING/02-Happy-Path-Testing.md`, `VERIFICATION.md`, `SCOPES.md`, `METERING-USAGE-API.md`, `TOKENISATION.md`, `CONNECTORS_PATTERN.md`. Take the flow **semantics**, not the UI steps.

**Data strategy** — every flow declares one: **Own** (creates and tears down everything it needs) · **Spine** (part of the shared-document chain) · **Setup** (creates a disposable persona or prerequisite first).
